vocabulary.definition: Software or applications designed to assist programmers in creating, debugging, and maintaining software applications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, developer tools are crucial for enhancing productivity and streamlining the software development process.

insight.nuance: The phrase 'developer tool' often connotes a specialized utility that caters to the needs of software engineers, rather than general users.

speaker: Ivan Zhao
text: We called it sugar-coated broccoli. People don't want to eat the broccoli but people like sugar, so it gave them the sugar then hide your broccoli inside of it.
keySentence: Sugar-coated broccoli hides the broccoli inside something people like.
text_ko: 우리는 그걸 '설탕 입힌 브로콜리(sugar-coated broccoli)'라고 불렀어요. 사람들은 브로콜리를 먹고 싶어 하지 않지만 달콤한 건 좋아하니까, 설탕으로 코팅해서 달콤함을 먼저 주고 그 안에 브로콜리를 숨겨 넣었어요.
text_zh: 我们叫它"糖衣西兰花"。大家都不爱吃西兰花，但都喜欢糖，所以就先给他们糖，然后把西兰花藏在里面。
text_es: Le decíamos brócoli con azúcar. A la gente no le gusta comerse el brócoli, pero el azúcar sí les gusta, entonces les das el azúcar y escondes el brócoli adentro.
fullContext: Ivan continues explaining Notion's strategy for making their developer-focused vision more accessible to regular users. After realizing people didn't care about creating software tools, they decided to package their powerful capabilities inside familiar productivity software that people already knew they needed. This metaphor captures how they made their complex, technical vision palatable by wrapping it in something people already wanted.

speaker: Ivan Zhao
text: What is the building a product or business. You want user. You want revenue. That's the product business. And building for something you want the world to have is building for your value. You have some taste. You have some aesthetic. There are different energy.
keySentence: building for something you want the world to have is building for your value.
text_ko: 제품이나 비즈니스를 만든다는 건 결국 사용자를 얻고 수익을 내고 싶다는 뜻이에요. 그게 바로 제품 비즈니스(product business)이에요. 반면에 세상이 갖길 바라는 무언가를 만드는 건 자신의 가치(value)를 위해 만드는 거예요. 취향(taste)이나 미학(aesthetic)이 있고, 완전히 다른 종류의 에너지(energy)가 흐르죠.
text_zh: 做一个产品(product)或一门生意(business)，到底是为了什么？你要用户(user)，要营收(revenue)。这就是做产品/做生意的出发点。但如果你是想把自己希望世界拥有的东西做出来，那就是在为你的价值(value)去创造——你有自己的品味，有自己的审美(aesthetic)，做出来的感觉和能量就不一样。
text_es: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre construir un producto y construir un negocio? Quieres usuarios. Quieres ingresos. Eso es un negocio de producto (product business). En cambio, construir algo que quieres que el mundo tenga es construir desde tus valores y tu visión. Tienes cierto gusto, una estética. Es otra energía.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ivan about key elements for finding something that works after years of struggle. Ivan explains the fundamental tension in building products - balancing what the market wants (users and revenue) versus what you personally believe the world needs (your values and vision). He describes this as managing different types of energy and warns against going too far in either direction.

vocabulary.definition: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty; a set of principles underlying the work of a particular artist or artistic movement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'aesthetic' often relates to the design and visual appeal of products, branding, and user interfaces, influencing customer perception and engagement.

insight.nuance: While 'aesthetic' primarily refers to visual aspects, it can also encompass the overall experience and emotional response elicited by a product or service.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity to do work or produce change; often associated with vitality and dynamism.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'energy' can refer to the enthusiasm and drive of a team, as well as the resources and momentum behind projects and initiatives.

insight.nuance: While 'energy' can denote physical or operational capacity, it often carries a connotation of passion and motivation in a team or organizational context.

speaker: Ivan Zhao
text: you realize you don't need a lot. But when you can do a lot at the same time or hire people who can do that, naturally keep the company small.
keySentence: naturally keep the company small.
text_ko: 많은 게 필요하진 않다는 걸 알게 돼요. 동시에 여러 일을 해낼 수 있거나 그런 사람들을 채용할 수 있다면 자연스럽게 회사 규모를 작게 유지하게 돼요.
text_zh: 你会发现其实不需要太多人。不过当你自己能同时做很多事，或者能找到那种能一肩挑多项工作的多面手，公司就会自然而然地保持小而精。
text_es: Te das cuenta de que no necesitas tanto. Pero si puedes abarcar muchas cosas a la vez —o contratar a personas que puedan hacerlo—, lo natural es mantener la empresa pequeña.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ivan why Notion has stayed remarkably lean and efficient compared to other companies of their scale - they're profitable, didn't hire a salesperson until 10M ARR, and kept their team very small. Ivan explains their approach centers on hiring versatile people who can handle multiple functions rather than specialists, and using better systems and tools (including Notion itself) to solve problems instead of throwing more people at them.

speaker: Ivan Zhao
text: We internally help other people and understand this. Internally we use the metaphor that Notion's a small bus. The bus, the smaller the bus, it's easier to turn corners, easier to accelerate, easier to maneuver.
keySentence: the smaller the bus, it's easier to turn corners, easier to accelerate, easier to maneuver.
text_ko: 우리는 내부적으로 서로 도와주면서 이 점을 잘 이해하고 있어요. 사내에선 노션을 '작은 버스'에 비유해요. 버스가 작을수록 코너 돌기도 쉽고, 가속하기도 쉽고, 기민하게 움직이기도 쉬워요.
text_zh: 在我们内部，大家会互相帮忙，也都认同这一点。我们常把 Notion（Notion）比作一辆小巴：车越小，转弯越灵活、起步越快、操控越容易。
text_es: Aquí dentro ayudamos a otros equipos y lo tenemos claro. Internamente decimos que Notion es como un microbús: cuanto más pequeño es, más fácil es girar, acelerar y maniobrar.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ivan for advice on how to actually stay lean when it's tempting to hire more engineers and designers. Ivan shares an internal metaphor they use at Notion to help employees understand why staying small is advantageous. He explains that like vehicles, smaller organizations can change direction and move faster, while larger ones become harder to steer and slower to respond to market changes.

vocabulary.definition: A figure of speech that involves an implicit comparison between two unlike things, suggesting that one thing is another to highlight similarities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, metaphors are often used to simplify complex concepts or to create relatable imagery that can enhance communication and understanding among team members.

insight.nuance: While metaphors can be powerful tools for persuasion and clarity, they should be used judiciously to avoid confusion or misinterpretation.

vocabulary.definition: To move or manipulate something skillfully or carefully, often in a strategic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, maneuvering can refer to navigating through challenges, adjusting strategies, or optimizing processes to achieve desired outcomes.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a level of skill and planning, and can sometimes carry a connotation of cunning or tactical thinking.

vocabulary.definition: To increase the speed or rate of something, often referring to processes or growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, accelerating growth or development is crucial for gaining market advantage and achieving scalability within a competitive landscape.

insight.nuance: While acceleration is generally positive, it can imply pressure or urgency that may lead to oversight if not managed carefully.

speaker: Ivan Zhao
text: I think just understand abstraction or system is a better curve than pecan curve, right? Linear. We internally help other people and understand this... I think the more interesting point here, it's like you can create progress through better abstractions.
keySentence: you can create progress through better abstractions.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 단순히 추상화(abstraction)나 시스템(system)을 이해하는 게 피칸 커브(pecan curve)보다 더 나은 곡선이라고 봐요 — 좀 더 선형(linear)에 가깝고요. 저희는 내부적으로 다른 사람들을 도와가며 이런 걸 이해하려고 하고요. 더 흥미로운 건, 더 나은 추상화(abstraction)를 통해 실제로 진전(progress)을 만들어낼 수 있다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得，理解抽象（abstraction）或系统（system）的收益曲线，比 pecan 曲线(pecan curve) 更好，对吧？它是线性的(Linear)。在我们内部，大家会互相帮助、把这些东西弄明白……更有意思的是，你可以通过更好的抽象来推动进步。
text_es: Creo que entender la abstracción (abstraction) o el sistema (system) es una curva de aprendizaje mejor que la "pecan curve" (pecan curve), ¿no? Es más lineal. Dentro del equipo nos ayudamos mutuamente a entender esto. Y creo que lo más interesante es que puedes generar progreso mediante mejores abstracciones (abstractions).
fullContext: Ivan is explaining why he advocates for not being afraid to reset and start over when building products. He argues that humans think linearly, but finding better abstractions or fundamental approaches can create exponential progress. This means that even if you throw away previous work to build on better foundations, you can recover that lost progress much faster than expected because the new approach compounds more effectively.

vocabulary.definition: The process of simplifying complex systems by focusing on the essential features while ignoring irrelevant details.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, abstraction is often used in software development to create models that help teams understand and manage complex systems more effectively.

insight.nuance: While abstraction can enhance clarity and efficiency, over-abstraction may lead to a loss of important details, making it crucial to find the right balance.

vocabulary.definition: Forward or onward movement towards a destination or goal; improvement or development in a particular area.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, progress is often measured through key performance indicators (KPIs) that track growth, efficiency, and innovation.

insight.nuance: While progress is generally viewed positively, it can sometimes imply a sense of urgency or pressure to achieve results quickly.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a straight line or a sequential progression; involving a direct relationship between cause and effect.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and product development, a linear approach often refers to a step-by-step process that follows a predetermined path, which can be effective for straightforward tasks.

insight.nuance: While linear processes can be efficient, they may not accommodate the complexities of more dynamic environments, where nonlinear approaches may be more appropriate.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: I had this belief that almost anybody can learn anything. People have different interests, not everybody wants to learn everything. But I find that if you're having trouble learning something, it's just because something's not clicking.
keySentence: If you're having trouble learning, something's not clicking in your mental model.
text_ko: 저는 거의 누구나 무엇이든 배울 수 있다고 믿었어요. 사람들마다 관심사가 달라서 모두가 모든 걸 배우고 싶어하는 건 아니에요. 그런데 경험상 뭔가를 배우는 데 어려움을 겪는다면 그건 그냥 어떤 부분이 딱 맞물리지 않아서인 경우가 많아요.
text_zh: 我一直觉得几乎任何人都能学会任何东西。只是大家兴趣不同，不是谁都想学所有东西。但我发现，要是你学不明白某样东西，通常只是哪里没对上——没抓到要领。
text_es: Creía que casi cualquiera puede aprender cualquier cosa. La gente tiene intereses distintos; no todo el mundo quiere aprender de todo. Pero me doy cuenta de que si te cuesta aprender algo, suele ser porque hay algo que no termina de encajar.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jackie about her motivation for writing her product management books. Jackie explains her philosophy on learning, which drove her to write accessible guides for PM interviews. She believes that when people struggle to learn something, it's usually because the information isn't being presented in a way that matches their mental framework, rather than an inability to understand the concept itself.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulty or problems that hinder progress or cause distress; a state of distress or difficulty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, trouble often refers to operational challenges or obstacles that impede efficiency, requiring problem-solving and strategic intervention.

insight.nuance: While 'trouble' can denote serious issues, it is also commonly used in a more casual sense to describe minor inconveniences or challenges.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: I very much saw the PM's role is a person who wants to say no to everybody.
keySentence: I very much saw the PM's role is a person who wants to say no to everybody.
text_ko: 저는 프로덕트 매니저(PM) 역할이 솔직히 모두에게 '아니요'라고 말하고 싶어 하는 사람처럼 보였어요.
text_zh: 我一直觉得，产品经理（PM）就是那个要对大家说“不”的人。
text_es: Para mí, el papel del responsable de producto (product manager) era el de alguien cuyo instinto es decir "no" a todo el mundo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jackie about mistakes she made early in her career at Asana. Jackie describes how she initially misunderstood the PM role as being a gatekeeper who needed to reject ideas to maintain focus. This defensive approach backfired when she shut down her boss's suggestion, leading to a pivotal learning moment about the importance of collaboration over control in product management.

vocabulary.definition: A role refers to the function or position that an individual or entity occupies within a specific context, often defining their responsibilities and expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In organizations, roles are clearly defined to ensure accountability and clarity in team dynamics, with each member contributing to the overall objectives.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a formal position or a more informal function within a group, and is often used in discussions about team structure and collaboration.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: For the next two weeks, say yes to everything. I think you can find a way to do your job and still say yes to people. You can say, 'yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes.
keySentence: For the next two weeks, say yes to everything.
text_ko: 앞으로 2주간은 일단 모든 요청에 '네'라고 해보세요. 일을 하면서도 사람들에게 '네'라고 할 방법을 찾을 수 있을 거예요. '네, 저도 동의해요. 그건 분명한 문제예요. 네.'라고 말하면 돼요.
text_zh: 接下来两周，凡事先说“好”。我觉得你能想办法把本职工作做好，同时又能答应别人。你可以这样说：“好，我同意，这确实是个问题。好。”
text_es: Durante las próximas dos semanas, di que sí a todo. Creo que puedes encontrar la manera de hacer tu trabajo y, aun así, decir que sí a la gente. Puedes decir: "Sí, estoy de acuerdo. Eso sí es un problema real. Sí."
fullContext: Jackie continues explaining how her coach helped her overcome her tendency to immediately reject ideas from colleagues. The coach challenged her to spend two weeks saying yes instead of no, which taught Jackie that she could maintain her PM responsibilities while being more collaborative. This experience showed her that being overly protective of the product roadmap was actually hindering effective teamwork.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: I worked with her for several months, but then once that was gone, then I did start to find that personally I would make things bigger when I had a coach, because I had something that I knew how to solve on my own.
keySentence: I would make things bigger when I had a coach, because I had something that I knew how to solve on my own.
text_ko: 몇 달 동안 그녀와 함께 일했어요. 그런데 그 관계가 끝나고 나서는 개인적으로 코치가 있을 때 사소한 일도 더 크게 만드는 경향이 있다는 걸 알게 됐어요. 스스로 해결할 수 있는 문제였음에도 코치가 있으니까 더 부풀렸던 거예요.
text_zh: 我跟她合作了几个月，后来她不在了，我才意识到：有教练在的时候我反而会把问题放大，把本来自己能解决的事当成大问题。
text_es: Trabajé con ella varios meses, pero luego, cuando eso se acabó, empecé a darme cuenta de que, personalmente, tendía a agrandar los problemas cuando tenía un entrenador (coach), porque eran cosas que sabía resolver por mi cuenta.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jackie about her experience with coaching and advice for PMs considering getting a coach. Jackie explains her personal approach to coaching - she prefers working with coaches when she has specific issues to address rather than ongoing general coaching. She discovered that bringing small problems to a coach sometimes made them feel unnecessarily magnified, so she uses coaching strategically for targeted skill development.

vocabulary.definition: In a way that relates to an individual rather than to someone else or to a group.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'personally' often indicates an individual's personal opinion or experience, distinguishing it from collective or organizational viewpoints.

insight.nuance: This term can convey a sense of ownership or emotional investment, making it more impactful in discussions about personal experiences or decisions.

vocabulary.definition: To find an answer to a problem or to deal with a difficult situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'solve' is frequently used in the context of problem-solving, innovation, and customer service, where finding effective solutions is crucial for success.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a sense of urgency and proactivity, suggesting that addressing issues is essential for progress.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you... it was a pretty effective way of advocating to get into this meeting.
keySentence: it was a pretty effective way of advocating to get into this meeting.
text_ko: 제가 그냥 같이 가면 시간도 에너지도 좀 절약해 드릴 수 있을 것 같아요... 사실 그 방식이 이 회의에 들어가도록 설득하는 데 꽤 효과적이었어요.
text_zh: 要是我加入你们，可能能帮你们省不少时间和精力……这是争取参加这次会议挺管用的办法。
text_es: Quizá te habría ahorrado algo de tiempo y energía si me hubiera sumado... fue una forma bastante efectiva de abrirse paso para entrar en esta reunión.
fullContext: Lenny asks what kept Jackie at Asana for eight years. Jackie explains how she grew within the company by strategically advocating for inclusion in higher-level planning meetings. When she found herself constantly asking her boss questions after his planning committee meetings, she positioned joining the meetings as a way to help him be more efficient rather than simply asking for more responsibility.

vocabulary.definition: The act of publicly supporting or recommending a particular cause or policy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, advocating often involves promoting ideas, products, or changes within an organization to influence decision-making and garner support from stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While advocating can imply a strong support for a cause, it may also carry a sense of urgency or passion that is not always appropriate in more neutral discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Producing a desired or intended result; successful in achieving a goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, effective strategies, processes, or communications are crucial for achieving objectives and maximizing productivity.

insight.nuance: The term 'effective' suggests not just success, but also efficiency in reaching outcomes, distinguishing it from merely being 'successful' which may imply a lack of efficiency.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: What I did is I wrote a document on the Local Universal Team, so I called it Local Universal Strategy. And I can't remember what I put in this document. I put it in just random... What my plan was.
keySentence: I wrote a document on the Local Universal Team, so I called it Local Universal Strategy.
text_ko: 제가 한 일은 로컬 유니버설 팀(Local Universal Team)에 관한 문서를 쓴 거예요. 그래서 '로컬 유니버설 전략(Local Universal Strategy)'이라고 이름 붙였고요. 근데 그 문서에 뭘 적어놨는지 기억이 잘 안 나요. 그냥 아무렇게나… 제 계획이 뭔지 대충 적어놨던 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我写了一份关于本地通用团队（Local Universal Team）的文档，就叫“本地通用战略（Local Universal Strategy）”。但我现在想不起来我往里具体写了什么，基本就是随便塞进去的……我当时到底打算怎么做也说不清楚。
text_es: Escribí un documento sobre el equipo Local Universal (Local Universal Team), así que lo titulé Estrategia Local Universal (Local Universal Strategy). Ahora no recuerdo qué incluí: lo hice un poco al azar... no sé cuál era mi plan.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jackie to define what strategy means in product management. Jackie explains how she initially struggled to understand strategy when she received feedback at Google that she needed to be 'more strategic' but no one could explain what that meant. She learned by writing down her strategic thinking and getting feedback, which helped her understand what others expected from strategic work.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, strategy refers to the comprehensive approach that organizations take to reach their goals, often involving market analysis and resource allocation.

insight.nuance: While 'strategy' implies a well-thought-out plan, it can also suggest flexibility and adaptability in response to changing circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: A written or electronic record that provides information or evidence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, documents can encompass reports, contracts, and proposals, serving as formal records that guide decision-making and compliance.

insight.nuance: The term 'document' often implies a level of formality and permanence, distinguishing it from casual notes or drafts.

vocabulary.definition: A detailed proposal for achieving a specific goal, often outlining steps and resources required.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a plan can refer to strategic initiatives, project timelines, or operational procedures that guide organizational activities.

insight.nuance: While 'plan' suggests a structured approach, it can also imply a degree of rigidity, which may not always be suitable in fast-paced environments.

speaker: Jackie Bavaro
text: Three parts of strategy are your vision. This is your inspiring picture of what the future looks like. And then you've got your strategic framework. This is where you're saying, 'Here is the market we're going after. Here's what success looks like.
keySentence: This is your inspiring picture of what the future looks like.
text_ko: 전략의 세 부분 중 하나가 바로 비전(vision)이에요. 비전은 미래가 어떤 모습일지에 대해 영감을 주는 그림이에요. 그리고 또 하나는 전략 프레임워크(strategic framework)이에요. 여기서는 '우리가 겨냥할 시장(market)은 어디고, 성공은 어떤 모습인지'를 정해요.
text_zh: 战略有三部分。第一是愿景(vision)，就是能激励人的未来画面。接着是战略框架(strategic framework)，在这部分你要说清楚：我们要瞄准的市场(market)是哪块，成功长什么样子。
text_es: La estrategia tiene tres partes: la visión. Es la imagen inspiradora de cómo será el futuro. Luego está tu marco estratégico: ahí dices, "este es el mercado al que vamos; así es como se ve el éxito."
fullContext: Jackie breaks down her framework for product strategy after years of learning what strategy actually means. She identifies three essential components that any complete strategy should include: an inspiring vision of the future, a strategic framework that defines the market and approach, and a roadmap that works backward from the vision to ensure the plan is realistic and achievable.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach that outlines the key components and direction of an organization's strategy, guiding decision-making and resource allocation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strategic framework helps teams align their efforts towards common goals, ensuring that all actions are coordinated and purposeful.

insight.nuance: The term implies a comprehensive and long-term perspective, often used when discussing high-level planning rather than day-to-day operations.

vocabulary.definition: An aspirational description of what an organization aims to achieve in the future, serving as a guiding star for its strategic direction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, a clear vision can motivate employees, attract investors, and provide a framework for decision-making and strategic initiatives.

insight.nuance: While often used interchangeably with mission, 'vision' specifically refers to future aspirations, making it more forward-looking and inspirational.

vocabulary.definition: The achievement of desired aims or goals, often measured by specific metrics or outcomes relevant to an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, success can be quantified through various indicators such as profit margins, market share, or customer satisfaction, and is crucial for long-term sustainability.

insight.nuance: Success can be subjective and context-dependent, varying significantly between different organizations or industries, and should be defined clearly to avoid ambiguity.

speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
text: I'd say test everything, we've run in the last four years over 600 experiments on the streaks, so every other day. We've actually set up really good infrastructure for copy testing.
keySentence: test everything, we've run in the last four years over 600 experiments on the streaks
text_ko: 전부 다 테스트해 보라고 말하고 싶어요. 지난 4년 동안 스트릭스(streaks) 관련해서 600건이 넘는 실험을 했어요. 거의 하루 걸러 한 번 꼴이에요. 실제로 카피 테스트(copy testing)를 위한 인프라도 정말 잘 갖춰놨아요.
text_zh: 我会说，什么都要测。过去四年里，我们在 streaks 功能（streaks）上做了 600 多个实验，差不多每两天就跑一个。其实我们已经把文案测试的基础设施（copy testing）搭得挺完善的。
text_es: Yo diría que prueben todo. En los últimos cuatro años hemos hecho más de 600 experimentos sobre los streaks (streaks), así que casi uno cada dos días. De hecho, hemos montado una infraestructura muy buena para hacer pruebas de copy (copy testing).
fullContext: Lenny asks Jackson about the key lessons and insights from Duolingo's journey of building and iterating on their streaks feature. Jackson is explaining Duolingo's philosophy of constantly testing and experimenting, sharing specific examples of how small changes like copy adjustments can have massive impact. He emphasizes the importance of testing rather than debating ideas internally, demonstrating how a simple change from 'continue' to 'commit to my goal' became a huge win for user engagement.

vocabulary.definition: The fundamental facilities and systems that support the operation of an organization or service, including physical structures and organizational frameworks.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, infrastructure refers to the underlying systems that enable operations, such as IT networks, software platforms, and logistical frameworks essential for efficient functioning.

insight.nuance: While often associated with physical structures, in a business context, it can also imply the organizational processes and technologies that support strategic goals.

vocabulary.definition: Systematic tests or trials conducted to discover or validate information, often involving the manipulation of variables to observe outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, experiments are crucial for product development and market research, allowing teams to test hypotheses and refine offerings based on data-driven insights.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a methodical approach to testing ideas, often implying a willingness to take risks and learn from failures.

vocabulary.definition: The act of evaluating a product, process, or concept to determine its functionality, performance, or quality, often through controlled conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, testing is essential for quality assurance, user experience optimization, and ensuring that products meet market needs before launch.

insight.nuance: While it implies a systematic approach, testing can also carry a connotation of trial and error, highlighting the importance of experimentation in innovation.

speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
text: And this is not just the subjective retention PM talking, I think this is our biggest feature, with the exception of the lessons. Streaks are a great engagement hack.
keySentence: Streaks are a great engagement hack for user retention at the core.
text_ko: 이건 단지 제가 리텐션 담당 PM(retention PM)이라서 하는 주관적인 말이 아니라, 레슨(lessons)을 제외하면 이게 우리 제품에서 가장 큰 기능이라고 생각해요. 스트릭스(Streaks)는 참여를 끌어올리는 효과적인 기법(engagement hack)이에요.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jackson to explain the impact that the streaks feature has had on Duolingo's success and growth. Jackson is emphasizing that while streaks can be a powerful engagement mechanic for any app, they only work when layered on top of a product that users genuinely want to use. He's making the point that streaks are an 'engagement hack' - a retention tool that amplifies user engagement - but cannot substitute for core product value.

vocabulary.definition: Retention refers to the ability to keep customers or employees engaged and continuing to use a product or service over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, retention is a critical metric that indicates customer loyalty and satisfaction, often measured through customer retention rates or employee turnover rates.

insight.nuance: While retention generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a need for improvement if retention rates are low, suggesting potential issues with customer satisfaction or product value.

vocabulary.definition: Engagement refers to the level of interaction, involvement, and emotional connection that users or employees have with a product, service, or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, engagement is often used to assess how actively users participate with a platform or how committed employees are to their work, impacting overall productivity and satisfaction.

insight.nuance: Engagement can be both positive and negative; high engagement often indicates a strong connection, while low engagement may suggest apathy or dissatisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: A feature is a distinctive attribute or aspect of a product or service that provides value to users and differentiates it from competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, features are often highlighted in marketing strategies to attract users and can be critical in product development discussions to ensure alignment with customer needs.

insight.nuance: While 'feature' typically has a neutral connotation, it can imply complexity or unnecessary additions if overused or poorly implemented.

speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
text: We have right now over 9 million users with a year plus streak. So, 9 million of our users have used Duolingo every year, almost every day, for well over a year. Which is pretty...
keySentence: Over 9 million users have a year plus streak, like a large city.
text_ko: 지금 1년 이상 연속 사용 기록(스트릭, streak)을 가진 사용자가 900만 명이 넘어요. 다시 말해 900만 명의 사용자가 1년 넘게 거의 매일 듀오링고를 사용해 왔어요. 그건 꽤 인상적이에요.
text_zh: 我们现在有超过900万用户保持一年以上的连胜（streak）。也就是说，有900万用户一年多来几乎每天都在用 Duolingo。挺厉害的。
text_es: Ahora mismo tenemos más de 9 millones de usuarios que llevan una racha de más de un año (streak). Es decir, 9 millones de nuestros usuarios han usado Duolingo casi todos los días durante más de un año. Lo cual es bastante...
fullContext: Jackson is providing concrete statistics to demonstrate the massive scale and impact of Duolingo's streaks feature. He's explaining that 9 million users have maintained streaks for over a year, meaning they've used the app almost daily for that entire period. He uses the analogy of imagining all these users as a large city to help contextualize the impressive scale of user engagement and retention that the streaks feature has achieved.

speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
text: What Duolingo really focuses on is, how do we help users build habits around language learning? Getting user come back the next day is the biggest problem to solve.
keySentence: Getting user come back the next day is the biggest problem to solve.
text_ko: 듀오링고가 진짜로 신경 쓰는 건 이용자들이 언어 학습을 습관화(habit formation)하도록 어떻게 도와줄지예요. 사용자가 다음 날에도 돌아오게 하는 게 가장 큰 문제예요.
text_zh: Duolingo真正关心的是，怎么帮用户养成学语言的习惯。让用户第二天还会回来，才是我们要解决的最大问题。
text_es: Lo que Duolingo realmente se pregunta es: ¿cómo ayudamos a los usuarios a convertir el aprendizaje de idiomas en un hábito? Conseguir que vuelvan al día siguiente es el mayor reto.
fullContext: Jackson is explaining Duolingo's core philosophy and approach to user retention. He's describing how Duolingo views the challenge of language learning - that the biggest obstacle isn't the learning content itself, but getting users to return consistently to build lasting habits. He emphasizes that from a growth perspective, streaks have objectively been their most effective tool for driving daily active users, which aligns with their broader growth strategy of focusing on retention rather than just acquisition.

vocabulary.definition: To build habits means to establish consistent behaviors or routines that become automatic over time. This often involves repeated actions that reinforce a desired behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and tech, building habits is crucial for user engagement, as companies strive to create products that encourage regular usage and integration into daily life.

insight.nuance: The phrase 'build habits' implies a long-term commitment to behavior change, often requiring strategies that promote gradual adoption rather than immediate results.

speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
text: We actually tested, hey, what if we make it even easier to extend your streak? And so, we actually tested, hey, if you do one exercise, just one exercise in a lesson will extend your streak.
keySentence: if you do one exercise, just one exercise in a lesson will extend your streak.
text_ko: 사실 저희가 '스트릭(streak)을 더 쉽게 이어가게 하면 어떨까?' 하고 실제로 테스트해봤어요. 한 레슨에서 연습 문제 하나만 해도 스트릭(streak)이 이어지도록요.
text_zh: 我们其实做了个测试，想看看要是把延长打卡天数(streak)弄得更容易会怎样。于是我们就试了：只要在一节课里做哪怕一个练习，打卡天数(streak)就会续上。
text_es: De hecho lo probamos: ¿y si lo hacemos aún más fácil para alargar la racha? Resultó que con hacer un solo ejercicio en una lección ya basta para que la racha se extienda.
fullContext: Jackson is sharing a specific example of an experiment that failed, where Duolingo tested making it even easier to maintain a streak by requiring just one exercise instead of a full lesson. This was following their successful experiment of simplifying streaks from XP-based to lesson-based. He explains that this experiment taught them about the importance of having a meaningful 'unit of measure' - the core action that users need to complete. Making the requirement too easy actually captured less engaged users and provided no benefit to daily active users.

vocabulary.definition: To increase the length, duration, or scope of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, extending often refers to expanding product features, service offerings, or customer engagement strategies to enhance user experience.

insight.nuance: While 'extend' generally has a positive connotation of growth and improvement, it can also imply overreach if not managed properly.

speaker: Jackson Shuttleworth
text: One of the fun ones that we did, and it's honestly as much about process as it is about the feature itself, was we have a feature called streak goal, and it is...
keySentence: it's honestly as much about process as it is about the feature itself
text_ko: 저희가 했던 재밌는 것들 중 하나였는데요, 솔직히 기능 자체만큼이나 그 과정을 중시한 프로젝트였어요. '연속 달성 목표(streak goal)'라는 기능이 있고, 그건...
text_zh: 我们做过的一个挺有意思的事儿，老实说这事儿跟功能本身比起来，更像是在讲流程。我们有个叫“连胜目标”(streak goal)的功能，它是……
text_es: Una de las cosas más divertidas que hicimos, y la verdad es que tiene tanto que ver con el proceso como con la funcionalidad (feature) en sí, fue implementar una funcionalidad llamada objetivo de rachas (streak goal), y es...
fullContext: Jackson is describing the development of Duolingo's 'streak goal' feature, which allows users to commit to reaching specific streak milestones. He's emphasizing how innovations often seem obvious in hindsight but were novel when first conceived. This feature emerged from focusing on the critical 0-7 day user experience, where they discovered that once users reach a 7-day streak, loss aversion kicks in and retention dramatically improves. The streak goal feature helps guide users toward that crucial milestone.

vocabulary.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end or result.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'process' often refers to workflows or methodologies that guide project execution and operational efficiency.

insight.nuance: While 'process' implies a systematic approach, it can sometimes suggest rigidity; in creative contexts, flexibility may be preferred.

vocabulary.definition: A distinctive attribute or aspect of a product or service that provides value to users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, 'feature' often describes specific functionalities within software or applications that enhance user experience and engagement.

insight.nuance: The term 'feature' can imply a selling point, but overemphasis on features without addressing user needs may lead to product failures.

speaker: Jag Duggal
text: We rarely scale a project, a product we've launched, until we know the Sean Ellis score and we know that it's hit a threshold that we find really compelling.
keySentence: We know the Sean Ellis score has hit a threshold we find really compelling.
text_zh: 我们很少会把一个上线的项目或产品扩大规模，除非我们知道它的 Sean Ellis 得分(Sean Ellis score)，并且确认这个得分已经达到让我们愿意大规模投入的门槛。
text_es: Rara vez escalamos un proyecto o producto que ya hayamos lanzado hasta que conozcamos la puntuación Sean Ellis (Sean Ellis score) y comprobemos que ha superado un umbral que nos resulte realmente convincente.
fullContext: Lenny asks about how Nubank measures whether customers truly love their products before scaling them. Jag explains that they use the Sean Ellis score methodology, which asks customers how disappointed they would be if the product went away. At Nubank, they require at least 50% of customers to say they would be 'very disappointed' before scaling a product, which is higher than the typical 40% threshold due to Brazilian customers being more polite and optimistic.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, capacity, or scope, often in a systematic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, scaling refers to the ability of a company to grow its operations and revenue without being hampered by its structure or available resources when facing increased production demands.

insight.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it can also suggest the need for careful planning to ensure that expansion does not compromise quality or efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: A point or level at which something begins or changes; a limit that must be reached.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a threshold often refers to metrics or benchmarks that must be met before a project can proceed or be considered successful.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a critical juncture, suggesting that crossing the threshold is necessary for further action or investment.

vocabulary.definition: Evoking interest, attention, or admiration in a powerfully irresistible way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a compelling product or idea is one that strongly attracts customers or investors due to its unique value proposition or potential impact.

insight.nuance: While 'compelling' often conveys a sense of urgency or necessity, it can also suggest a deeper emotional or intellectual appeal that resonates with stakeholders.

speaker: Jag Duggal
text: Good enough, isn't good enough. Is it great enough? Because that's the bar, particularly for some of our ten-pole products, but we try to apply it largely across the board. A lot of companies spend a ton of money on marketing.
keySentence: Good enough isn't good enough; we aim for great enough across the board.
text_ko: 그냥 '충분하다' 수준으론 안 돼요. 정말로 충분히 훌륭한가요? 그게 바로 기준이에요. 특히 일부 주력 제품(ten-pole products)에 대해서는 더더욱 그렇고, 가능한 한 전반에 걸쳐 그 기준을 적용하려고 해요. 많은 회사들이 마케팅에 막대한 돈을 써요.
text_zh: “差不多”不行。够不够出色？那才是我们的标准。尤其是对我们的一些重磅产品 (tentpole products)，但我们尽量把这个标准推广到大部分产品上。很多公司在营销 (marketing) 上花了很多钱。
text_es: Lo "suficientemente bueno" no basta. ¿Es realmente excelente? Porque ese es el listón, sobre todo para algunos de nuestros productos "ten-pole" (ten-pole), aunque tratamos de aplicarlo en buena parte de lo que hacemos. Muchas empresas gastan una fortuna en mercadotecnia (marketing).
fullContext: Lenny is asking about Nubank's approach to building products people love fanatically. Jag shares a phrase from their lead designer about raising the bar beyond just 'good enough' to 'great enough.' He explains this philosophy helps them avoid spending heavily on marketing since truly great products generate word-of-mouth growth instead of requiring massive advertising budgets.

vocabulary.definition: Core products or services that are essential to a company's success and generate significant revenue.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, ten-pole products are often the flagship offerings that define a brand and drive customer loyalty.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a strong reliance on these key products, and it is typically used in discussions about product strategy and portfolio management.

vocabulary.definition: Applicable to all cases or instances without exception.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'across the board' is often used to indicate that a policy, change, or standard will affect all departments or areas of the organization equally.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies inclusivity and uniformity, and is often used in contexts where comprehensive application is emphasized.

vocabulary.definition: Sufficient to meet a minimum standard but not exceptional or outstanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'good enough' can refer to products or services that meet basic requirements but may lack competitive edge or innovation.

insight.nuance: This phrase often carries a negative connotation, suggesting complacency rather than striving for excellence.

speaker: Jag Duggal
text: Don't ask a researcher to come up with a plan to go do the research to then summarize it, to then bring it to you, which has so many degrees of distance built in.
keySentence: which has so many degrees of distance built in.
text_ko: 연구자한테 계획 세우고 실제로 연구를 수행해서 요약한 다음 다시 가져오라고 하지 마세요. 그렇게 하면 중간 단계가 너무 많아져서 결과와 의도 사이에 간극이 생겨요.
text_zh: 别让研究员先拟个计划去做研究、再把总结拿回来给你——中间环节太多，信息早就被一层层稀释、脱节了。
text_es: No le pidas a un investigador que diseñe un plan, haga la investigación, te la resuma y luego te la entregue: eso introduce demasiados pasos intermedios.
fullContext: Lenny asks about how product managers can get closer to customer feedback. Jag explains Nubank's approach of having product managers directly call customers rather than going through multiple layers of research intermediaries. He advocates for this direct approach because it eliminates the distance between the product builder and customer voice, and patterns emerge quickly after just a few conversations.

vocabulary.definition: To present the main points or essential information of a larger body of work in a concise form.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, summarizing is crucial for communicating findings, reports, or proposals efficiently to stakeholders who may not have time to review the full details.

insight.nuance: While summarizing is often seen as a skillful way to distill information, it can sometimes oversimplify complex ideas, so care must be taken to retain key insights.

vocabulary.definition: A measure of separation or disconnection between two entities, often in terms of communication or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management or team dynamics, degrees of distance can refer to the levels of involvement or engagement among team members, affecting collaboration and decision-making.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a negative connotation, suggesting that too many layers of separation can hinder effective communication and lead to misunderstandings.

speaker: Jag Duggal
text: We are not going to take a small problem and scale it because if we do that, we end up with a big mess.
keySentence: We won't scale a small problem; it could end up with a big mess.
text_ko: 작은 문제를 그냥 스케일(scale)하지는 않을 거예요. 그렇게 하면 결국 큰 골칫거리가 돼요.
text_zh: 我们不会把小问题做大，因为那样最后只会把事情搞成一团糟。
text_es: No vamos a convertir un problema pequeño en uno grande; si lo hacemos, acabamos con un gran lío.
fullContext: Lenny is discussing the pressures product managers face to scale products quickly. Jag explains Nubank's disciplined approach of not scaling products until they have achieved product-market fit at a small scale. He emphasizes that it's better to solve problems when they're small rather than create bigger messes by scaling prematurely, and that proper scaling often happens naturally once the product is truly working.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, capacity, or scope, often in a systematic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, scaling refers to the ability of a company or system to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance.

insight.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it can also suggest the need for careful planning to avoid operational challenges.

vocabulary.definition: A situation that is disorganized or chaotic, often resulting from poor planning or execution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a 'mess' can refer to operational failures or mismanagement that lead to complications and inefficiencies.

insight.nuance: While 'mess' can convey a sense of urgency to rectify a situation, it may also carry a negative connotation that suggests a lack of professionalism.

speaker: Jag Duggal
text: We may not be right, but at least we are clear.
keySentence: We may not be right, but at least we are clear.
text_ko: 틀릴 수도 있겠지만, 적어도 우리가 하는 말은 분명해요.
text_zh: 也许我们不一定对，但至少把话说清楚了。
text_es: Puede que no acertemos, pero al menos dejamos las cosas claras.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jag about his approach to strategy development. Jag quotes Kevin Systrom from Instagram's early days to illustrate the importance of strategic clarity. He argues that having a clear strategy, even if imperfect, allows teams to quickly identify when they're going off course because they have concrete expectations about what should be happening.

speaker: Jag Duggal
text: We're not trying to be incrementally better. We are trying to be fundamentally different. We're in the business of being fundamentally different, not incrementally better. Only fundamentally different, gets customers to tell their friends.
keySentence: We are trying to be fundamentally different.
text_ko: 우리는 단지 점진적으로 더 나아지는 것(incrementally better)을 목표로 하지 않아요. 우리가 추구하는 건 근본적으로 다른 것(fundamentally different)이에요. 우리 비즈니스는 점진적 개선(incrementally better)을 하는 게 아니라 근본적 차이(fundamentally different)를 만드는 일이에요. 오직 근본적으로 다른 것만이 고객들이 친구들에게 이야기하게 만들어요.
text_zh: 我们不是想做得好一点（incrementally better）。我们想做的是彻底不一样（fundamentally different）。我们的生意就是去做到这种根本性的不同，而不是一点点的改进。只有真正不一样的东西，才会让客户主动去把它推荐给朋友。
text_es: No buscamos ser simplemente un poco mejores. Queremos ser radicalmente distintos. Nos dedicamos a eso: a ser radicalmente distintos, no a mejorar paso a paso. Solo lo verdaderamente distinto hace que los clientes se lo cuenten a sus amigos.
fullContext: Lenny is asking about Nubank's philosophy and approach to product development. Jag explains their core principle that appears on company mugs - they focus on being fundamentally different rather than incrementally better. He clarifies that while some features may be incremental improvements, they constantly search for anchor products and experiences that are fundamentally different because only those drive word-of-mouth growth.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic and essential way; at the core or root of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'fundamentally' often refers to a significant change or innovation that alters the foundational aspects of a product, service, or strategy.

insight.nuance: This term implies a deep, intrinsic change rather than superficial adjustments, making it suitable for discussions about transformative ideas.

vocabulary.definition: In small, gradual steps or amounts; progressively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, 'incrementally' describes improvements or changes that are made in small, manageable phases rather than through radical shifts.

insight.nuance: This term is often used to suggest a cautious or conservative approach to change, which may not always capture the urgency for innovation.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time. And for over a decade, John and I have been, in quotes, designing time as part of our work with startups, helping them find or expand product market fit.
keySentence: We designed time to help startups find or expand product market fit.
text_ko: 답을 드리기 전에 Make Time의 아주 짧은 역사를 먼저 말씀드릴게요. 지난 10년 넘게 존과 저는 소위 '시간을 설계한다'는 방식으로 스타트업들과 함께 일하면서 그들이 제품-시장 적합성(product-market fit)을 찾거나 확장할 수 있게 도와왔어요.
text_zh: 为交代清楚答案，我先简短介绍一下 Make Time 的来龙去脉。十多年来，我和 John 在和创业公司合作时，可以说一直在做所谓的“时间设计”，帮他们找到或扩大产品与市场的契合(product market fit)。
text_es: Para poner en contexto la respuesta, te voy a contar una historia súper breve de Make Time. Y durante más de una década, John y yo hemos estado, entre comillas, «diseñando el tiempo» como parte de nuestro trabajo con startups, ayudándoles a encontrar o ampliar el encaje producto‑mercado (product-market fit).
fullContext: Lenny asks Jake what most people get wrong when they're trying to become more productive. Jake begins by explaining the background of their book Make Time and how it emerged from their work with startups. He describes how they've been 'designing time' for over a decade through their work helping startups find product-market fit, which led to developing design sprints at Google Ventures.

vocabulary.definition: The process of intentionally structuring and allocating time to enhance productivity and efficiency in tasks or projects.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, 'designing time' refers to the strategic planning of schedules and workflows to optimize team performance and project outcomes.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a proactive approach to time management, suggesting that time can be shaped and utilized effectively rather than merely passing.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, scope, or capacity; to develop or grow in a particular area.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, 'expand' often refers to scaling operations, entering new markets, or broadening product offerings to reach a larger audience.

insight.nuance: While 'expand' generally has a positive connotation of growth, it can also imply the risks associated with overextension or loss of focus.

vocabulary.definition: The degree to which a product satisfies a strong market demand, indicating that a product is well-suited to its target audience.
vocabulary.businessContext: Achieving product market fit is crucial for startups as it validates their business model and is often seen as a key indicator of potential success and scalability.

insight.nuance: The term suggests not only the alignment of product features with customer needs but also the importance of ongoing adaptation to maintain that fit over time.

vocabulary.definition: Newly established businesses, typically in the early stages of development, focused on innovative products or services and often seeking rapid growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, startups are often characterized by their pursuit of disruptive ideas and reliance on venture capital to scale operations quickly.

insight.nuance: The term 'startup' conveys a sense of dynamism and risk-taking, but it can also imply instability and uncertainty in the early phases of business development.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: So, even though we are not productivity gurus, this hasn't been like this thing we were doing forever, it's not our full-time job, but we thought we want to share this framework.
keySentence: we are not productivity gurus
text_ko: 그래서 저희는 생산성 전문가도 아니고, 이걸 오래 해온 것도 아니고, 전업으로 하는 일도 아니지만, 이 프레임워크(framework)를 공유하고 싶었어요.
text_zh: 所以我们虽然不是生产力大师(productivity gurus)，也没一直做这件事、也不是全职在做，但还是想把这个框架分享给大家。
text_es: Así que, aunque no somos gurús de la productividad (productivity gurus), esto no es algo que llevemos haciendo siempre ni es nuestro trabajo a tiempo completo; aun así, pensamos que valía la pena compartir este marco (framework).
fullContext: Jake continues explaining the origin story of their Make Time book. He emphasizes that they aren't traditional productivity experts - this wasn't their main career focus, but rather emerged as a side project to share practical lessons they discovered while working with startups on design sprints and applying those insights to their personal productivity.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a particular issue.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, a framework often refers to a set of guidelines or best practices that help teams develop strategies, products, or processes more effectively.

insight.nuance: While 'framework' implies a supportive structure, it can also suggest rigidity; thus, it is important to use it when referring to established systems rather than informal or flexible methods.

vocabulary.definition: The measure of efficiency in converting inputs into outputs, often expressed in terms of output per unit of input.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, productivity is crucial for assessing performance, optimizing processes, and maximizing profitability.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a positive connotation of efficiency but may also imply pressure or stress when associated with unrealistic expectations.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: Our perspective is basically that those are the defaults. Just like our software that we use, apps that we use have defaults, those are the defaults of life, of the companies that we work in, the culture that we live in.
keySentence: those are the defaults of life, of the companies that we work in, the culture that we live in.
text_ko: 우리 관점은 기본적으로 그런 것들이 '기본값(defaults)'이라는 거예요. 우리가 쓰는 소프트웨어(software)나 앱(apps)에 미리 정해진 설정이 있듯이, 삶의 방식이나 우리가 일하는 회사들, 우리가 속한 문화에도 그런 기본값들이 있다는 얘기예요.
text_zh: 我们的观点很简单：那些就是默认(defaults)。就像我们用的软件和应用有默认设置一样，生活、我们工作的公司、我们所处的文化也都有这些默认。
text_es: Lo vemos así: eso viene por defecto. Igual que los programas (software) y las aplicaciones (apps) que usamos, la vida, las empresas donde trabajamos y la cultura en la que vivimos tienen esos ajustes por defecto (defaults).
fullContext: Lenny asks about what people get wrong with productivity, and John explains their core philosophy. He argues that most productivity advice focuses on being more efficient at existing tasks (emails, meetings), but their approach is about changing the fundamental defaults of how we structure our time, similar to how software has default settings that can be customized.

vocabulary.definition: Defaults refer to pre-set options or configurations that are automatically applied unless changed by the user.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, defaults often pertain to software settings or operational procedures that dictate standard practices within an organization.

insight.nuance: While defaults can streamline processes, they may also imply a lack of customization or adaptability if not reviewed regularly.

vocabulary.definition: Perspective is a particular attitude or way of considering something, often shaped by personal experiences and beliefs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, perspective can influence decision-making, strategic planning, and team dynamics, as it reflects how individuals interpret situations and challenges.

insight.nuance: Understanding different perspectives is crucial for collaboration and innovation, but it can also lead to conflict if not managed effectively.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: The idea of the busy bandwagon is just this expectation that everybody's busy.
keySentence: The busy bandwagon creates an expectation that everyone is busy.
text_ko: 바쁘다는 밴드왜건(busy bandwagon)은 그냥 모두가 바쁘다고 기대하는 거예요.
text_zh: 所谓“忙碌从众”（busy bandwagon），就是大家默认别人都很忙。
text_es: Lo que hay detrás de la moda de estar siempre ocupado es la expectativa de que todo el mundo esté ocupado.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the concepts of 'busy bandwagon' and 'infinity pools' that prevent people from making time for important things. Jake explains the busy bandwagon as a cultural expectation in the US where being busy is the default response and almost a badge of honor, creating internal pressure to always appear busy and reactive to others' demands.

vocabulary.definition: A belief or anticipation about what will happen in the future, often based on prior experiences or social norms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, expectations can refer to projected outcomes for sales, performance, or customer behavior, influencing strategic planning and decision-making.

insight.nuance: While expectations can drive motivation and performance, unrealistic expectations may lead to disappointment or burnout.

vocabulary.definition: A popular trend or activity that many people join or support, often without critical evaluation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, the 'bandwagon effect' can influence consumer behavior, leading companies to adopt popular strategies or products to remain competitive.

insight.nuance: While joining a bandwagon can lead to quick gains, it may also result in a lack of innovation or critical thinking if followed blindly.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: And so, when you put these two things together, the busy bandwagon and the infinity pool, you kind of have this, it's like a flywheel, but bad. You feel like you really need to be busy, you really need to be on top of everything.
keySentence: The busy bandwagon and infinity pool create a flywheel, but bad.
text_ko: 그래서 이 두 가지, 바쁜 밴드왜건(busy bandwagon)과 인피니티 풀(infinity pool)을 합치면 일종의 플라이휠(flywheel) 같긴 한데, 안 좋은 쪽이에요. 계속 바쁘지 않으면 안 될 것 같고, 모든 걸 다 챙기고 있어야 할 것 같은 느낌이에요.
text_zh: 把这两样东西放一起——大家都跟着忙的那股从众风潮 (busy bandwagon) 和无边泳池 (infinity pool)——就会形成一种有点像飞轮 (flywheel) 的循环，不过是糟糕的那种。你会觉得非得一直忙着，什么事都要亲自盯着。
text_es: Así que cuando juntas estas dos cosas —la moda de estar ocupado (busy bandwagon) y la piscina infinita (infinity pool)— se forma algo así como una rueda de inercia (flywheel), pero para mal: te hace sentir que tienes que estar siempre ocupado y que debes estar encima de todo.
fullContext: John is explaining how the busy bandwagon (cultural pressure to be busy) combines with infinity pools (endlessly refreshing content like social media and email) to create a destructive cycle. He describes how these two forces work together - the internal pressure to stay busy meets apps designed to capture attention, creating what he calls 'a flywheel, but bad.'

vocabulary.definition: To be in control of or fully aware of a situation, often implying effective management or oversight.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business environments, being 'on top of' tasks or projects indicates that a manager or team is effectively tracking progress and addressing issues proactively.

insight.nuance: While it conveys competence, overuse of this phrase may suggest an unrealistic expectation of constant vigilance, which can lead to stress.

vocabulary.definition: A swimming pool that creates the illusion of extending infinitely into the horizon, often used in luxury settings to enhance aesthetic appeal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the hospitality and real estate industries, infinity pools are marketed as premium features that enhance property value and attract clientele seeking luxury experiences.

insight.nuance: While primarily a design feature, the term can also metaphorically represent limitless possibilities or aspirations in business contexts.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: At any given point in time, I probably give myself a B to B-, and sometimes it's a C and sometimes it's a D, and sometimes it's an A, and I'm really plugging away, but it's totally an ongoing challenge.
keySentence: it's totally an ongoing challenge.
text_ko: 어떤 시점에선 제 자신에게 아마 B에서 B- 정도 점수를 주는 것 같아요. 가끔은 C나 D일 때도 있고, 또 가끔은 A일 때도 있어요. 정말 열심히 하고 있긴 한데, 계속되는 도전이에요.
text_zh: 说实话，我平时给自己打分大概是B到B-，有时候是C，有时候是D，偶尔能到A。我一直在努力，但这确实是个不断的挑战。
text_es: En un momento dado me pondría probablemente una B o B-; otras veces un C, otras un D y a veces una A. Estoy dándolo todo, pero sigue siendo un reto constante.
fullContext: Lenny asks Jake and John about their own productivity and how well they follow their Make Time framework. Jake gives an honest assessment of his own performance, rating himself between B- and D most days. He emphasizes that productivity is an ongoing challenge and he doesn't want to present himself as having it all figured out perfectly.

vocabulary.definition: A persistent difficulty or obstacle that requires continuous effort to address or overcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, an ongoing challenge may refer to issues such as market competition, resource allocation, or employee engagement that need constant attention and strategic planning.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies that the challenge is not a one-time issue but rather a recurring situation that demands sustained focus.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: The notion what the highlight is, start your day out and you imagine it's the end of the day, you're looking back on the day. If someone asked you, 'What was the highlight of your day,' what would you say?
keySentence: Looking back on the day, what was the highlight you want to remember?
text_ko: 이건 하루의 하이라이트가 무엇인지 미리 정해보는 개념이에요. 하루를 시작할 때 마치 하루가 끝나서 뒤돌아보고 있는 것처럼 상상해보세요. 누군가 '오늘 하루의 하이라이트가 뭐였어요?'라고 물어본다면 뭐라고 대답하겠어요?
text_zh: 有个想法是：一开始就想象这一天已经结束、你在回顾当天。如果有人问你“你今天的亮点是什么？”，你会怎么回答？
text_es: La idea de pensar cuál sería lo más destacado: empiezas la jornada imaginando que ya es el final y haces balance. Si alguien te preguntara, «¿Cuál fue lo mejor de tu día?», ¿qué dirías?
fullContext: Jake is explaining the concept of a 'highlight' - the central component of their Make Time framework. This is about choosing one main thing you want to accomplish each day by imagining what you'd want to tell someone was the best part of your day. It's the anchor that helps you structure your time around what truly matters to you.

vocabulary.definition: A notion is an idea, belief, or concept that may not be fully formed or substantiated. It often represents a preliminary understanding or impression of a subject.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, a notion may refer to an initial concept for a project or strategy that requires further development and validation before implementation.

insight.nuance: While 'notion' can imply a casual or vague understanding, it is often used in brainstorming sessions where ideas are still being explored.

vocabulary.definition: To highlight means to emphasize or make something stand out, often to draw attention to its importance or significance. It can also refer to the most notable or memorable part of an experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In presentations or reports, highlighting key findings or achievements is crucial for ensuring that stakeholders focus on the most impactful information.

insight.nuance: The term 'highlight' carries a positive connotation, suggesting that the emphasized element is worthy of recognition or celebration.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: So, most days, the first half of the day before lunch is my focus time, and I protect that very, very intensely, and then use that time to work on whatever my highlight is.
keySentence: I protect that very, very intensely focus time for my highlight work.
text_ko: 보통 점심 전 오전이 제 집중 시간이어서 그 시간을 정말 철저히 지켜요. 그 시간엔 그날의 하이라이트(highlight)에만 집중해요.
text_zh: 所以呢，大部分时候，上午到午饭前这段时间是我的专注时间，我会非常非常严格地保护这个时间段，然后用这个时间来处理我当天的重点工作。
text_es: Entonces, la mayoría de los días, toda la mañana hasta el almuerzo es mi tiempo de concentración, y lo cuido muchísimo, y uso ese tiempo para trabajar en lo que sea mi prioridad del día.
fullContext: John is describing his personal implementation of the Make Time framework as a venture capitalist. He explains how he structures his calendar to prioritize focused work time for his daily highlight, despite the naturally chaotic and meeting-heavy environment of VC work. This shows how to apply the highlight concept in a demanding professional context.

vocabulary.definition: A designated period during which an individual concentrates on a specific task or project without distractions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, focus time is crucial for productivity, allowing employees to engage deeply with their work, often leading to higher quality outcomes.

insight.nuance: Focus time implies a proactive approach to managing one's schedule, emphasizing the importance of uninterrupted work periods.

vocabulary.definition: To emphasize or make something stand out, often to draw attention to its significance or importance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In presentations and reports, highlighting key achievements or data points is vital for effective communication and persuasion.

insight.nuance: Highlighting suggests a selective focus on critical elements, which can influence perceptions and decisions.

speaker: Jake Knapp
text: This thing, I think we basically are steered toward becoming reaction machines and this notion of, 'I'm going to have an empty inbox. I'm going to do every task. I'm going to be a fast responder, I'm going to be in every meeting.
keySentence: We are steered toward becoming reaction machines and fast responders.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 우리는 기본적으로 반응 기계(reaction machines)가 되도록 몰리고 있는 것 같아요. '받은 편지함(empty inbox)을 비울 거야. 할 일은 다 해낼 거야. 답장은 빨리할 거야. 모든 회의에 다 들어갈 거야.' 같은 생각이요.
text_zh: 我觉得我们基本上被推着变成“反应机器”（reaction machines），大家都往那种思路走：要把收件箱清空（empty inbox）、把每项任务都做完、尽量快速回复（fast responder）、参加每一个会议……
text_es: Creo que esto nos está empujando a convertirnos en máquinas reactivas, con la mentalidad de: "voy a mantener la bandeja de entrada vacía (empty inbox), voy a hacer todas las tareas, voy a responder rápido (fast responder), voy a estar en todas las reuniones."
fullContext: Jake is explaining why people struggle with productivity and fall into reactive patterns. He describes how the desire to be helpful and responsive leads people to become 'reaction machines' - constantly responding to others' demands rather than focusing on their own important work. This reactive mode prevents people from doing meaningful, proactive work.

vocabulary.definition: An individual or entity that quickly reacts to inquiries, issues, or changes, often seen as a desirable trait in customer service and team dynamics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In customer service, being a fast responder is critical for maintaining customer satisfaction and loyalty, as it demonstrates attentiveness and reliability.

insight.nuance: While speed is important, being a fast responder should not come at the expense of thoroughness or accuracy in addressing issues.

vocabulary.definition: A general idea, belief, or concept that may not be fully formed or substantiated.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, notions can serve as the foundation for brainstorming sessions, innovation, and the development of new strategies or products.

insight.nuance: Notions can be seen as preliminary thoughts that require further exploration and validation before being acted upon in a business context.

speaker: Janna Bastow
text: Honestly, it wasn't so much that we set out to build a community, it was that we got together with some product people with the idea that we didn't know what we were doing.
keySentence: we got together with some product people with the idea that we didn't know what we were doing.
text_ko: 솔직히 말하면, 우리가 커뮤니티(community)를 만들려고 한 건 아니었어요. 오히려 프로덕트 사람들(product people) 몇 명이 ‘우리가 뭘 하는지 모른다’는 마음으로 모였던 거예요.
text_zh: 说实话，我们并不是一开始就打算去建个社区，更多是和几个产品人(product people)聚在一块儿，大家心里都清楚——我们其实也不知道自己在干什么。
text_es: La verdad no fue tanto que quisiéramos construir una comunidad; fue que nos juntamos con algunas personas de producto (product people) porque no teníamos ni idea de lo que estábamos haciendo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Janna about what has been most important in building and maintaining the quality of the Mind the Product community, which is the world's largest community of product managers. Janna explains that they didn't initially set out to build a community but rather came together with other product people because they felt uncertain about their work. The key insight is that successful communities often grow organically from genuine shared learning needs rather than being artificially constructed.

vocabulary.definition: To create and foster a group of individuals who share common interests or goals, often around a specific brand or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, building a community can enhance customer loyalty, facilitate feedback, and encourage user engagement, particularly in tech and startup environments.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a collaborative and inclusive approach, rather than a top-down directive.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who are involved in the development, management, and marketing of a product, typically including roles such as product managers, designers, and developers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, product people play a crucial role in aligning product features with customer needs and business objectives.

insight.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork among various roles focused on product success.

vocabulary.definition: To begin a journey or endeavor with a specific goal or intention in mind.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, this phrase often describes the initial phase of a project or initiative, highlighting the objectives that a team aims to achieve.

insight.nuance: It implies a sense of purpose and planning, but can also suggest that the outcome may evolve or change over time.

speaker: Janna Bastow
text: When running a conference, it's one of the most expensive and unleanest things you can possibly do. It's really difficult as a product person to pull that off, because it pulls at your heart. You want to do something that's lean iterative, but you can't.
keySentence: Running a conference is one of the most unleanest things you can do.
text_ko: 컨퍼런스(conference)를 운영하는 건 아마도 할 수 있는 일 중에서 비용이 가장 많이 들고 린(lean)하지 않은 일 중 하나예요. 프로덕트 담당자(product person) 입장에서는 그걸 해내기가 정말 어려운데, 자꾸 마음이 끌리거든요. 린(lean)하고 반복(iterative)적인 방식으로 해보고 싶지만, 그럴 수가 없어요.
text_es: Al organizar una conferencia, es una de las cosas más caras y menos eficientes (lean) que puedes hacer. Si eres de producto, es muy difícil sacarlo adelante porque te toca la fibra: quieres hacerlo de forma iterativa y eficiente (lean), pero no puedes.
fullContext: Lenny asks Janna about mistakes they made while building their community. Janna explains the challenges of running conferences, particularly how they conflict with typical product management principles. She describes conferences as 'unlean' because unlike product development where you can iterate quickly, conference problems must be solved in real-time without the ability to iterate until the following year.

vocabulary.definition: Costing a lot of money; high in price.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term 'expensive' often refers to products, services, or operations that require significant financial investment, impacting budgeting and profitability.

insight.nuance: While 'expensive' typically has a negative connotation, it can also imply high quality or value in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by inefficiency or excess; not streamlined.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'unleanest' describes processes or operations that are burdened with unnecessary steps, leading to wasted resources and time.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in contrast to 'lean,' which emphasizes efficiency and minimalism in operations.

vocabulary.definition: Involving repetition; a process that is refined through successive cycles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development and project management, 'iterative' refers to a methodology where products are developed in incremental stages, allowing for continuous improvement based on feedback.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a flexible approach to development, contrasting with linear or rigid methodologies.

speaker: Janna Bastow
text: One of the things that I have been super lucky in my career is that by being part of Mind the Product I've gotten to watch every last Mind the Product speaker, top end speakers.
keySentence: by being part of Mind the Product I've gotten to watch every last Mind the Product speaker
text_ko: 제 경력에서 정말 운이 좋았던 것 중 하나는 Mind the Product의 일원이 되어 최정상급 연사들(top-end speakers)을 하나도 빠짐없이 직접 볼 수 있었다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我职业生涯里有一件特别幸运的事：作为 Mind the Product（Mind the Product）的一员，我有机会见识到他们的每一位顶尖演讲者。
text_es: Una de las cosas por las que he tenido la enorme suerte en mi carrera es que, al formar parte de Mind the Product, he podido ver a todos y cada uno de sus ponentes, incluidos los de primer nivel (top-end speakers).
fullContext: Lenny asks Janna about what has helped her become a better speaker and storyteller, noting that communication skills are crucial for product leaders. Janna explains that her unique position with Mind the Product gave her extensive exposure to high-quality speakers. This allowed her to develop pattern recognition for effective presentations by observing audience reactions and understanding what techniques work versus what fails.

vocabulary.definition: Highly regarded or exceptional speakers, often recognized for their expertise and ability to engage an audience effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In conferences and industry events, top end speakers are sought after for their insights and ability to inspire, making them valuable assets for attracting attendees and enhancing the event's reputation.

insight.nuance: The term 'top end' suggests a level of exclusivity and high quality, often associated with industry leaders or renowned experts.

speaker: Janna Bastow
text: One of the things that I've stopped doing is I used to sit down with a PowerPoint and start writing my deck in PowerPoint or Slides, now. What I now do is I start with my story points. I start with my narratives.
keySentence: I start with my story points and fit it into the deck.
text_ko: 제가 그만둔 것 중 하나는 예전엔 파워포인트(PowerPoint)나 슬라이드(Slides)를 켜고 바로 프레젠테이션(덱, deck)을 작성하던 거예요. 지금은 먼저 스토리 포인트(story points), 그러니까 전달할 내러티브(narratives)부터 정리해요.
text_zh: 有件事我不做了：以前我会坐下来直接在PPT (PowerPoint) 或 Slides (Slides) 里把整套幻灯片做出来。现在我都是先把要讲的点和故事线理清楚，先把叙事搭好，再去做幻灯片。
text_es: Una de las cosas que he dejado de hacer es sentarme con una presentación (PowerPoint o Slides) y armarla diapositiva por diapositiva. Ahora empiezo por los puntos clave de la historia (story points) y por mi narrativa (narratives).
fullContext: Lenny asks Janna about lessons from her speaking coach that she continues to apply to new presentations. Janna shares a key insight about presentation preparation methodology. She explains that she used to get trapped in 'presentation mode' by starting with slides, but now focuses on crafting the narrative first and then building slides to support that story, which creates more compelling and coherent presentations.

vocabulary.definition: Structured accounts or stories that convey information, ideas, or experiences in a compelling manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, narratives are used to frame company missions, product stories, or customer experiences, making complex information more relatable and memorable.

insight.nuance: Narratives often carry emotional weight and are used strategically to influence perceptions and drive engagement.

vocabulary.definition: A unit of measure used in agile project management to estimate the complexity or effort required to complete a task or feature.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, story points help teams prioritize work and manage project timelines by translating user stories into quantifiable metrics.

insight.nuance: Story points emphasize relative estimation rather than absolute time, encouraging teams to focus on complexity and effort rather than duration.

speaker: Janna Bastow
text: So the whole beef with the timeline roadmap is just taking apart the concept of the timeline. It doesn't mean we live in la la land.
keySentence: The whole beef with the timeline roadmap is not penalizing ourselves with dates.
text_ko: 그래서 타임라인 로드맵(timeline roadmap)에 대한 모든 불만은 결국 타임라인(timeline)이라는 개념을 다시 뜯어보자는 거예요. 그렇다고 우리가 현실 감각을 잃었다는 뜻은 아니에요.
text_zh: 所以大家对时间线路线图 (timeline roadmap) 的抱怨，其实就是在拆解“时间线”这个概念。这并不代表我们在做白日梦。
text_es: El problema con la hoja de ruta (timeline roadmap) es que básicamente se está desmontando la idea del cronograma. Eso no quiere decir que vivamos en las nubes.
fullContext: Lenny asks Janna to explain her strong feelings against Gantt-based roadmapping. Janna clarifies her position on timeline-based roadmaps, explaining that she's not against all dates but rather against forcing artificial deadlines on every item. Her 'now, next, later' framework allows for dates when genuinely necessary (like regulatory deadlines) while avoiding the problems that arise when everything must have a timeline commitment.

vocabulary.definition: A roadmap is a strategic plan that outlines the goals, milestones, and steps necessary to achieve a particular objective or vision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a roadmap serves as a guiding document that helps teams align their efforts and track progress towards product development, project timelines, or strategic initiatives.

insight.nuance: While a roadmap provides a high-level overview, it is often subject to change based on market conditions or organizational priorities, making it important to communicate its flexible nature.

vocabulary.definition: A timeline is a graphical representation that displays a sequence of events or milestones in chronological order, often used to illustrate project schedules or historical developments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and business planning, timelines help stakeholders visualize deadlines, dependencies, and the overall duration of tasks or phases within a project.

insight.nuance: Timelines can vary in detail and format, and while they are useful for planning, they may not capture the complexity of interrelated tasks or unforeseen delays.

vocabulary.definition: A concept is an abstract idea or a general notion that serves as a foundation for understanding or developing a theory, product, or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and innovation, concepts are critical for brainstorming new ideas, developing marketing strategies, or creating product prototypes that address specific market needs.

insight.nuance: The term 'concept' often implies a preliminary stage of development, and it is important to differentiate between a concept and a fully realized product or plan.

speaker: Janna Bastow
text: So the value isn't the prototype, the value is in the prototyping process. The value isn't in your roadmap, the value is in the roadmapping process. What you're actually doing is laying out your assumptions of the problems that you're solving.
keySentence: The value is in laying out your assumptions during the prototyping process.
text_ko: 가치는 프로토타입(prototype) 자체에 있는 게 아니라 프로토타이핑 과정(prototyping process)에 있어요. 로드맵(roadmap)도 마찬가지로, 로드맵 수립 과정(roadmapping process)에 가치가 있어요. 결국 우리가 실제로 하는 건 해결하려는 문제들에 대한 가정들을 정리해 놓는 거예요.
text_zh: 所以，价值不在于原型 (prototype)，而在于做原型的过程 (prototyping process)。价值不在于路线图 (roadmap)，而在于制定路线图的过程 (roadmapping process)。你其实是在把关于要解决的问题的那些假设摆出来。
text_es: El valor no está en el prototipo (prototype); el valor está en el proceso de prototipado (prototyping process).
