vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, magical thinking can be critiqued when entrepreneurs or stakeholders hold unrealistic expectations about success without grounding their beliefs in data or practical analysis.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting naivety or a lack of critical thinking, and is best used to caution against overly optimistic or unfounded assumptions.

speaker: Katie Dill
text: But between all of those highlights, there were so many B moments that get shoved under the rug because it's just easier for me and it's more impressive for others.
keySentence: Many B moments get shoved under the rug, but they are part of our lives.
text_ko: 하지만 그 하이라이트들 사이사이에는 제게는 더 편하고 다른 사람들한테는 더 인상적으로 보이니까 그냥 묻혀버리는 B급 순간들(B moments)이 정말 많았어요.
text_zh: 但是在这些高光时刻之间，有太多平淡的B级时刻被我刻意掩盖了，因为这样对我来说更省事，对别人来说也更有面子。
text_es: Pero entre todos esos momentos de gloria, hubo muchas situaciones regulares que prefiero no mencionar porque me resulta más fácil y queda mejor con los demás.
fullContext: Lenny asks Gina about her concept of having both an 'A side' and 'B side' to everyone's career - where the A side contains impressive achievements that people share publicly. Gina explains that people naturally focus on sharing their highlights (A side) while hiding their failures and struggles (B side), but she believes it's important to acknowledge these B moments because they're a normal part of everyone's professional journey.

vocabulary.definition: Evoking admiration through size, quality, or skill; remarkable.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, something that is impressive can refer to a product, presentation, or achievement that stands out and captures the attention of stakeholders or clients.

insight.nuance: While 'impressive' generally has a positive connotation, it can sometimes imply that the quality is superficial or not backed by substance.

vocabulary.definition: The most important or notable parts of something; key features.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business report or presentation, highlights refer to the key achievements or significant data points that are emphasized to convey success or progress.

insight.nuance: The term 'highlights' suggests a focus on positive aspects, potentially overlooking less favorable details.

vocabulary.definition: To conceal or ignore something unpleasant or problematic.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, issues that are 'shoved under the rug' may refer to unresolved conflicts or failures that are overlooked to maintain a facade of success.

insight.nuance: This phrase carries a negative connotation, suggesting avoidance rather than resolution, and is often used to criticize management practices.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: there was that first two-day period where it was complete chaos at Twitter with the sink and Elon spreading his tentacles trying to find out who are the people that he wants to keep
keySentence: Elon spread his tentacles during the complete chaos at Twitter's takeover.
text_ko: 초반 이틀 동안 트위터는 완전히 혼란스러웠어요. 싱크(sink)도 있었고, 일론은 촉수를 뻗어 누구를 남겨두고 싶어하는지 알아내느라 분주했어요.
text_es: Hubo esos primeros dos días en los que todo fue un caos en Twitter: con el "sink" (the sink) y Elon extendiendo sus tentáculos para averiguar a quiénes quería mantener.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kayvon to share the story about getting Elon Musk up to speed at Twitter after the acquisition. Kayvon explains the chaotic first days after Elon took control of Twitter in October 2022, following an eight-month legal battle. During this period, Elon was trying to identify key personnel and interesting projects at the company. Scott Belsky had recommended that Elon speak with Kayvon, leading to their first meeting.

vocabulary.definition: A state of complete disorder and confusion, often characterized by unpredictability and a lack of organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, chaos can refer to periods of instability during major changes, such as mergers, acquisitions, or leadership transitions, where normal operations are disrupted.

insight.nuance: While chaos often has negative connotations, it can also lead to innovation and new opportunities if managed effectively.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: We wanted to change the lack of ambition, the lack of creativity, the lack of customers feeling that the product had changed at all.
keySentence: the lack of ambition, the lack of creativity, the lack of customers feeling that the product had changed at all.
text_ko: 우리는 야망과 창의성이 부족한 현실, 그리고 고객들이 제품이 전혀 달라졌다고 느끼지 못하는 상황을 바꾸고 싶었어요.
text_zh: 我们想改变那种没有冲劲、缺乏创新、客户根本察觉不到产品有任何变化的现状。
text_es: Queríamos acabar con la falta de ambición y creatividad, y con que los clientes no notaran para nada que el producto había cambiado.
fullContext: Lenny asks about how Kayvon transformed Twitter's product culture from stagnant to shipping regularly. Kayvon explains that while Twitter had successfully returned to user growth by 'refining the core' and optimizing existing features, this approach had made the organization risk-averse. He wanted to maintain that growth while also adding new capabilities and addressing customer complaints that the product hadn't meaningfully changed in years.

vocabulary.definition: A strong desire to achieve success or a particular goal, often requiring determination and hard work.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, ambition is crucial for driving growth, innovation, and competitive advantage, as it motivates individuals and teams to pursue challenging objectives.

insight.nuance: While ambition is generally viewed positively, it can sometimes imply a relentless pursuit of success that may overlook ethical considerations.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to generate original ideas, solutions, or products through imaginative thinking.
vocabulary.businessContext: Creativity is essential in business for product development, marketing strategies, and problem-solving, enabling companies to differentiate themselves in the market.

insight.nuance: Creativity is often associated with artistic endeavors but is equally important in analytical and technical fields, where innovative solutions are needed.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: I might flame out completely, but hell if I don't try. And so that was both fun and exhausting, like I said.
keySentence: I might flame out completely, but hell if I don't try to innovate.
text_ko: 완전히 망해버릴 수도 있지만, 그래도 해보지 않으면 안 되죠. 그래서 말했듯이 재밌기도 했고, 진짜로 많이 지쳤어요.
text_zh: 我可能会彻底栽跟头，但我偏要试一试。就像我说的，那既好玩也挺折腾的。
text_es: Podría estrellarme por completo, pero vaya si no lo intento. Así que fue a la vez divertido y agotador, como dije.
fullContext: Kayvon continues explaining his approach to transforming Twitter's product culture. He describes his mindset when taking on the challenge of making Twitter more innovative and ambitious. He emphasizes that the starting point was being passionate users of Twitter themselves, as he believes you need to be a customer of the product to build something wonderful. This was part of his strategy to identify pain points and build features they themselves wanted to use.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: The sacred cows are like their own roadmap. What are all the things that you think we're not allowed to change? Let's start there. Everything from moving from reverse chron to a ranked feed, that was a sacred cow.
keySentence: What are all the things that you think we're not allowed to change?
text_ko: 건드리지 말아야 할 것들(sacred cows)이 마치 그들만의 로드맵처럼 작동해요. 우리가 바꿀 수 없다고 생각하는 게 뭐가 있는지 다 얘기해 보세요. 시간 역순(reverse chron)에서 순위 기반 피드(ranked feed)로 옮기는 것까지, 그 모든 게 신성시되는 것이었어요.
text_zh: 那些不准动的“禁区”反而成了他们自己的路线图。你觉得有哪些东西是我们不能改的？先从这儿开始。比如把倒序时间线（reverse chron）换成按算法排序的推荐流（ranked feed），以前就是禁区。
text_es: Las vacas sagradas son como su propia hoja de ruta. ¿Qué cosas piensan que no podemos cambiar? Empecemos por ahí. Todo, desde pasar del orden cronológico inverso (reverse chron) a un feed ordenado por ranking (ranked feed), era una vaca sagrada.
fullContext: Kayvon explains his strategy for driving product innovation at Twitter. He describes how Twitter had many 'sacred cows' - long-held beliefs about things that couldn't be changed. Rather than seeing these as obstacles, he flipped the perspective and used them as a roadmap for potential improvements. These untouchable elements included the chronological timeline, the 140-character limit, and policies around user control over their reply spaces.

vocabulary.definition: A term used to describe beliefs, practices, or policies that are unchangeable or immune to criticism within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'sacred cows' often refer to established procedures or products that are considered too important to challenge, even if they may hinder progress or innovation.

insight.nuance: This phrase can carry a negative connotation, suggesting resistance to change and a lack of critical evaluation.

vocabulary.definition: A strategic plan that outlines the steps or milestones needed to achieve specific goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, a roadmap serves as a guiding document that communicates the vision and direction for product development and market strategy.

insight.nuance: While it typically implies a clear path forward, a roadmap can also suggest rigidity if not regularly updated to reflect changing circumstances.

vocabulary.definition: A method of displaying content or information in a prioritized order based on relevance, engagement, or other criteria.
vocabulary.businessContext: In digital platforms, a ranked feed is used to enhance user experience by presenting the most pertinent content first, thereby increasing user engagement and satisfaction.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a systematic approach to content delivery, which can be contrasted with chronological feeds that may not prioritize relevance.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: I remember we had a PM on our team who was leading this feature who a few weeks into this project mentioned to me that she had had a conversation with someone on the engineering team that told them, 'Don't work on this feature.
keySentence: Don't work on this feature.
text_ko: 기억해요. 우리 팀에 이 기능(feature)을 담당해 리드하던 프로덕트 매니저(PM)가 있었는데, 프로젝트 시작한 지 몇 주쯤 됐을 때 그분이 엔지니어링 팀(engineering team)의 한 사람과 얘기했더니 그 사람이 "이 기능은 작업하지 마"라고 말했다고 제게 전했어요.
text_zh: 我记得我们团队有个负责这个功能的产品经理（PM）。项目开始几周后，她跟我说她和工程团队（engineering team）里一个人聊过，那人跟他们说：“别做这个功能。”
text_es: Recuerdo que teníamos una responsable de producto (PM) en el equipo que lideraba esta funcionalidad (feature) y que, unas semanas después de arrancar el proyecto, me comentó que había hablado con alguien del equipo de ingeniería que le había dicho: «No trabajes en esta funcionalidad».
fullContext: Kayvon shares a specific example of Twitter's risk-averse culture while discussing the 'hide replies' feature. This feature would allow users to hide unwanted replies to their tweets, giving them more control over their reply space without impacting free speech. The story illustrates how deeply ingrained the resistance to change was at Twitter - an engineer actually advised a product manager not to work on the feature because it was seen as career-damaging to be associated with initiatives that challenged Twitter's established principles.

vocabulary.definition: A distinct attribute or aspect of a product or service that provides value to users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, features are often discussed in the context of product development, where teams prioritize which features to implement based on user feedback and market demand.

insight.nuance: The term 'feature' can imply a technical specification or a user-facing capability, and it's important to distinguish between essential features and those that are merely 'nice to have.'

vocabulary.definition: An informal exchange of ideas, thoughts, or information between two or more individuals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, conversations are crucial for collaboration, networking, and decision-making, often taking place in meetings, emails, or casual discussions.

insight.nuance: While 'conversation' suggests a two-way dialogue, it can also refer to a more structured discussion, so context is important to clarify the nature of the interaction.

vocabulary.definition: The application of scientific and mathematical principles to design, build, and analyze structures, machines, and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech companies, engineering refers to the teams responsible for developing software and hardware products, and their work is often central to a company's innovation and competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: The term can encompass various fields, including software engineering, mechanical engineering, and civil engineering, and is often associated with technical expertise and problem-solving skills.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: you've got to identify whether someone's on the wagon or off the wagon and either quickly convince them to get on the wagon or if they're not on the wagon, they shouldn't be there.
keySentence: Identify if someone's on the wagon or off the wagon to drive cultural change.
text_ko: 누가 온 더 왜건(on the wagon)에 있는지, 아니면 오프 더 왜건(off the wagon)인지 빨리 파악해서, 온 상태가 되도록 재빨리 설득하든지, 그렇지 않다면 그 자리에 있어서는 안 돼요.
text_zh: 你得判断清楚一个人到底是在这条船上还是不在，要么尽快把他们拉上来，要么他们就别待在这儿。
text_es: Tienes que identificar si alguien está a bordo o no: o convencerlo rápido de que se suba al proyecto, o, si no lo está, no debería estar ahí.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the ingredients that helped turn around Twitter's product culture. Kayvon explains that after building momentum and telling a compelling vision story, team members would either be inspired by the new direction or remain pessimistic. He describes the critical need to determine who was aligned with the cultural change vision ('on the wagon') versus who wasn't, and to act accordingly. He admits Twitter was terrible at this and lacked the organizational structure to make swift decisions about team alignment.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or establish the identity of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, identifying key stakeholders, market trends, or customer needs is crucial for strategic decision-making and effective communication.

insight.nuance: While 'identify' is often used in a straightforward manner, it can imply a deeper analysis or understanding when used in strategic discussions.

vocabulary.definition: To persuade someone to believe or do something through reasoning or argument.
vocabulary.businessContext: Convincing stakeholders, clients, or team members is essential in negotiations, sales, and marketing efforts to achieve desired outcomes.

insight.nuance: The term 'convince' carries a connotation of influence and may imply a challenge, as it suggests that the other party initially holds a different view.

speaker: Kayvon Beykpour
text: You need a special type of person to be able to both operate within the existing structure and change the structure, to know when to use the system and to know when to fuck the system.
keySentence: You need to know when to fuck the system and when to operate within it.
text_ko: 기존 구조 안에서 잘 운영할 수 있으면서도 그 구조를 바꿀 줄 아는, 즉 시스템을 언제 활용해야 하고 언제 과감히 무시해야 하는지를 아는 그런 특별한 사람이 필요해요.
text_zh: 你需要那种既能在现有体系里运作、又能去改变体系的人，知道什么时候该利用系统，什么时候该不按常规出牌。
text_es: Se necesita una persona especial que pueda operar dentro de la estructura existente y, al mismo tiempo, cambiarla; que sepa cuándo usar el sistema y cuándo saltárselo.
fullContext: Kayvon explains Twitter's strategy of using small acquisitions and acquihires to drive cultural change and lead ambitious product initiatives. He describes how they would acquire founders and entrepreneurs to lead speculative bets like Spaces, Communities, and Community Notes (formerly Birdwatch). These leaders needed to balance entrepreneurial startup skills with the savviness to navigate a large organization. Kayvon reflects on how this strategy helped him personally, as he was a beneficiary of such a bet when Periscope was acquired.

vocabulary.definition: To function or perform tasks while adhering to established rules, systems, or structures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, this phrase often refers to working effectively within the constraints of organizational policies or frameworks.

insight.nuance: It implies a level of compliance and adaptability, suggesting that one is capable of navigating existing systems without challenging them.

vocabulary.definition: To alter the framework or organization of a system, process, or entity to improve efficiency or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: This phrase is commonly used in discussions about organizational development, where leaders seek to modify hierarchies or workflows to better meet business goals.

insight.nuance: It carries a connotation of innovation and transformation, often associated with strategic initiatives aimed at long-term improvement.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: Every business that you have heard of has gotten rejected by at least a handful of venture capitalists at one point or another. And so that drive to keep going if you believe in the business is critical, absolutely critical.
keySentence: Every business faces rejection; the drive to keep going is critical.
text_ko: 여러분이 들어본 거의 모든 사업은 언젠가 적어도 몇몇 벤처 투자자(venture capitalists)에게 거절당한 적이 있어요. 그러니까 비즈니스를 믿는다면 포기하지 않고 계속 나아가려는 의지가 정말 중요해요, 절대적으로 중요해요.
text_zh: 你听说过的每家公司，都在某个时候被好几位风险投资人(venture capitalists)拒过。所以如果你看好这门生意，能坚持下去的那股劲儿非常关键，真的至关重要。
text_es: Todas las empresas de las que has oído hablar han sido rechazadas por al menos un puñado de capitalistas de riesgo (venture capitalists) en algún momento. Por eso, el empuje para seguir adelante cuando crees en tu negocio es fundamental, absolutamente fundamental.
fullContext: Lenny asks Keith about advice for founders going through tough fundraising periods. Keith reflects on DoorDash's difficult Series D funding round, when they had very little runway left and had been rejected by numerous venture capitalists. He emphasizes that rejection is universal among successful businesses and shares how Tony Xu's persistence was crucial during their near-bankruptcy situation.

vocabulary.definition: Of great importance; essential for success or failure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being 'critical' often refers to decisions or factors that can significantly impact the viability of a project or company.

insight.nuance: While it can imply urgency, 'critical' also suggests a level of importance that cannot be understated, making it suitable for high-stakes discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Investors who provide capital to startups and small businesses with perceived long-term growth potential in exchange for equity.
vocabulary.businessContext: Venture capitalists play a crucial role in the startup ecosystem by funding innovative ideas and helping entrepreneurs scale their businesses.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of high risk and high reward, as venture capitalists typically invest in early-stage companies that may not yet be profitable.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: And for me, one of the top things I always hear about DoorDash from an executive standpoint when we do the internal survey is it's a "no politics, no asshole" culture.
keySentence: DoorDash has a no politics, no asshole culture from an executive standpoint.
text_ko: 제 경험상, 내부 설문조사를 하면 임원들 사이에서 도어대시(DoorDash)에 대해 가장 자주 듣는 말 중 하나가 "정치질 없고 무례한 사람이 없는 문화"예요.
text_zh: 对我来说，我们做内部调查时，高管们常说DoorDash有种“不搞办公室政治、不容混蛋”的文化（'no politics, no asshole'）。
text_es: Para mí, una de las principales cosas que siempre oigo sobre DoorDash por parte de los ejecutivos, cuando hacemos la encuesta interna, es que tienen una cultura de "sin juegos de poder ni gente tóxica" (no politics, no asshole).
fullContext: Lenny asks Keith about a story where he called a candidate an "asshole" during the interview process. Keith explains DoorDash's "no politics, no asshole" culture and describes how Ryan Sokol, who is now their VP of engineering, initially came across as aloof and gave curt answers during his interview, which made Keith concerned about cultural fit.

vocabulary.definition: A perspective or viewpoint that reflects the considerations and priorities of senior management or executives within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, discussing issues from an executive standpoint often involves focusing on strategic decisions, financial implications, and overall organizational goals.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the importance of high-level decision-making and may imply a disconnect from the operational or employee-level perspectives.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic method of gathering information and feedback from employees within an organization to assess various aspects of the workplace.
vocabulary.businessContext: Internal surveys are commonly used in businesses to gauge employee satisfaction, engagement, and organizational culture, often influencing management decisions.

insight.nuance: While valuable for insight, internal surveys may be subject to bias if employees feel their responses could impact their job security.

vocabulary.definition: The shared values, beliefs, and behaviors that characterize an organization and influence its practices and interactions among employees.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, culture plays a critical role in shaping employee engagement, retention, and overall organizational effectiveness, often being a key factor in recruitment.

insight.nuance: The term can carry both positive and negative connotations, depending on whether it reflects a supportive environment or a toxic atmosphere.

vocabulary.definition: The activities, actions, or policies used to gain and maintain power within an organization, often involving negotiation and influence among individuals or groups.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, politics can refer to the dynamics of power relationships that affect decision-making and resource allocation, sometimes leading to conflicts or alliances.

insight.nuance: While some level of politics is inevitable in organizations, excessive political maneuvering can create a toxic work environment and hinder collaboration.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: Life's too short to work with people you don't really enjoy.
keySentence: Life's too short to work with people you don't really enjoy.
text_ko: 인생은 짧아요. 함께 일하는 게 정말 즐겁지 않은 사람들과는 굳이 일하지 않는 게 좋아요.
text_zh: 人生苦短，别跟合不来的人共事。
text_es: La vida es demasiado corta para trabajar con gente con la que no disfrutas colaborar.
fullContext: Keith continues the story about Ryan Sokol's hiring process. After having dinner and addressing the cultural concerns directly, Ryan later explained that DoorDash's willingness to potentially reject a qualified candidate solely based on attitude actually convinced him to join. This demonstrated to Ryan that the company genuinely prioritized cultural fit over just technical qualifications.

vocabulary.definition: To take pleasure in or derive satisfaction from an experience or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a workplace setting, enjoying one's work can lead to higher morale, productivity, and employee retention, making it a critical factor in organizational culture.

insight.nuance: While the term is generally positive, it should be used carefully in professional contexts to maintain a balance between enjoyment and professionalism.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: If you want to achieve a 10x outcome, hiring someone that's an expert in the field, it's maybe unlikely you're going to achieve that 10x outcome, because they're likely to do things the way things have always been done.
keySentence: they're likely to do things the way things have always been done.
text_ko: 만약 10배 성과(10x outcome)를 내고 싶다면, 해당 분야의 전문가를 채용한다고 해서 그 목표를 달성할 가능성은 낮아요. 전문가들은 대개 기존에 해오던 방식대로 일을 처리하려는 경향이 있거든요.
text_zh: 如果你想实现10倍的成果 (10x outcome)，去请行业里的专家反而不太可能做到，因为他们往往会照老一套做事。
text_es: Si buscas un resultado 10x (10x outcome), es poco probable que lo consigas contratando a alguien que sea experto en el sector; lo más normal es que haga las cosas como siempre se han hecho.
fullContext: Lenny asks Keith how he's able to credibly lead teams in areas where he lacks expertise. Keith explains Tony Xu's philosophy from the book "Range" about why generalists can be better than specialists. He describes how Tony deliberately puts people in roles outside their expertise area because domain experts tend to stick to conventional approaches, while outsiders are more likely to completely reimagine systems and achieve breakthrough results.

vocabulary.definition: To successfully reach a desired objective or result through effort or skill.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'achieve' often refers to meeting specific goals, such as sales targets, project milestones, or performance metrics.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting accomplishment and success, and is often used in motivational contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A person with extensive knowledge or skill in a particular area or field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, hiring an expert is often seen as a strategy to gain insights and improve performance in specialized areas.

insight.nuance: While 'expert' implies a high level of competence, it can also suggest rigidity in thinking, as experts may adhere closely to established practices.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: And I think it's a big part of our success, is this desire to be successful, regardless of who's in charge. And that comes from the fact when I joined DoorDash, we were getting our tails kicked. We were in fourth place in the space.
keySentence: Our success stems from the desire to succeed despite getting our tails kicked.
text_ko: 그리고 저는 누가 책임자든 상관없이 성공하려는 그 마음가짐이 우리 성공의 큰 부분이라고 생각해요. 그건 제가 DoorDash에 합류했을 때 우리가 엄청 고전하고 있었던 경험에서 온 거예요. 그때 우리는 그 분야에서 4위였어요.
text_zh: 我觉得这是我们成功的一个重要原因：大家都有那股想成功的劲儿，不管谁当家。因为我加入 DoorDash 的时候，我们当时被打得很惨，在这条赛道上只排第四。
text_es: Y creo que gran parte de nuestro éxito se debe a ese deseo de triunfar, sin importar quién esté a cargo. Y eso viene de que cuando me uní a DoorDash nos estaban ganando por goleada; estábamos en cuarto lugar en ese mercado.
fullContext: Keith discusses his philosophy of hiring people better than himself and then getting out of their way as they succeed. He explains how this collaborative mindset became part of DoorDash's DNA because when he joined, the company was struggling badly - they were in fourth place in food delivery and Uber had just entered the market and quickly gained leadership position.

vocabulary.definition: Success is the achievement of a desired aim, goal, or purpose, often measured by the attainment of financial, operational, or personal milestones.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, success can be quantified through metrics such as revenue growth, market share, and customer satisfaction, and is a primary objective for organizations.

insight.nuance: While 'success' generally connotes positive outcomes, it can also imply pressure to maintain or exceed previous achievements, making it a complex and sometimes subjective term.

vocabulary.definition: Regardless means without paying attention to the present situation; it indicates a lack of concern for certain factors or conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'regardless' is often used to emphasize commitment to goals or actions despite challenges or changes in leadership or circumstances.

insight.nuance: This term can carry a tone of determination, but it may also suggest a disregard for important details, so it should be used carefully to avoid appearing dismissive.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: And so one thing I noticed is, it's hard to come into a place and be new and understand how things work and what it means to be successful there. And so the idea was to do our best to scale that.
keySentence: it's hard to come into a place and be new and understand how things work and what it means to be successful there.
text_ko: 제가 하나 느낀 건, 새로운 곳에 들어가 신입으로서 그 조직이 어떻게 돌아가는지, 거기서 성공하려면 무엇이 필요한지 이해하기가 참 어렵다는 점이에요. 그래서 그걸 최대한 확장(scale)할 수 있도록 최선을 다하자는 생각이었어요.
text_zh: 我发现一件事：刚到一个地方当新人的时候，很难弄清楚这里怎么运作、什么才算是成功。我们的想法就是尽力把这些做法规模化（scale），让更多人能更快上手。
text_es: Me di cuenta de que es difícil llegar a un sitio siendo nuevo y entender cómo funcionan las cosas y qué significa tener éxito allí. Por eso quisimos hacer todo lo posible para escalar eso (scale).
fullContext: Lenny asks Keith about his "How to work with Keith" document that he created for his teams. Keith explains that as DoorDash was growing rapidly (2-3x headcount each year), it became difficult to scale culture and help new employees understand how to be successful. Tony Xu taught him that written documentation is one of the most effective ways to scale knowledge and culture across a fast-growing organization.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, amount, or capacity in a systematic way, often in relation to business operations or production.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, scaling refers to the ability of a company to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance or losing revenue potential.

insight.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it can also suggest the need for efficiency and sustainability in operations.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something; to comprehend.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding is crucial for effective communication, decision-making, and strategic planning.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a deeper level of insight beyond surface-level knowledge, often requiring analysis and experience.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity; marked by favorable outcomes or accomplishments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, success is often measured by profitability, market share, and the achievement of strategic goals.

insight.nuance: The term can carry subjective meanings depending on individual or organizational goals, and what constitutes success can vary widely.

speaker: Keith Yandell
text: And so now if I get a blind reference, people are going to hear that, "It's not all about the company. It's not all about Keith. It's about you and your career," and that's going to pay back 10x.
keySentence: A blind reference emphasizes it's about your career, paying back 10x.
text_ko: 그러면 이제 제가 블라인드 레퍼런스(blind reference)를 받으면 사람들은 "이건 회사 이야기만 하는 게 아니고, 키스(Keith) 이야기만 하는 것도 아니에요. 당신과 당신의 커리어(career)를 위한 거예요."라고 들을 거고, 그게 10배로 돌아올 거예요.
text_zh: 所以现在，如果有人给我做盲推荐（blind reference），别人会听到我说：“这不全是为了公司，也不全是为了Keith，而是为了你和你的职业发展”，这会带来十倍回报（10x）。
text_es: Así que ahora, si recibo una referencia a ciegas (blind reference), la gente va a escuchar: "No se trata solo de la empresa. No se trata solo de Keith. Se trata de ti y de tu carrera", y eso va a dar un retorno diez veces mayor.
fullContext: Keith explains his philosophy of helping employees find their next job, even if it's outside DoorDash. He describes the long-term benefits of this approach - when people do reference checks on him as a manager, they hear that he puts employees' career interests first. This reputation pays dividends in attracting talent, even if it occasionally means losing someone who would have left eventually anyway.

vocabulary.definition: To return money that was borrowed or to compensate someone for a favor or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'pay back' can refer to the return on investment (ROI) that a company expects from a project or initiative, indicating the financial benefits gained over time.

insight.nuance: While often used in a financial context, 'pay back' can also imply a moral obligation to reciprocate support or assistance.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: Part of what I think is pretty exciting about product management is you are a leader from day one in product management. There's leadership all over the place, but that's your job. You're a leader. You don't have any formal authority, but you're a leader.
keySentence: You're a leader without formal authority in product management.
text_ko: 제가 생각하기에 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management)의 흥미로운 부분 중 하나는 시작하는 날부터 리더라는 점이에요. 리더십이 조직 곳곳에 있긴 하지만, 그게 바로 당신의 일이에요. 정식 권한(formal authority)은 없을 수 있어도, 그래도 리더예요.
text_zh: 我觉得产品管理（product management）最吸引人的地方之一，就是从第一天起你就是个领导。到处都要体现领导力，而这正是你的工作——你就是领导。虽然你没有正式的权力（formal authority），但你依然要去带头。
text_es: Una de las cosas que me parece más emocionante de la gestión de producto (product management) es que, desde el primer día, eres líder. El liderazgo está presente en todas partes, y ese es precisamente tu trabajo: liderar. No tienes autoridad formal, pero aun así eres líder.
fullContext: This quote appears at the very beginning of the episode as Ken introduces the foundational challenge of product management. Ken is establishing the core tension that product managers face throughout their careers - they must lead and influence without traditional hierarchical power. This sets up one of his key themes about why product management is such excellent training for executive leadership roles.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to guide, influence, or direct individuals or teams towards achieving goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, leadership is crucial for driving innovation, fostering collaboration, and navigating challenges within teams and projects.

insight.nuance: While often associated with formal titles, true leadership can also emerge from informal roles where influence and vision are key.

vocabulary.definition: The legitimate power granted to an individual or position within an organization to make decisions and enforce rules.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate structures, formal authority is typically associated with managerial roles that have defined responsibilities and decision-making capabilities.

insight.nuance: While formal authority can enhance a leader's ability to effect change, it is not always necessary for effective leadership, especially in collaborative environments.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: I started to simultaneously recognize the shortcomings of giving advice, because it seemed like, well, I can meet with these folks, I could tell them what I did, I could tell them what Google did, and that'll answer all their questions.
keySentence: I started to simultaneously recognize the shortcomings of giving advice.
text_ko: 저는 동시에 조언을 해주는 것의 한계도 느끼기 시작했어요. 왜냐하면 제가 이분들을 만나 제가 했던 일이나 구글이 했던 일을 말해주면 그분들의 모든 질문이 해결될 것처럼 보였거든요.
text_zh: 我也开始意识到，光给建议其实有不少问题。表面上看，好像只要我跟这些人见个面，跟他们说说我当时怎么做的，或者告诉他们Google怎么做的，就能回答他们所有的问题。
text_es: Al mismo tiempo me fui dando cuenta de que dar consejos tiene sus límites, porque parecía que, bueno, podía reunirme con estas personas, contarles lo que yo hice, explicarles lo que hizo Google, y con eso se resolvían todas sus dudas.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ken how he transitioned from being a Google executive to becoming a full-time executive coach. Ken explains his realization while working at Google Ventures that traditional advice-giving has significant limitations. He discovered that simply telling portfolio founders what worked at Google wasn't effective because it lacked context for their specific situations, leading him to discover the power of coaching over mentoring.

vocabulary.definition: Deficiencies or failures to meet a certain standard or expectation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, shortcomings may refer to gaps in a product, service, or strategy that hinder performance or customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a need for improvement or acknowledgment of limitations, making it important to use in constructive criticism.

vocabulary.definition: Occurring at the same time; concurrently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, tasks or processes may need to be executed simultaneously to enhance efficiency and meet deadlines.

insight.nuance: While it suggests coordination, it can also imply complexity, so it should be used carefully in contexts where multitasking is involved.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: There's a sense of what got me here isn't going to get me there. That's oftentimes when they reach out for coaching.
keySentence: What got me here isn't going to get me there; internal work is essential.
text_ko: 지금까지 저를 여기까지 이끌어준 방식으로는 앞으로 원하는 곳까지는 못 가겠다는 느낌이 들어요. 많은 분들이 바로 그때 코칭(coaching)을 찾으세요.
text_zh: 会有一种感觉：把我带到现在的那些做法，帮不上忙让我走到下一步。很多时候就是在这种情况下，他们会去找教练(coaching)求助。
text_es: Cuando sienten que lo que les trajo hasta aquí no les va a llevar a donde quieren llegar, muchas veces recurren al asesoramiento (coaching).
fullContext: Lenny asks Ken what types of clients he works with and when people typically come to him for coaching. Ken explains that his clients are usually senior product leaders (CPOs, VPs of product) who are facing career milestones or transitions. These leaders have already mastered the technical aspects of their roles but recognize they need to do deeper personal development work to reach the next level of effectiveness.

vocabulary.definition: To make contact with someone, typically for the purpose of seeking assistance or establishing a connection.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'reaching out' often refers to initiating communication with colleagues, clients, or mentors to solicit advice, support, or collaboration.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of initiative and openness, often used in networking or when seeking guidance, but may be perceived as informal in more traditional corporate environments.

vocabulary.definition: A process of guiding individuals or teams to improve their performance and achieve specific goals through feedback and support.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, coaching is utilized to enhance employee skills, foster leadership development, and facilitate personal growth within organizations.

insight.nuance: Coaching implies a collaborative relationship focused on development rather than mere instruction, and is often preferred over terms like 'training' when emphasizing personal empowerment.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: But then suddenly you're put in a place where you realize that the rules of the game aren't so black and white. Maybe there's a long delay now between when you get to see what you did and the score of it.
keySentence: The rules of the game aren't black and white; expect long delays and surprises.
text_ko: 그런데 어느 순간 갑자기 게임의 룰(rules of the game)이 그렇게 흑백이 아니라는 걸 깨닫게 돼요. 이제는 내가 뭘 했는지와 그게 어떻게 평가되는지 사이에 꽤 긴 시차가 있을 수도 있어요.
text_zh: 但突然你会发现自己处在一种境地：游戏规则并不像想象中那样黑白分明。也许从你做了某件事到看到它的评分(score)，现在会有很长的延迟。
text_es: Pero de repente te encuentras en una situación en la que te das cuenta de que las reglas del juego no son tan blanco y negro. Puede que ahora pase mucho tiempo entre el momento en que ves lo que hiciste y la valoración (score) que recibes.
fullContext: Ken is using a video game analogy to explain the transition from individual contributor to senior leader. He describes how early career feels like learning to play a structured game with clear rules and immediate feedback, but senior leadership roles are much more ambiguous. The transition is jarring because suddenly others expect you to set the rules rather than just follow them, which requires a fundamental mindset shift.

vocabulary.definition: A phrase used to describe a situation that is clear-cut or straightforward, with no ambiguity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'black and white' often refers to policies or decisions that are clear and unambiguous, making it easier for stakeholders to understand expectations.

insight.nuance: While it suggests clarity, it can also imply a lack of flexibility or consideration for complex situations.

vocabulary.definition: To become fully aware of something as a fact; to understand or grasp the significance of an idea or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'realize' often refers to the moment when stakeholders understand the implications of data or decisions, which can lead to strategic pivots or innovations.

insight.nuance: It conveys a sense of awakening or enlightenment, often after a period of confusion or oversight.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: Are you responding to the world from a place of fear... or are you responding to the world from a place of openness, possibility, curiosity, passion, growth, purpose?
keySentence: Responding from a place of fear limits growth; choose a place of openness instead.
text_ko: 세상에 반응할 때 두려움에서 반응하고 있어요... 아니면 열린 마음, 가능성, 호기심, 열정, 성장, 목적 같은 마음가짐으로 반응하고 있어요?
text_zh: 你对这个世界的反应，是被恐惧左右，还是以开放的心态、看到可能性、保持好奇、充满热情、追求成长、并带着使命感去回应？
text_es: ¿Respondes al mundo desde un lugar de miedo... o desde un lugar de apertura, posibilidad, curiosidad, pasión, crecimiento y propósito?
fullContext: Lenny asks Ken about a key concept he's been developing around leadership mindset shifts. Ken explains his framework of 'creative versus reactive' leadership, which distinguishes between two fundamental ways leaders can approach challenges. This framework, adapted from various leadership theories, identifies whether leaders operate from fear and defensiveness (reactive) or from openness and possibility (creative).

vocabulary.definition: Possibility refers to the potential for something to happen or be achieved; it embodies the idea of opportunity and potential outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, possibility is often associated with innovation and the exploration of new markets, where entrepreneurs assess various scenarios for growth and success.

insight.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting optimism and openness to new ideas, but can also imply uncertainty when discussing risks.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: For me, the key to that was letting go of needing to be liked and redefining it as an admiration that takes place over time.
keySentence: Letting go of needing to be liked redefines leadership as admiration over time.
text_ko: 저에게 그 핵심은 '좋아해 달라'는 욕구를 내려놓고, 그걸 시간이 지나면서 생기는 존경으로 재정의한 거예요.
text_zh: 对我来说，关键是别再执着于一定要被别人喜欢，而把这事看成是会随着时间慢慢累积起来的欣赏。
text_es: Para mí, la clave fue dejar de necesitar que me acepten y verlo como una admiración que se gana con el tiempo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ken for specific advice on how to shift from the reactive 'need to be liked' mindset to a more creative leadership approach. Ken shares his personal transformation from seeking immediate approval to focusing on long-term respect and admiration. This represents his shift from reactive leadership (needing instant validation) to creative leadership (operating from purpose and long-term vision).

vocabulary.definition: To change the meaning or interpretation of something, often to suit new circumstances or perspectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, redefining can refer to altering a company's mission, vision, or strategies to better align with market demands or internal values.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a significant shift in understanding or approach, and should be used when discussing substantial changes rather than minor adjustments.

speaker: Ken Norton
text: I think probably the number one category, I'm not sure it's necessarily a problem, but maybe category or problems, is how much all of the challenges that senior executives are dealing with come down to people versus product.
keySentence: Challenges for executives come down to people, not just product.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 아마 가장 큰 카테고리(꼭 문제라고만 하긴 어렵지만)는 고위 경영진들(senior executives)이 겪는 거의 모든 과제가 결국 사람 문제냐 제품 문제냐로 귀결된다는 점인 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得首要的一类——我不确定这一定能算是个“问题”，也许更像一种分类——就是高管 (senior executives) 面临的很多挑战，很多都归结到“人”还是“产品 (product)”的问题上。
text_es: Creo que la categoría número uno —y no estoy seguro de que sea necesariamente un problema, quizá más bien una categoría de problemas— es hasta qué punto todos los retos que enfrentan los altos directivos se reducen a personas frente a producto.
fullContext: Lenny asks Ken about the most common blind spots he sees in product leaders. Ken identifies that senior product executives often underestimate how much of their role becomes about managing people rather than managing products. While early-career product managers focus on user research, optimization, and product features, senior leaders spend most of their time on persuasion, team dynamics, and organizational challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulties or obstacles that require a solution or response.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, challenges often refer to issues that organizations face in achieving their goals, such as market competition, resource limitations, or internal conflicts.

insight.nuance: While challenges can imply a negative situation, they also suggest opportunities for growth and improvement when addressed effectively.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals in senior management positions responsible for making strategic decisions and overseeing the operations of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: Executives play a crucial role in shaping company policies, driving business strategies, and leading teams to achieve organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: The term often connotes authority and high-level responsibility, distinguishing these individuals from lower-level managers or staff.

speaker: Kenneth Berger
text: If you're more in the people pleasing camp, maybe you're used to not asking at all. You're hoping that people are reading your mind.
keySentence: People pleasing often leads to hoping others are reading your mind.
text_ko: 사람들 맞춰주기 성향(people-pleasing)이라면, 아예 요청을 안 하는 게 익숙할 수도 있어요. 사람들이 제 마음을 읽어주길 바라고 있죠.
text_zh: 如果你比较倾向于讨好别人，可能已经习惯不主动提要求，指望别人能看懂你的心思。
text_es: Si tiendes más a complacer a los demás, quizá estés acostumbrado a no pedir nada y a quedarte esperando que la gente lea tu mente.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kenneth how people can know if they need to work on asking for what they want. Kenneth explains that there are two common problematic approaches people take when they struggle with this skill. He identifies that people typically fall into one of two camps when it comes to making requests - either they avoid asking entirely and expect others to intuitively understand their needs, or they become overly controlling and demanding in their communication style.

vocabulary.definition: The tendency to prioritize the approval and satisfaction of others over one's own needs or desires.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, people pleasing can lead to a reluctance to voice opinions or make decisions that may upset colleagues, potentially hindering effective teamwork and leadership.

insight.nuance: While people pleasing can foster harmony, it may also result in personal burnout and a lack of authenticity in professional relationships.

vocabulary.definition: The act of requesting information, assistance, or clarification from others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, asking is crucial for effective communication, collaboration, and problem-solving, as it encourages transparency and shared understanding.

insight.nuance: While asking can demonstrate vulnerability, it can also be perceived as a strength when it leads to informed decision-making and team cohesion.

speaker: Kenneth Berger
text: Complaints are great inspiration. Every complaint implies a dream. Let me envision a better future. Let me think about what's an effective way to actually move towards that. See what it's like to not be sort of living in fear all the time.
keySentence: Complaints are great inspiration, implying a dream for a better future.
text_ko: 불만은 훌륭한 영감이에요. 모든 불만에는 더 나은 무언가를 바라는 꿈이 담겨 있어요. 제가 더 나은 미래를 상상하게 해줘요. 그리고 그걸 실제로 향해 나아가게 할 효과적인 방법이 무엇인지 생각하게 해줘요. 늘 두려움에 사로잡혀 살지 않는 삶이 어떤지 느껴보게 해줘요.
text_zh: 客户抱怨其实是很好的灵感来源。每一个抱怨背后都藏着一个期待，让我去想象一个更好的未来。让我想想怎么才能真正有效地朝那个方向努力。看看不用总是提心吊胆过日子是什么感觉。
text_es: Las quejas son una inspiración increíble. Cada queja esconde un sueño. Déjame imaginar un futuro mejor. Déjame pensar en cuál sería una manera efectiva de realmente avanzar hacia eso. Ver cómo sería no estar viviendo con miedo todo el tiempo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kenneth how people can figure out what they want in their lives and careers, especially for those who struggle with knowing their own desires. Kenneth introduces a technique he calls "dream behind the complaint" - the idea that people are often better at complaining than dreaming, but every complaint contains valuable information about what they actually want. He suggests using complaints as starting points to envision better futures and develop effective strategies to achieve them.

vocabulary.definition: The process of being mentally stimulated to do or feel something, especially to do something creative or innovative.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, inspiration often drives innovation and motivates teams to pursue new ideas or solutions to problems.

insight.nuance: While inspiration can be a powerful motivator, it is often fleeting and should be complemented by strategic planning and execution.

vocabulary.definition: Successful in producing a desired or intended result; capable of achieving goals efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, effective strategies and practices are essential for maximizing productivity and achieving organizational objectives.

insight.nuance: The term 'effective' implies not only achieving results but doing so in a manner that is appropriate and sustainable over time.

vocabulary.definition: To imagine or visualize a future possibility or scenario, often in a detailed and vivid manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: Leaders in business often need to envision future trends and opportunities to guide strategic planning and decision-making.

insight.nuance: Envisioning goes beyond mere dreaming; it involves a clear mental picture that can inspire actionable plans.

speaker: Kenneth Berger
text: it's fundamentally disrespectful to go into a meeting already deciding that you're right and the other person is wrong because you can't know that for sure.
keySentence: It's fundamentally disrespectful to assume you're right without knowing for sure.
text_ko: 회의에 들어갈 때 이미 내가 옳고 상대방이 틀리다고 단정하고 가는 건 근본적으로 무례해요. 확실히 알 수 없거든요.
text_zh: 开会前就认定自己对、别人错，这很不尊重对方——你没法那么肯定。
text_es: Es una falta de respeto entrar a una reunión ya convencido de que tienes la razón y la otra persona está equivocada, porque no puedes saberlo con certeza.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kenneth for an example from his own career where he failed to ask for what he wanted effectively. Kenneth reflects on his tendency to be overly attached to being right, particularly in his product management role. He explains how this mindset of entering conversations with predetermined conclusions about being correct is not only ineffective but also disrespectful to others, as it prevents genuine dialogue and learning from new information.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic and essential way; at the core or foundation of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'fundamentally' is often used to highlight core principles or values that underpin strategic decisions or organizational culture.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a sense of importance and can imply that the issue at hand is not just superficial but deeply rooted.

vocabulary.definition: Showing a lack of respect or consideration for someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, being 'disrespectful' can damage relationships, hinder collaboration, and create a toxic workplace culture, particularly during negotiations or meetings.

insight.nuance: This term carries a strong negative connotation and is often used to describe behavior that undermines professional decorum.

speaker: Kenneth Berger
text: So one of my favorite techniques here is this concept they call dream behind the complaint.
keySentence: this concept they call dream behind the complaint.
text_ko: 여기서 제가 가장 좋아하는 기법 중 하나는 사람들이 '불만 뒤에 숨은 꿈(dream behind the complaint)'이라고 부르는 개념이에요.
text_zh: 我最喜欢的技巧之一，就是所谓的“抱怨背后的真实诉求”(dream behind the complaint)。
text_es: Una de las técnicas que más me gusta usar aquí es explorar la motivación detrás de la queja (dream behind the complaint).
fullContext: Lenny asks Kenneth for specific techniques to help people identify what they want, particularly those who struggle with articulating their desires or tend to prioritize others' happiness over their own needs. Kenneth introduces his "dream behind the complaint" technique, explaining that while people often find it intimidating to articulate big dreams or visions, they're naturally skilled at identifying problems and frustrations. He suggests using complaints as a practical starting point for discovering underlying desires.

vocabulary.definition: Methods or ways of doing something, often based on practical skills or knowledge.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, techniques can refer to specific strategies or practices used to improve processes, enhance productivity, or solve problems.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a level of expertise and can imply that the methods are tried and tested, although they may vary in effectiveness depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: An abstract idea or a general notion that represents something, often used as a foundation for further development or discussion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a concept can refer to a new product idea, a marketing strategy, or a business model that is being developed or evaluated.

insight.nuance: While 'concept' suggests a foundational idea, it may also imply that the idea is still in the early stages of development and not yet fully realized.

speaker: Kenneth Berger
text: So I have a more expansive definition of no than most people, I think, because for me it's not a yes unless it's a hell yes. Because you really want enthusiastic consent. Not just, "Maybe, kinda. I'll try. We'll see.
keySentence: I have a more expansive definition of no; it's not a yes unless it's a hell yes.
text_ko: 저는 '아니오'를 대부분 사람들보다 좀 더 넓게 해석하는 편이에요. 저한테는 '네'라고 하기 위해선 정말 확실한, 완전한 '네'여야 해요. 진짜로는 적극적인 동의(enthusiastic consent)를 원하거든요. 그냥 "음… 아마도, 좀… 해볼게요. 두고 보죠" 같은 애매한 반응이면 안 돼요.
text_zh: 我觉得我比大多数人更会把很多情况当成“不要”。对我来说，除非是那种特别想做、毫不犹豫的“要”，否则就算是“不要”。因为你真正需要的是热情的同意(enthusiastic consent)，不是那种“也许吧、有点儿、我试试、到时候再说”。
text_es: Creo que mi definición de "no" es más amplia que la de la mayoría: para mí no vale como sí a menos que sea un "sí" rotundo. Lo ideal es obtener consentimiento entusiasta, no un "bueno, quizá, lo intento, ya veremos".
fullContext: Lenny asks Kenneth about overcoming the fear of hearing "no" when asking for what you want. Kenneth explains his philosophy around accepting responses, particularly his belief that anything short of enthusiastic agreement should be treated as a "no." He emphasizes the importance of seeking genuine, wholehearted commitment rather than settling for lukewarm or hesitant responses, as these often lead to problems later when people don't fully follow through on their commitments.

vocabulary.definition: Enthusiastic consent refers to a clear and affirmative agreement to participate in an activity, characterized by eagerness and willingness rather than mere acceptance or compliance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business negotiations or partnerships, enthusiastic consent ensures that all parties are fully committed and engaged, fostering a more productive and collaborative environment.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of genuine interest and agreement, distinguishing it from passive or reluctant consent.

vocabulary.definition: An expansive definition is a broad interpretation of a term or concept that encompasses a wide range of meanings or applications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In strategic planning or product development, an expansive definition can encourage innovative thinking by allowing for diverse perspectives and potential uses.

insight.nuance: While useful for fostering creativity, an overly expansive definition can lead to ambiguity and confusion if not clearly communicated.

speaker: Kenneth Berger
text: Part of really respecting them is respecting that they can make the choices they want and they're grownups enough that they can deal with the consequences of those choices.
keySentence: Respecting them means acknowledging they are grownups enough to deal with consequences.
text_ko: 진정으로 그들을 존중한다는 건, 그들이 자기 원하는 선택을 할 권리가 있고 그 선택의 결과를 스스로 감당할 수 있는 어른이라는 걸 인정해 주는 것도 포함돼요.
text_zh: 真正尊重他们，就是要相信他们有能力做自己想做的决定，而且他们都是成年人了，完全可以为自己的选择负责。
text_es: Parte de respetarlos de verdad es entender que pueden tomar sus propias decisiones y que son lo suficientemente adultos como para asumir las consecuencias de esas decisiones.
fullContext: Kenneth discusses a common challenge he sees with "nice" founders who struggle to deliver difficult feedback or create consequences when team members aren't meeting expectations. He's explaining how these leaders often avoid creating accountability because they want to be liked and seen as kind. Kenneth argues that truly respecting people means acknowledging their autonomy to make decisions while also maintaining appropriate professional consequences for those choices.

vocabulary.definition: Consequences are the outcomes or effects that result from a particular action or decision. They can be positive or negative and often influence future choices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding the consequences of decisions is crucial for risk management and strategic planning, as it helps organizations anticipate potential challenges and opportunities.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a weighty implication, suggesting that the outcomes are significant and should be carefully considered before taking action.

vocabulary.definition: Respecting involves acknowledging the rights, feelings, and opinions of others, often resulting in a considerate and professional interaction. It fosters trust and collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, respecting colleagues' autonomy and decisions is essential for a positive culture, as it encourages open communication and empowers employees.

insight.nuance: While respecting is generally viewed positively, it must be balanced with accountability to ensure that decisions align with organizational goals.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: I am kind of annoyed at how much it's being mentioned these days.
keySentence: I am kind of annoyed at how much it's being mentioned these days.
text_ko: 요즘 이 얘기가 너무 많이 언급돼서 좀 짜증나요.
text_zh: 我有点烦，最近大家老提这事儿。
text_es: Me molesta un poco lo mucho que se habla de esto últimamente.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about his thoughts on super apps, given that many US companies like Uber and Twitter are trying to become super apps. Kevin explains his mixed views on the super app strategy, arguing that while super apps sound appealing to VCs and analysts because they promise benefits like lower customer acquisition costs and higher retention, these theoretical advantages often don't materialize in practice.

vocabulary.definition: To refer to something briefly and without elaboration, often in a conversation or written context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, something that is mentioned may require follow-up or further discussion, especially if it pertains to important issues or decisions.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a lack of depth in discussion, suggesting that the topic may need more attention or detail.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling irritated or displeased, often due to a repeated action or situation that is bothersome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a professional setting, being annoyed can affect teamwork and communication, making it important to address grievances constructively.

insight.nuance: While 'annoyed' conveys a sense of irritation, it may also indicate a need for change or improvement in a situation, and should be used carefully to maintain professionalism.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: And so I think this kind of illustrates the importance of having these unifying concepts that are easy for customers to think about the multiple different services.
keySentence: Unifying concepts help customers understand multiple services better.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 이게 고객들이 여러 가지 서비스를 떠올릴 때 이해하기 쉬운 통합 개념(unifying concepts)을 갖는 게 얼마나 중요한지를 잘 보여준다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 我觉得这在某种程度上说明了，拥有能把不同服务串在一起、让客户容易理解的统一概念有多重要。
text_es: Creo que esto ilustra la importancia de contar con conceptos que unifiquen y que a los clientes les resulten fáciles a la hora de entender los distintos servicios.
fullContext: Lenny is asking Kevin to elaborate on why super apps don't work as well as expected. Kevin is explaining that customers need a mental framework to understand why different services belong together in one app. He uses examples from Gojek where services connected to drivers made sense to customers (ride-hailing, food delivery, package delivery), but other services like mobile top-ups didn't because they lacked this unifying concept.

vocabulary.definition: Broad ideas or themes that bring together various elements or components into a cohesive understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, unifying concepts help streamline communication and decision-making by providing a common framework for discussing complex products or services.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a simplification of complex ideas, making them more accessible to stakeholders; however, it should be used carefully to avoid oversimplification.

vocabulary.definition: Demonstrates or highlights the significance or value of a particular idea or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In presentations and reports, illustrating the importance of certain strategies or practices can persuade stakeholders to prioritize them in decision-making.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of urgency or necessity; it should be used when the implications of the idea are critical to understanding the overall context.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: But I wish I did have to start there because we actually started as a very scrappy company where we were by far the underfunded player and without brand.
keySentence: We were by far the underfunded player before achieving escape velocity.
text_ko: 근데 솔직히 저는 거기서부터 시작했어야 했을 텐데요. 저희는 처음에 정말 열악하게 시작한 회사였어요. 자금도 단연 부족했고 브랜드도 전혀 없었거든요.
text_zh: 但我倒希望自己当时真得从那儿开始，因为我们其实一开始就是很草根、资金极其有限、没有品牌影响力的公司。
text_es: Ojalá hubiera tenido que empezar por ahí, porque en realidad empezamos como una compañía muy austera: éramos, con mucha diferencia, los menos financiados y no teníamos marca.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about the importance of brand for startups and how to prioritize it. Kevin explains that while he opened by discussing Gojek's massive scale, he actually prefers to emphasize how they started as an extremely underfunded company. He argues that brand was crucial to their survival and growth, allowing them to compete against much better-funded competitors who had raised over 100 times more capital than Gojek in the early days.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by a resourceful and determined attitude, often in the face of adversity or limited resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a 'scrappy' company often refers to startups that operate with minimal resources, relying on creativity and hard work to achieve their goals.

insight.nuance: While 'scrappy' conveys a positive connotation of resilience, it can also imply a lack of polish or sophistication.

vocabulary.definition: Having insufficient financial resources to support operations, projects, or growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, being 'underfunded' can hinder a company's ability to scale, innovate, or compete effectively in the market.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that a company is at a disadvantage compared to better-funded competitors.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: And so we would have these actual physical locations where there would be lions of drivers essentially taking cash. And we eventually figured this out of like, okay, we'll work with a bank and integrate with an ATM network and all that.
keySentence: we'll work with a bank and integrate with an ATM network
text_ko: 그래서 실제 오프라인 장소들이 있었는데, 거기엔 운전기사들이 현금을 받으려고 길게 줄 서 있곤 했어요. 결국엔 은행하고 협력해서 ATM 네트워크(ATM network)에 연동하기로 했어요.
text_zh: 于是我们在线下的一些点，会有一大群司机基本上当场收现金。后来我们想通了：跟银行合作，把ATM网络(ATM network)接入进来之类的。
text_es: Teníamos ubicaciones físicas donde se formaban largas colas de conductores que, básicamente, recibían pagos en efectivo. Al final lo resolvimos pensando: bueno, trabajaremos con un banco y nos integraremos con la red de cajeros automáticos (ATM) y cosas por el estilo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin for stories about how scrappy Gojek was in the early days. Kevin explains one of their biggest challenges: paying drivers when digital payments didn't exist in Indonesia. Since drivers needed to convert their digital earnings to physical cash, Gojek created physical cash distribution centers with vaults where drivers could line up to withdraw their money, essentially building their own primitive ATM network before proper banking integration was available.

vocabulary.definition: To combine or coordinate different components into a unified whole.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, integration often refers to the process of linking various systems or processes to enhance efficiency and functionality.

insight.nuance: While 'integrate' implies a harmonious combination, it can also suggest the complexity of merging differing systems or cultures.

vocabulary.definition: A group or system of interconnected people or things, often used to facilitate communication and collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, networking can refer to both the physical infrastructure that supports data exchange and the social connections that enable professional relationships.

insight.nuance: The term can imply both a technical setup (like a computer network) and a social aspect (like networking events), depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: Specific, tangible places where activities or operations occur, as opposed to virtual or online spaces.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, physical locations are crucial for operations, customer interactions, and logistical considerations, especially in retail and service industries.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the importance of a geographical presence, which can be a strategic advantage or a limitation depending on the business model.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: I really don't like the idea of moats. Again, one of the concepts that gets thrown out a lot by strategy type folks of what's the moat of your business or your product?
keySentence: I really don't like the idea of moats.
text_ko: 저는 해자(moat)라는 개념 자체를 정말 안 좋아해요. 전략 쪽 사람들이 '너희 사업이나 제품의 해자(moat)가 뭐예요?' 하고 자주 던지는 질문 중 하나예요.
text_zh: 我其实不太认同“护城河（moat）”这套说法。做战略的人老爱抛出这种问题：你的业务或产品有什么护城河？
text_es: La verdad no me gusta la idea de los fosos (moats). Es uno de esos conceptos que la gente de estrategia menciona mucho: «¿cuál es el foso de tu negocio o de tu producto?»
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about Gojek's philosophy of doing hard things instead of taking the easy path that most startups prefer. Kevin explains his contrarian view on competitive moats - the business advantages that supposedly protect companies from competition. He argues that traditional moats like special features or distribution partnerships aren't sustainable because competitors can eventually replicate them, but doing genuinely difficult things creates a more durable advantage.

vocabulary.definition: Strategy is a plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, particularly in a competitive context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, strategy encompasses the decisions and actions taken to position a company effectively in the market and achieve its objectives.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a level of foresight and adaptability, as effective strategies often require ongoing evaluation and adjustment based on market conditions.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: And so we actually ran a fairly big private security operation for a fairly long time until it became common to have Gojek drivers do all of these things across cities.
keySentence: we actually ran a fairly big private security operation for a fairly long time
text_ko: 그래서 사실 도시 전역에서 Gojek 기사들이 이런 일들을 다 하게 되는 게 일반화될 때까지, 저희는 꽤 오랜 기간 상당히 큰 규모의 사설 보안 운영(private security operation)을 했어요.
text_zh: 所以我们当时确实在运营一个规模不小、持续很久的私人安保项目 (private security operation)，直到这些工作在各城市逐渐由Gojek司机 (Gojek drivers) 来承担为止。
text_es: Así que, en realidad, llevamos una operación de seguridad privada bastante grande durante mucho tiempo, hasta que se volvió habitual que los conductores de Gojek se encargaran de todo eso en distintas ciudades.
fullContext: Lenny is asking Kevin for more examples of Gojek doing hard things. Kevin describes how Gojek drivers faced violent resistance from motorcycle taxi mafia who controlled certain areas through intimidation and physical assault. Instead of treating drivers as independent contractors and leaving them to handle the violence alone, Gojek hired private security companies to protect their drivers and extract them from dangerous situations, demonstrating their commitment to driver safety.

vocabulary.definition: A coordinated series of activities or tasks aimed at achieving a specific goal or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'operation' often refers to the processes and activities that a company undertakes to deliver its products or services efficiently.

insight.nuance: While 'operation' can refer to any activity, in a business context it often implies a level of complexity and organization.

vocabulary.definition: Occurring frequently or widely; shared by many people or entities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, 'common' can describe practices, tools, or features that are widely adopted across various companies or platforms.

insight.nuance: While 'common' indicates frequency, it can also imply a lack of uniqueness or innovation.

speaker: Kevin Aluwi
text: And so a lot of times I felt like I needed to understand, okay, what is this job? What exactly does it entail is, and seeing how bad I am at it allowed me to understand what good looked like.
keySentence: seeing how bad I am at it allowed me to understand what good looked like.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 종종 이 일이 도대체 뭔지, 정확히 어떤 일을 하는지 이해해야겠다고 느꼈어요. 제가 그 일을 얼마나 못하는지를 보면서 오히려 잘하는 모습이 어떤 건지 알게 됐어요.
text_zh: 很多时候我觉得得先弄明白：这份工作到底是什么，具体要做哪些事。看到自己做得这么糟，反而让我更清楚什么才算做得好。
text_es: Así que muchas veces sentía que tenía que entender: ¿qué es exactamente este trabajo, en qué consiste? Ver lo mal que lo hacía me ayudó a hacerme una idea de cómo sería hacerlo bien.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about why he personally held so many different roles at Gojek, from CEO to performance marketer to driver. Kevin explains this wasn't just about being scrappy, but about understanding what excellence looks like in each role. Since experienced talent was scarce in Indonesia's early tech ecosystem, he couldn't easily hire proven professionals, so he first learned the roles himself to understand what good performance looked like before finding people who could do those jobs much better.

vocabulary.definition: To involve or require as a necessary part or consequence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding what a project entails is crucial for effective planning and resource allocation.

insight.nuance: While 'entail' suggests a necessary connection, it can imply complexity or additional responsibilities.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, understanding market trends is essential for strategic decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a deeper comprehension beyond surface-level knowledge.

speaker: Kevin Weil
text: Our general mindset is in two months, there's going to be a better model and it's going to blow away whatever the current set of limitations are. And we say this to developers too.
keySentence: there's going to be a better model and it's going to blow away whatever the current set of limitations are.
text_ko: 저희 일반적인 생각은 두 달만 지나면 더 나은 모델(model)이 나와서 현재의 제약들을 완전히 뛰어넘을 거라는 거예요. 이 얘기는 개발자들(developers)한테도 똑같이 해요.
text_zh: 我们普遍的想法是：两个月内会有更好的模型 (model) 出来，能把现在这些限制都彻底打破。我们也会这么跟开发者 (developers) 说。
text_es: Tendemos a pensar que en dos meses saldrá un modelo (model) mejor que dejará obsoletas las limitaciones actuales. Se lo decimos también a los desarrolladores (developers).
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about what it's like working at the center of the AI revolution at OpenAI. Kevin explains their philosophy of 'model maximalism' - the idea that instead of building extensive workarounds for current model limitations, they focus on the fact that AI models improve dramatically every few months. He's advising both internal teams and external developers to push the boundaries of what's currently possible, knowing that upcoming model improvements will make products that barely work today perform exceptionally well in the near future.

vocabulary.definition: A particular way of thinking or a mental attitude that influences how one perceives and responds to situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a growth mindset encourages innovation and adaptability, essential for navigating challenges and seizing opportunities.

insight.nuance: While 'mindset' generally refers to a person's attitude, it can imply a fixed or flexible approach depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: Restrictions or constraints that hinder progress or performance in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, understanding limitations is crucial for setting realistic goals and developing strategies to overcome obstacles.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting barriers that need to be addressed or mitigated.

vocabulary.definition: A representation or framework that illustrates a concept, system, or process, often used for analysis or simulation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, a business model outlines how a company creates, delivers, and captures value, guiding strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: The term can refer to both theoretical frameworks and practical applications, so context is important to clarify its use.

speaker: Kevin Weil
text: Everywhere I've ever worked before this, you kind of know what technology you're building on, but that's not true at all with AI.
keySentence: you kind of know what technology you're building on, but that's not true at all with AI.
text_ko: 여태까지 일해본 곳들에서는 보통 어떤 기술을 기반으로 하는지 대충 알 수 있었어요. 그런데 인공지능(AI)은 전혀 그렇지 않아요.
text_zh: 在我以前工作的那些地方，通常能大概看出你们是搭在什么技术上的，但在人工智能（AI）这块完全不是这么回事。
text_es: En todos los trabajos anteriores más o menos sabes en qué tecnología te apoyas, pero con la inteligencia artificial (AI) eso no es así en absoluto.
fullContext: Lenny asks what's most different about working at OpenAI compared to Kevin's previous roles at traditional tech companies like Twitter, Instagram, and Facebook. Kevin explains that unlike conventional software development where the underlying technology stack remains relatively stable, AI development is fundamentally different because the core capabilities of the models evolve rapidly. This constant advancement in AI capabilities requires product teams to continuously rethink their approach and strategies.

vocabulary.definition: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry. It encompasses tools, systems, and methods that enhance productivity and efficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, technology is often a key driver of innovation, enabling companies to improve processes, create new products, and gain competitive advantages.

insight.nuance: While 'technology' typically refers to modern innovations, it can also imply a broader range of tools and systems, so context is important to clarify its scope.

vocabulary.definition: To develop or expand upon an existing idea, foundation, or framework, often to enhance or innovate further.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, 'building on' refers to leveraging existing technologies or concepts to create new products or services, fostering growth and evolution.

insight.nuance: This phrase suggests a collaborative or cumulative approach to development, emphasizing the importance of prior work while also indicating potential for further advancement.

speaker: Kevin Weil
text: keep going, because you're doing something right... the models are going to be great, and suddenly the product that you have that just barely worked is really going to sing.
keySentence: Keep going if your product barely worked; models will soon really sing.
text_ko: 계속 밀고 가세요. 지금 하시는 게 맞아요. 모델(models)이 훨씬 좋아질 거고, 어느 순간 겨우 돌아가던 프로덕트(product)가 진짜 빛을 발할 거예요.
text_zh: 坚持下去，你现在做对了。模型(models)会越来越强，那个现在还只是勉强能用的产品，突然就会大放异彩。
text_es: Sigue así, porque estás haciendo algo bien... los modelos (models) van a ser excelentes, y de repente ese producto que apenas funcionaba va a empezar a brillar.
fullContext: Lenny asks about OpenAI's product philosophy and how they approach building products when the underlying AI technology is constantly improving. Kevin is explaining their 'model maximalism' approach - rather than building extensive workarounds for current AI limitations, they advise developers to build products that push current model capabilities to their limits. His point is that products struggling with today's models will excel as the models rapidly improve over the coming months.

speaker: Kevin Weil
text: I think you're definitely going to live in a world where you have researchers built into every product team. And I don't even mean just at foundation model companies because I think the future...
keySentence: you're definitely going to live in a world where you have researchers built into every product team.
text_ko: 앞으로는 분명 모든 제품 팀(product team)에 연구자들이 정규 멤버로 들어가는 세상에서 살게 될 거예요. 그리고 제가 그걸 파운데이션 모델 회사들(foundation model companies)에만 해당된다고 말하는 것도 아니에요. 제 생각엔 미래에는...
text_zh: 我觉得将来你肯定会生活在一个每个产品团队里都配备研究员（researchers）的世界里。我并不是只说那些做基础模型的公司（foundation model companies），因为我觉得未来……
text_es: Creo que, sin duda, vamos a vivir en un mundo en el que cada equipo de producto va a tener investigadores integrados. Y no me refiero solo a las empresas de modelos fundacionales (foundation model companies), porque creo que el futuro...
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about how product teams might change in the future as AI becomes more prevalent. Kevin predicts that product teams across all companies, not just AI companies, will need to include researchers or machine learning engineers. He explains that the future will involve extensive use of fine-tuned models - AI models customized for specific use cases rather than using generic models. This will require teams to have the expertise to adapt and optimize models for their particular product needs.
