vocabulary.definition: A product team is a group of professionals responsible for the development, design, and management of a specific product or product line within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product teams often include roles such as product managers, designers, and engineers who collaborate to bring a product from concept to market.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes collaboration and cross-functional expertise, distinguishing it from other teams that may focus solely on marketing or sales.

vocabulary.definition: A foundation model refers to a large-scale machine learning model that serves as a base for further customization and fine-tuning for specific applications or tasks.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, foundation models are often utilized in artificial intelligence to streamline the development of applications, enabling companies to leverage advanced capabilities without building models from scratch.

insight.nuance: The term implies a robust and versatile model that can be adapted for various uses, highlighting its foundational role in AI development.

vocabulary.definition: Researchers are individuals who conduct systematic investigations to establish facts, gather data, and develop new knowledge in a specific field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of tech and startups, researchers play a critical role in innovation, often working on product development, market analysis, and technological advancements.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of rigor and academic inquiry, and is typically used to refer to individuals with advanced expertise in their field.

speaker: Kevin Weil
text: if you teach your kids to be curious, to be independent, to be self-confident, you teach them how to think... those are going to be skills that are going to be important in any configuration of the future.
keySentence: if you teach your kids to be curious, to be independent, to be self-confident, you teach them how to think
text_ko: 자녀에게 호기심을 갖게 하고, 자립심과 자신감을 길러주면 사고하는 법을 가르치는 거예요. 그런 능력들은 미래가 어떻게 변하든 어디서나 중요해요.
text_zh: 如果你培养孩子的好奇心、独立性和自信，实际上就是在教他们怎么思考——这些能力在任何未来场景下都会很重要。
text_es: Si enseñas a tus hijos a ser curiosos, independientes y seguros de sí mismos, les estás enseñando a pensar por sí mismos. Esas habilidades serán clave en cualquier escenario futuro.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin, who has three children, what skills he's encouraging his kids to learn to prepare for an AI-dominated future. A community member jokingly worried that by 2036, kids might need to compete for spots in roofing or plumbing programs as AI takes over other jobs. Kevin responds with a thoughtful perspective that instead of trying to predict specific career paths, parents should focus on developing fundamental human capabilities that will remain valuable regardless of how technology evolves.

vocabulary.definition: Not relying on others for support or guidance; capable of self-sufficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being independent often refers to individuals or teams that can make decisions and take actions without needing approval from higher authorities, fostering innovation and agility.

insight.nuance: While independence is generally positive, it can imply a lack of collaboration if taken to an extreme.

vocabulary.definition: Having a strong belief in one's own abilities and judgment; assured in oneself.
vocabulary.businessContext: Self-confidence is crucial in business environments, as it enables individuals to present ideas assertively, negotiate effectively, and lead teams with conviction.

insight.nuance: Self-confidence is often viewed positively, but excessive self-confidence can lead to overestimating one's abilities and making poor decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The arrangement or setup of components in a system or structure; the way in which something is organized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, configuration often refers to the setup of software systems, networks, or organizational structures to optimize performance and functionality.

insight.nuance: Configuration can imply a level of customization or adaptability, and is often used in contexts where specific arrangements are necessary for efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: The abilities or expertise that enable an individual to perform tasks effectively; often acquired through training or experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, skills are critical for workforce development, as they determine an employee's capability to contribute to projects and drive organizational success.

insight.nuance: The term 'skills' can encompass both hard skills (technical abilities) and soft skills (interpersonal abilities), and is often used in discussions about employee training and development.

speaker: Kevin Weil
text: It fundamentally disappoints me that this doesn't exist in the world today because the world would be a better place if we'd been able to ship that product. We tried to launch a new blockchain. It was a basket of currencies originally.
keySentence: It fundamentally disappoints me that we couldn't ship that product; the world needs it.
text_ko: 솔직히 이게 아직 세상에 없는 게 너무 안타까워요. 그 제품을 출시할 수만 있었더라면 세상이 더 나아졌을 거예요. 저희는 새 블록체인(blockchain)을 출시하려고 했어요. 원래는 여러 통화를 묶은 통화 바스켓(basket of currencies)이었어요.
text_zh: 让我很失望的是，这东西现在还不存在——要是我们能把那款产品真的推出来，世界会更好一些。我们当时试着推出一个新的区块链(blockchain)，最初打算把它做成一个货币篮子(basket of currencies)。
text_es: Me decepciona profundamente que esto no exista hoy en día; el mundo sería un lugar mejor si hubiéramos podido sacar ese producto al mercado. Intentamos lanzar una nueva cadena de bloques (blockchain). Al principio era una cesta de divisas (basket of currencies).
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about Libra, the cryptocurrency project he worked on at Facebook that ultimately failed. Kevin explains that Libra was designed to solve real problems like expensive international remittances, where people pay 20% fees to send money to family in other countries. The project aimed to enable instant, free money transfers through WhatsApp and Messenger using a new blockchain and basket of currencies. Kevin expresses genuine disappointment that this product never launched because he believes it would have made the world better by solving these costly, inefficient payment problems.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic and essential way; at the core or root of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'fundamentally' is often used to emphasize the core principles or values that underpin a strategy or decision.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a sense of depth and importance, suggesting that the issue at hand is not just superficial but intrinsic to the matter.

vocabulary.definition: To introduce a new product, service, or initiative to the market or public.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, 'launch' refers to the critical phase when a company makes its product available to consumers, often accompanied by marketing efforts.

insight.nuance: The term implies a sense of excitement and anticipation, and is often associated with significant planning and investment.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: The PM job can become a little too internal, influencing my stakeholders and getting alignment and all these things. But if you can't sell or support your own product, I don't trust you to build the product.
keySentence: If you can't sell your product, I don't trust you to build it.
text_ko: 프로덕트 매니저(PM) 일은 이해관계자(stakeholders)를 설득하고 얼라인먼트(alignment)을 맞추는 등 너무 내부적인 일에만 빠질 수 있어요. 그런데 자기 제품을 직접 팔거나 지원(support)을 할 줄 모르면 그 사람을 제품을 만드는 사람으로는 믿을 수 없어요.
text_zh: 产品经理这个工作有时候太偏内部了，就是影响各方利益相关者(stakeholders)啊，搞定大家的一致性(alignment)啊，这些事情。但是如果你连自己的产品都卖不出去或者支持不了，我真的不相信你能把产品做好。
text_es: El trabajo de PM puede volverse demasiado interno, influyendo en los stakeholders y buscando alineación y todas esas cosas. Pero si no puedes vender o dar soporte a tu propio producto, no confío en que puedas construir el producto.
fullContext: Lenny is discussing the importance of writing skills for product managers. Kevin explains that while internal alignment is important, PMs must also be able to create compelling external messaging. He believes that if a PM cannot effectively sell or support their own product to customers, they shouldn't be trusted to build that product in the first place.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or groups that have an interest or investment in a particular project or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, stakeholders can include employees, customers, investors, and suppliers, all of whom can influence or be affected by the outcomes of a project.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a level of responsibility or involvement, suggesting that stakeholders should be engaged in decision-making processes.

vocabulary.definition: The process of ensuring that all parties involved in a project or organization are on the same page regarding goals and objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, alignment is crucial for effective collaboration and can involve synchronizing strategies among teams, departments, or stakeholders.

insight.nuance: While alignment suggests harmony, it can also imply the need for negotiation and compromise among differing perspectives.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or occurring within an organization or entity, rather than with external factors or stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, internal processes, communications, and dynamics are crucial for operational efficiency and team cohesion.

insight.nuance: While 'internal' can imply a focus on organizational matters, it may also suggest a lack of external engagement or market awareness.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: We all talk about product sense. To me, it's just a fancy way of saying you can make good decisions with insufficient data.
keySentence: Product sense is a fancy way of saying you can make decisions with insufficient data.
text_ko: 다들 '프로덕트 센스(product sense)'에 대해 얘기하죠. 제게는 그게 데이터가 충분하지 않아도 좋은 결정을 내릴 수 있다는 걸 멋있게 포장한 말일 뿐이에요.
text_zh: 大家都在说产品直觉 (product sense)。在我看来，这不过是个高大上的说法，意思就是在数据不够的时候还能做出靠谱的决策。
text_es: Todos hablamos mucho sobre el sentido del producto (product sense). Para mí, no es más que una forma elegante de decir que puedes tomar buenas decisiones con información limitada.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin whether every PM should keep a decision log. Kevin explains that product sense, which is often viewed as a mystical quality, is actually just the ability to make good decisions without complete information. He advocates for PMs to practice decision-making by documenting their reasoning and tracking outcomes to improve their judgment over time.

vocabulary.definition: The intuitive ability to understand what makes a product valuable and appealing to users, often based on market trends and user feedback.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, 'product sense' is crucial for product managers and developers to create offerings that resonate with target audiences and drive sales.

insight.nuance: While 'product sense' implies a level of instinct and experience, it can sometimes be viewed as subjective, making it essential to balance intuition with data-driven insights.

vocabulary.definition: The process of selecting the best course of action from available options, often involving analysis and judgment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, the ability to make good decisions is vital for leadership roles, as it can significantly impact the direction and success of a company.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the importance of sound judgment and critical thinking, suggesting that decisions should be well-informed rather than impulsive.

vocabulary.definition: A situation where the available information is inadequate to draw reliable conclusions or make informed decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, insufficient data can hinder strategic planning, product development, and market analysis, leading to potential risks and missed opportunities.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of thorough research or analysis, which can undermine confidence in decision-making.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: When you get to offer stage, I send an email and I say all the terrible things that are probably going to reinforce their fears.
keySentence: I send an email and I say all the terrible things that are probably going to reinforce their fears.
text_ko: 오퍼 단계(offer stage)에 이르면 이메일을 보내서, 아마 그들의 우려를 더 강화할 만한 안 좋은 얘기들을 전부 해요.
text_zh: 到了发offer（offer stage）那步，我会发封邮件，把那些可能会让他们更担心的所有问题都摆出来。
text_es: Cuando se llega a la fase de oferta (offer stage), les mando un correo y les digo todas las peores cosas que probablemente solo van a confirmar sus temores.
fullContext: Lenny introduces Kevin's unique hiring approach called the 'unsell email.' Kevin describes how he sends candidates an honest email at the offer stage outlining all the potential downsides and challenges of the role. His philosophy is that if someone remains equally enthusiastic after learning about these negatives upfront, they're likely to be an excellent long-term hire who won't be surprised or disappointed later.

vocabulary.definition: To strengthen or support an idea, behavior, or structure, often by providing additional evidence or encouragement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, reinforcing a strategy or decision can help solidify team commitment and enhance the likelihood of successful implementation.

insight.nuance: While 'reinforce' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a lack of flexibility if used excessively in discussions about change.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: We are not even beneath the dust on the surface when it comes to what's going to change.
keySentence: We are not even beneath the dust on the surface of change.
text_ko: 앞으로 어떤 변화가 올지는 아직 본질에조차 닿지 못했어요.
text_zh: 说到未来的变化，我们现在掌握的那点东西连皮毛都算不上。
text_es: Ni siquiera hemos arañado la superficie de todo lo que va a cambiar.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin about interesting uses of AI in his work. Kevin shares a story about his 7-year-old daughter using Midjourney and asking 'Did I draw that?' after generating an image. He realizes that for her generation, AI image generation is just another tool like a crayon. Kevin uses this powerful metaphor to express how little we understand about the transformative potential of AI technology.

vocabulary.definition: The act or process of making something different from what it is or from what it would be if left alone.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, change often refers to organizational transformations, shifts in strategy, or adaptations in response to market dynamics.

insight.nuance: While 'change' can imply improvement or progress, it can also suggest disruption or instability, so context is important when discussing it.

vocabulary.definition: The outermost layer or boundary of an object; in a metaphorical sense, it refers to the visible aspects of a situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'surface' often describes the initial, observable factors of a problem or opportunity, suggesting that deeper analysis is required.

insight.nuance: Using 'surface' can imply that there is more complexity beneath the apparent simplicity, which is crucial in strategic evaluations.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: When you are building a product, you have this team, engineers, designers, so much potential. The purpose of product management, not the person, but the practice, is to convert that potential into as much realized value for someone as possible, right? Minimum loss.
keySentence: Product management converts so much potential into realized value with minimum loss.
text_ko: 제품을 만들 때 팀, 엔지니어, 디자이너 등 잠재력이 정말 많아요. 여기서 말하는 제품 관리(product management)는 사람을 가리키는 게 아니라 그 실천을 뜻하는 건데요, 목적은 그 잠재력을 가능한 한 많이 누군가에게 돌아가는 실현된 가치로 전환하는 거예요. 손실은 최소화하면서요.
text_zh: 当你在做产品的时候，你有这个团队，工程师、设计师，潜力巨大。产品管理(product management)这个实践的目的，不是说某个人，而是这套做法，就是要把这些潜力最大化地转换成对用户的实际价值，对吧？损失要最小。
text_es: Cuando estás desarrollando un producto, tienes este equipo, ingenieros, diseñadores, un potencial increíble. El objetivo de la gestión de producto, no me refiero a la persona sino a la práctica en sí, es convertir todo ese potencial en el máximo valor real posible para alguien, ¿verdad? Con la mínima pérdida.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin why he discourages people from going straight into product management roles. Kevin uses a physics analogy of potential and kinetic energy to explain his philosophy. He defines product management as the practice of converting a team's potential energy (the collective capabilities of engineers, designers, etc.) into kinetic energy (actual value delivered to customers) with minimal waste or loss.

vocabulary.definition: To change something into a different form or use; to transform.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'convert' often refers to the process of turning leads into customers or transforming potential into actual revenue.

insight.nuance: While 'convert' can imply a positive transformation, it can also suggest a degree of manipulation, so context is important when using it.

vocabulary.definition: The actual worth or benefit derived from an asset, investment, or effort after it has been fully realized or utilized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development, 'realized value' refers to the tangible benefits that customers experience from a product, as opposed to its potential or theoretical value.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of delivering measurable outcomes, making it crucial in performance evaluations and financial assessments.

vocabulary.definition: The inherent ability or capacity for growth, development, or future success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'potential' often describes untapped opportunities within a market, team, or product that could lead to significant gains if properly leveraged.

insight.nuance: While 'potential' is generally positive, it can also imply a lack of current effectiveness, so it should be used carefully to avoid suggesting underperformance.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of overseeing the development, marketing, and lifecycle of a product to ensure it meets customer needs and business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, product management is crucial for aligning cross-functional teams and guiding a product from conception to market launch and beyond.

insight.nuance: This term encompasses both strategic and tactical elements, and while it can refer to a specific role, it is often used to describe a broader organizational practice.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: I think some of this is changing with the advent of large language models and the ability to actually just mimic someone else's tone.
keySentence: the ability to actually just mimic someone else's tone.
text_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(large language models)의 등장으로 실제로 다른 사람의 말투를 그대로 흉내 낼 수 있게 되면서 이런 부분들이 일부 바뀌고 있는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得情况正在变化，随着大型语言模型（large language models）的兴起，我们现在真的可以直接模仿别人的语气了。
text_es: Creo que parte de esto está cambiando con la llegada de los modelos de lenguaje a gran escala (large language models) y la capacidad real de simplemente imitar el tono de otra persona.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kevin how to become a great writer, since Kevin believes writing skills are crucial for PMs. Kevin acknowledges that AI tools are changing the landscape but still emphasizes the importance of consuming quality content. He quotes celebrity chef Anthony Bourdain's philosophy about food - that to create good work, you must consume a lot of work, including some that isn't great, to develop your taste and judgment.

vocabulary.definition: The arrival or introduction of a notable person, event, or phenomenon.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, the 'advent' of new technologies or methodologies often signifies a shift in market dynamics or operational practices.

insight.nuance: The term 'advent' carries a sense of anticipation and significance, making it suitable for discussing innovations that are expected to have a transformative impact.

vocabulary.definition: To imitate or replicate someone or something, often in a way that closely resembles the original.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, companies may 'mimic' successful strategies or tones to resonate with target audiences or to establish a competitive edge.

insight.nuance: While 'mimic' can imply imitation, it may also suggest a lack of originality, so it should be used carefully to avoid negative connotations.

speaker: Kevin Yien
text: I explicitly do not mean read a bunch of other PM artifacts. You're not going to become a better writer by reading PRDs or whatever it is or support articles. It needs to be writing that compels.
keySentence: You won't become a better writer by reading PM artifacts; it needs to be writing that compels.
text_ko: 제가 분명히 말하는 건 다른 PM 관련 산출물(PM artifacts)을 잔뜩 읽으라는 뜻이 절대 아니에요. 제품 요구사항 문서(PRD)나 지원 문서(support articles)를 읽는다고 글쓰기 실력이 늘진 않아요. 중요한 건 사람을 사로잡고 움직이게 하는 글이에요.
text_zh: 我说的不是叫你去翻看一堆别人的产品经理的产出物(PM artifacts)。光看产品需求文档(PRDs)或者其他支持文章(support articles)，并不会让你写得更好。你需要的是那种能真正打动人的写作。
text_es: No me refiero a que te pongas a leer un montón de artefactos de PM (PM artifacts). No vas a mejorar como redactor solo por leer PRDs (PRDs) u otros artículos de soporte. Tiene que ser un texto que realmente enganche y convenza.
fullContext: Lenny continues asking about Kevin's advice for becoming a better writer. Kevin clarifies that PMs shouldn't just read typical product management documents like PRDs (Product Requirements Documents) or support articles. Instead, they need to read writing that compels action - writing that moves people to do something different. This is because the ultimate goal of PM writing is to motivate and guide others toward specific actions.

vocabulary.definition: Artifacts are tangible items or documents created during a process that provide evidence of that process or its outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, artifacts often refer to project documentation, such as product requirement documents (PRDs), design specifications, and user stories, which are essential for communication and project management.

insight.nuance: The term can imply not just physical items, but also digital documents or outputs that hold significance in a project lifecycle.

vocabulary.definition: To compel means to drive or force someone to take a specific action or adopt a particular viewpoint.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, compelling content or arguments are crucial for persuading stakeholders, customers, or team members to engage with a product or idea.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a sense of urgency or necessity, suggesting that the action taken is not merely encouraged but required.

vocabulary.definition: Explicitly means clearly and without ambiguity; it indicates that something is stated directly and in detail.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, being explicit is vital to ensure that all parties understand the expectations, requirements, or instructions without room for misinterpretation.

insight.nuance: While being explicit is generally positive, it can sometimes imply a lack of subtlety or sensitivity in communication.

speaker: Kim Scott
text: What could I do or stop doing that would make it easier to work with me?
keySentence: What could I do to make it easier to work with me sounds authentic.
text_ko: 저와 함께 일하기가 더 편해지도록 제가 뭘 더 하고, 뭘 안 하면 좋을까요?
text_zh: 我应该做些什么，或者别再做哪些事，才能让和我合作更顺利？
text_es: ¿Qué puedo hacer o dejar de hacer para que sea más fácil trabajar conmigo?
fullContext: Lenny asks Kim about how to solicit feedback effectively from colleagues and employees. Kim explains that asking generic questions like 'Do you have any feedback for me?' is ineffective because people will just say everything is fine. She shares her go-to question but emphasizes that leaders must adapt the language to sound authentic to their own communication style, otherwise people won't believe they genuinely want honest feedback.

speaker: Kim Scott
text: If I march into a room and I say, 'Lenny, I'm going to tell you the truth.' I'm kind of implying I've got a pipeline to God and you don't know anything. And that's not what this is all about.
keySentence: This is a dialogue, not a monologue, not a pipeline to God.
text_ko: 제가 방에 막 들어가서 "레니, 내가 진실을 말해줄게"라고 하면, 그건 마치 제가 신과 직통 연결돼 있고 레니는 아무것도 모른다는 식으로 암시하는 거예요. 그런데 그게 이 일이 하려는 바는 아니에요.
text_zh: 要是我大摇大摆走进房间，对Lenny说，“Lenny，我要告诉你真相。”那其实就是在暗示我好像跟上帝有直通线，而你什么都不懂。但这不是重点。
text_es: Si entro a una sala y digo: "Lenny, te voy a decir la verdad", estoy dando a entender que tengo una línea directa con Dios y que tú no sabes nada. Y no se trata de eso.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kim for specific language and phrases to use when giving direct feedback without making people defensive. Kim explains why she uses the term 'candor' instead of 'truth' when giving feedback. She emphasizes that effective feedback should be humble and conversational rather than authoritative, because claiming to know 'the truth' creates an adversarial dynamic instead of collaborative dialogue.

vocabulary.definition: To suggest or indicate something indirectly rather than stating it explicitly.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, implying can be used to convey a message or expectation without overtly stating it, which can be useful in negotiations or subtle feedback.

insight.nuance: Implying often carries a tone of assumption, which can be perceived as patronizing if not handled delicately.

speaker: Kim Scott
text: Six seconds is a really long time. Almost nobody can endure six full seconds of silence. So they'll probably tell you something. So now you've dragged this poor soul out on a conversational limb that they never wanted to go on.
keySentence: Silence can drag this poor soul out on a conversational limb.
text_ko: 여섯 초는 정말 긴 시간이에요. 거의 아무도 여섯 초 동안의 완전한 침묵을 견디지 못해요. 그래서 대부분 뭔가 말하게 돼요. 그렇게 하면 결국 상대를 원치 않았던 대화의 난처한 상황으로 끌어낸 셈이에요.
text_zh: 六秒钟其实挺长的。基本上没人能忍受整整六秒的沉默。所以他们多半会说点什么。这样一来，你就把这个可怜的家伙逼到了一个他们根本不想聊的话题上。
text_es: Seis segundos es muchísimo tiempo. Casi nadie aguanta seis segundos completos de silencio. Así que probablemente te van a decir algo. Y ahí ya tienes a esta pobre persona metida en una conversación que nunca quiso tener.
fullContext: Kim is explaining her framework for soliciting feedback from colleagues and employees. After asking for feedback, she recommends counting to six seconds of silence to embrace the discomfort, because most people cannot tolerate that much silence and will eventually share something. She describes this as putting the other person in an uncomfortable but necessary position to get honest feedback.

vocabulary.definition: To suffer patiently or to tolerate something difficult or unpleasant over a period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'endure' may refer to the ability of a company or its employees to withstand challenges such as market fluctuations or high-pressure situations.

insight.nuance: While 'endure' implies a sense of resilience, it can also suggest a passive acceptance of hardship rather than active engagement.

speaker: Kim Scott
text: A person takes a huge risk, especially if this person is your employee. A person takes a huge risk to give you critical feedback. And if you do not reward that risk richly, you're never going to get any feedback again.
keySentence: Reward that risk richly or lose future feedback.
text_ko: 누군가, 특히 직원이 당신에게 중요한 피드백(critical feedback)을 주려면 큰 위험을 감수하는 거예요. 그 위험을 충분히 보상해주지 않으면 다시는 피드백을 받을 수 없을 거예요.
text_zh: 员工给你提尖锐意见，这其实是冒了很大风险的。如果你不好好回应这种勇气，以后就别想再听到什么真话了。
text_es: Cuando una persona se arriesga enormemente, sobre todo si es tu empleado, para darte feedback crítico o retroalimentación dura, y tú no valoras ese riesgo como se merece, puedes estar seguro de que nunca más vas a recibir ese tipo de comentarios honestos.
fullContext: Kim is explaining the final step in her framework for soliciting feedback - the importance of rewarding candor. She emphasizes that when employees give their boss critical feedback, they're putting themselves in a vulnerable position that could potentially harm their career. Leaders must demonstrate appreciation and take action on the feedback to encourage future honest communication.

vocabulary.definition: Constructive criticism or evaluation provided to someone regarding their performance or work, aimed at improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, critical feedback is essential for employee development, fostering a culture of open communication and continuous improvement.

insight.nuance: While critical feedback is intended to be helpful, it can be perceived negatively if not delivered tactfully.

vocabulary.definition: Something given in recognition of service, effort, or achievement, often used to motivate or reinforce desired behaviors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, rewards can take the form of bonuses, promotions, or public recognition, serving to encourage employee engagement and loyalty.

insight.nuance: The effectiveness of a reward can vary based on individual preferences and organizational culture; it should be meaningful to the recipient.

vocabulary.definition: The possibility of loss, damage, or any negative outcome that may arise from a decision or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, assessing risk is crucial for strategic planning and decision-making, as it influences investment choices and operational strategies.

insight.nuance: Risk can be perceived differently depending on the context; what is considered a risk in one scenario may be seen as an opportunity in another.

speaker: Kim Scott
text: We all behave like assholes sometimes. And it's a big problem for us as well as for the people around us. And here's my story, when I acted like a jerk, what's yours?
keySentence: We all behave like assholes sometimes.
text_ko: 우리 모두 가끔은 정말 못되게 행동할 때가 있어요. 그건 우리 자신에게도, 주변 사람들에게도 큰 문제예요. 제가 먼저 얘기할게요 — 제가 무례하게 굴었을 때의 이야기예요. 당신 얘기는요?
text_zh: 我们有时候都会表现得像个混蛋。这不仅是我们自己的问题，对周围的人也很麻烦。我来说个我当混蛋的经历——你的呢？什么时候你也这样？
text_es: Todos actuamos como unos idiotas a veces. Y eso es un gran problema, tanto para nosotros como para quienes nos rodean. Te cuento la mía: cuando actué como un idiota. ¿Cuál es la tuya?
fullContext: Lenny asks Kim how to help leaders who have low self-awareness and believe obnoxious aggression is the only way to give feedback. Kim explains her approach of first sharing her own stories of when she made mistakes and acted poorly, then asking them for similar examples. This creates a safe space for self-reflection without judgment, helping leaders develop a growth mindset about their behavior.

speaker: Kim Scott
text: It's not disagreement that poses a risk to our relationships. It's unspoken disagreement. Many, I don't know about you Lenny, but a lot of my best professional relationships began with a good respectful disagreement.
keySentence: Unspoken disagreement poses a risk to our relationships, unlike respectful disagreement.
text_ko: 우리 관계를 위협하는 건 의견 차이 자체가 아니에요. 말로 꺼내지 않는, 즉 입밖으로 나오지 않은 의견 차이예요. 레니, 당신은 어떨지 모르겠지만 제 경험으론 가장 좋은 직장 관계들이 존중을 바탕으로 한 건설적인 의견 충돌에서 시작된 경우가 많아요.
text_zh: 对我们关系构成威胁的不是意见分歧，而是那些憋在心里不说出来的分歧。我不知道你怎么样，Lenny，但我很多最好的职场关系都是从一次良性的、相互尊重的争论开始的。
text_es: No es el desacuerdo lo que pone en riesgo nuestras relaciones. Es el desacuerdo que nos callamos. Muchas de mis mejores relaciones profesionales, no sé si te pase igual Lenny, pero muchas empezaron con un buen desacuerdo respetuoso.
fullContext: Kim is explaining how to handle feedback that you disagree with. She advises finding something you can agree with, then respectfully explaining your disagreement rather than just saying thank you and moving on. She makes the point that avoiding conflict by not voicing disagreements actually damages relationships more than having honest, respectful disagreements.

vocabulary.definition: Not expressed in words; implied or understood without being directly stated.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, unspoken issues can lead to misunderstandings and unresolved conflicts, which may hinder collaboration and team dynamics.

insight.nuance: While unspoken can suggest a level of subtlety or diplomacy, it may also imply avoidance of necessary communication.

vocabulary.definition: Showing politeness and consideration for others; valuing their opinions and feelings.
vocabulary.businessContext: In professional settings, being respectful fosters a positive work environment, encourages open dialogue, and enhances teamwork.

insight.nuance: Respectful behavior is essential in negotiations and discussions, as it can lead to more productive outcomes and stronger relationships.

vocabulary.definition: A difference of opinion or a conflict in views between individuals or groups.
vocabulary.businessContext: Disagreement in business can stimulate innovation and lead to better decision-making when managed constructively.

insight.nuance: While disagreement can be seen as negative, it can also be a catalyst for growth and improvement when approached with an open mind.

vocabulary.definition: The connections or associations between individuals or groups, often characterized by mutual interests or goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: Building strong professional relationships is crucial for networking, collaboration, and achieving long-term success in business.

insight.nuance: The term relationships encompasses both formal and informal connections, and the quality of these relationships can significantly impact business outcomes.

speaker: Kristen Berman
text: We want to remove the field that was like an open text fields where we're asking people an open-ended question and we improved conversion by 40% page over page. So, for sure, some questions are harder and you should not ask them.
keySentence: we improved conversion by 40% page over page.
text_ko: 사람들한테 열린 형식으로 답을 쓰게 하는 자유 입력 필드(open text field)를 빼고 싶었는데, 페이지별로 전환율(conversion)이 40%나 개선됐어요. 확실히 어떤 질문들은 더 어려워서 그런 질문들은 물어보지 않는 게 좋아요.
text_zh: 我们想把那个像开放式文本输入框(open text fields)的字段删掉，就是让人写开放式回答的那种。删掉后，页面的转化率(conversion)环比(page over page)提升了40%。所以，有些问题确实比较难，就别问了。
fullContext: Lenny asks about when adding questions to signup flows works versus when it doesn't. Kristen explains that while adding questions can sometimes increase conversion by getting users to think about benefits, the difficulty of the question matters greatly. She shares an example where removing an open text field improved conversion by 40% because open-ended questions require too much cognitive effort from users during signup.

vocabulary.definition: The process of changing or transforming something into a different state, often referring to turning potential customers into actual buyers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, conversion typically refers to the rate at which potential customers complete a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a service.

insight.nuance: While 'conversion' can refer to various changes, in a business context it often implies a successful outcome, particularly in sales and marketing.

vocabulary.definition: A type of question that allows for a free-form response, encouraging detailed answers rather than simple 'yes' or 'no' replies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In market research and customer feedback, open-ended questions are used to gather qualitative insights and understand customer opinions more deeply.

insight.nuance: Open-ended questions can provide richer data but may be more challenging to analyze compared to closed questions, which have predefined answers.

vocabulary.definition: Made better or enhanced in quality, performance, or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'improved' often describes enhancements in processes, products, or metrics, indicating progress and increased efficiency.

insight.nuance: The term 'improved' suggests a positive change, but it is important to specify the criteria or metrics used to measure that improvement.

speaker: Kristen Berman
text: we prioritize our present self over our future self... you actually have to give them a reason to take an action today.
keySentence: Present bias leads us to prioritize our present self over our future self.
text_ko: 우리는 현재의 나(present self)를 미래의 나(future self)보다 더 우선시하는 경향이 있어요. 그래서 사람들에게 오늘 바로 행동하게 하려면, 실제로 그들이 지금 행동할 이유를 줘야 해요.
text_zh: 我们往往更在乎现在的自己，而不是未来的自己……所以你得让他们今天就有理由去行动。
text_es: El problema es que priorizamos nuestro yo presente por encima del yo futuro, así que tienes que darles una razón para que actúen hoy.
fullContext: Kristen explains the third component of her 'Three Bs' framework for behavior change - Benefits. She's describing how people naturally prioritize immediate rewards over future benefits, which is a key insight for product design. This means product teams need to provide immediate, tangible benefits to motivate users to take action now, rather than relying solely on long-term value propositions.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange or deal with tasks or items in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, prioritizing is crucial for effective project management and resource allocation, ensuring that critical tasks receive the attention they require.

insight.nuance: While prioritizing often implies a systematic approach, it can also suggest a subjective judgment about what is most important, which may vary among individuals or teams.

speaker: Kristen Berman
text: I like to say we are what we measure, and it really matters what you measure. I'll give you a personal example. LendingClub, a while ago, hired me to increase their conversion flow for borrowers.
keySentence: it really matters what you measure.
text_ko: 저는 '우리는 무엇을 측정하느냐에 따라 달라진다'고 말하곤 해요. 그래서 뭘 측정하느냐가 정말 중요해요. 개인적인 예를 하나 들게요. 얼마 전 LendingClub에서 대출자 대상 전환 흐름(conversion flow)을 개선해 달라고 저를 고용했어요.
text_zh: 我常说，你衡量什么，就会成为什么；所以你到底在量什么很重要。举个我自己的例子：前一阵子，LendingClub找我去帮他们提升面向借款人的转化流程（conversion flow）。
text_es: Me gusta decir que somos lo que medimos, y realmente importa qué mides. Te doy un ejemplo personal: hace un tiempo LendingClub me contrató para aumentar su embudo de conversión (conversion flow) de prestatarios.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the potential dark side of behavioral design and how to avoid manipulating users. Kristen responds by explaining how incentive structures drive behavior, using her own experience as an example. She describes how LendingClub's payment structure - paying her only if she achieved a specific conversion increase - created problematic incentives that could lead to predatory lending practices.

vocabulary.definition: The process through which potential customers are guided towards completing a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, optimizing the conversion flow is crucial for maximizing sales and improving user experience, particularly in online platforms.

insight.nuance: While 'conversion flow' primarily refers to the user journey, it can also imply the efficiency and effectiveness of marketing strategies in leading to conversions.

vocabulary.definition: To assess the size, amount, or degree of something using a standard unit or method.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, measuring performance metrics is essential for evaluating success and making informed decisions based on data.

insight.nuance: The term 'measure' can imply both quantitative and qualitative assessments, but in business, it often emphasizes quantitative analysis.

speaker: Kristen Berman
text: So, we did this literature review. We came up with a hypothesis, and we had probably 30 different ways to implement this because the hypothesis is just a starting point. And then, we put it into quantitative research.
keySentence: The hypothesis is a starting point for de-risking our quantitative research.
text_ko: 그래서 문헌 검토(literature review)를 했어요. 가설(hypothesis)을 세웠는데, 가설은 출발점일 뿐이라 구현 방법이 아마 30가지쯤 나왔어요. 그리고 나서 그걸 정량 연구(quantitative research)로 진행했어요.
text_zh: 我们先做了文献回顾（literature review），提出了一个假设（hypothesis）。这个假设只是个出发点，所以大概有三十多种不同的实现方式。然后我们把这些方案拿去做量化研究（quantitative research）验证。
text_es: Así que hicimos una revisión bibliográfica (literature review). Formulamos una hipótesis y probablemente se nos ocurrieron unas 30 formas distintas de implementarla, porque la hipótesis es solo un punto de partida. Luego lo llevamos a investigación cuantitativa (quantitative research).
fullContext: Lenny asks about Kristen's process for developing the TikTok misinformation intervention that reduced shares by 24%. Kristen explains her team's rigorous approach, which starts with academic research, generates multiple implementation ideas, and then tests them quantitatively before building in-product. This systematic approach helps de-risk product launches and increase the likelihood of success.

vocabulary.definition: A proposed explanation or prediction that can be tested through research and experimentation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and research settings, a hypothesis serves as a foundational statement that guides the direction of studies, product development, or market analysis.

insight.nuance: While often seen as a starting point for investigation, a hypothesis should be formulated carefully to ensure it is testable and relevant.

vocabulary.definition: To put a plan, decision, or agreement into effect or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, implementing refers to the execution of strategies, processes, or systems that are designed to achieve specific objectives.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a structured approach, suggesting that careful planning and resource allocation are necessary for successful execution.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic investigation that primarily focuses on quantifying relationships, behaviors, or phenomena through statistical, mathematical, or computational techniques.
vocabulary.businessContext: Quantitative research is commonly used in market analysis, consumer behavior studies, and performance metrics to derive actionable insights from numerical data.

insight.nuance: This type of research is often contrasted with qualitative research, which explores subjective experiences and opinions rather than numerical data.

speaker: Kristen Berman
text: We never do a UX study where we're just showing people one thing because they could really like it or hate it, but they could really like or hate all the designs. We have no idea.
keySentence: We have no idea.
text_ko: 저희는 사용자 경험(UX) 연구(UX study)에서 한 가지 디자인만 보여주는 방식은 절대 안 해요. 사람들이 그걸 매우 좋아할 수도, 아주 싫어할 수도 있는데 다른 디자인들도 마찬가지로 좋아하거나 싫어할 수 있어서 어느 게 좋은지 전혀 알 수가 없거든요.
text_zh: 我们从不会在用户体验研究（UX study）里只给参与者看一个设计。因为他们可能会很喜欢或很讨厌，但别的设计也可能有同样的反应，这样我们就搞不清楚到底是哪一个设计在起作用。
text_es: Nunca hacemos un estudio de UX (UX study) en el que solo mostramos una opción, porque a la gente le puede encantar o le puede horrorizar —y lo mismo puede pasar con cualquiera de los diseños. No tenemos manera de saberlo.
fullContext: Lenny asks for advice on how product teams can conduct their own behavioral research. Kristen emphasizes the importance of comparative testing rather than absolute feedback. She explains that showing users only one design option provides no useful data since users might like or dislike all potential designs equally - the key insight comes from relative comparison between multiple options.

vocabulary.definition: The conceptual and aesthetic plans or arrangements of a product, service, or system that dictate its functionality and user experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, designs are critical as they directly influence user engagement and satisfaction, often requiring iterative testing and refinement based on user feedback.

insight.nuance: The term 'designs' can imply both the visual aspects and the underlying functionality, highlighting the importance of a holistic approach in product development.

speaker: Kristen Berman
text: There's kind of two steps. One, you can outline the full high level flow where you're saying maybe there's 50 steps in getting to the behavior, and you can do this before they hit your product, too.
keySentence: you can outline the full high level flow where you're saying maybe there's 50 steps in getting to the behavior
text_ko: 대체로 두 단계예요. 첫 번째는 전체적인 하이레벨 흐름(high-level flow)을 윤곽 잡는 건데, 원하는 행동(behavior)에 도달하기까지 50단계쯤 걸릴 거라고 보고 전체를 정리하는 거예요. 이건 사용자가 제품에 도달하기 전에도 미리 할 수 있어요.
text_zh: 基本上有两步。第一，你可以把整个高层流程(high-level flow)先梳理清楚——比如说，为了促成那个目标行为(behavior)，可能要走大概50个步骤。这件事也可以在用户还没接触到你的产品之前就做。
text_es: Hay como dos pasos. Primero, puedes trazar el flujo completo de alto nivel (high-level flow), donde planteas que quizá haya 50 pasos para lograr ese comportamiento, y puedes hacer esto incluso antes de que lleguen a tu producto.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the behavioral diagnosis process that Kristen mentioned as a key tool for product teams. A behavioral diagnosis is like a detailed journey map that analyzes every step users take to complete a desired behavior. Kristen explains how her team creates extremely detailed documentation (200-300 slides) of user flows, then overlays psychological insights to identify barriers at each step.

vocabulary.definition: A high level flow refers to a broad overview of a process or system, emphasizing the main stages without delving into intricate details.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, a high level flow is often used in project management and product development to communicate the essential steps involved in achieving a goal or completing a task.

insight.nuance: This term is typically used when discussing processes that require simplification for clarity, avoiding overly technical language that may confuse stakeholders.

vocabulary.definition: Behavior refers to the actions or reactions of an individual or group in response to external or internal stimuli.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business contexts, understanding customer behavior is crucial for marketing strategies, product design, and user experience optimization.

insight.nuance: While 'behavior' can imply both positive and negative actions, in a business setting it often focuses on consumer habits and preferences.

vocabulary.definition: To outline means to provide a structured summary or framework of the main points or components of a subject.
vocabulary.businessContext: Outlining is a common practice in business for planning presentations, reports, or project proposals, ensuring that all key aspects are addressed systematically.

insight.nuance: While outlining is generally seen as a preparatory step, it can also imply a lack of detail, so it should be used when clarity and organization are prioritized over depth.

speaker: Krithika Shankarraman
text: Everyone knew of ChatGPT, but when you clicked one zoom level further, the thing that came up was, 'I don't know what to use it for. I don't know what it replaces. Should I be using search for this?
keySentence: I don't know what to use it for.
text_ko: 다들 ChatGPT는 알고 있었는데, 한 단계 더 들어가 보면 돌아오는 반응은 "이걸 어디에 써야 할지 모르겠어요. 뭘 대신하는지도 모르겠고, 이럴 때 검색(search)을 써야 하나요?"였어요.
text_zh: 大家都知道 ChatGPT（ChatGPT），但你再往里点一层，会听到的是：“我不知道该怎么用它。我不知道它会替代什么东西。我是不是应该用搜索(search)来做这事？”
text_es: Todo el mundo conocía ChatGPT, pero si profundizabas un nivel más, lo que salía era: "No sé para qué sirve. No sé qué sustituye. ¿Debería usar la búsqueda (search) para esto?"
fullContext: Lenny asks Krithika about the value that marketing adds to a product like ChatGPT, which seems so magical that it wouldn't need marketing support. Krithika explains that while awareness wasn't the problem for ChatGPT - everyone had heard of it - the real challenge was helping people understand practical applications. The marketing team's role became creating moments of realization where users discovered new ways to incorporate ChatGPT into their daily workflows and decision-making processes.

vocabulary.definition: To take the place of something or to substitute one thing for another.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, 'replaces' often refers to innovations or new solutions that supplant older methods, products, or services, impacting market dynamics and consumer behavior.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a complete substitution or a more gradual transition, depending on the context of technological advancement or market evolution.

speaker: Krithika Shankarraman
text: A lot of marketing metrics tend to be vanity metrics about the number of clicks that you got, number of views, number of impressions. I think those are all bullshit numbers.
keySentence: I think those are all bullshit numbers.
text_ko: 많은 마케팅 지표들이 결국 클릭 수, 조회수, 노출수처럼 겉보기 좋은 허영 지표(vanity metrics)에 그치는 경우가 많아요. 저는 그런 숫자들이 다 쓸모없는 숫자라고 생각해요.
text_zh: 很多营销指标（marketing metrics）往往只是虚荣指标（vanity metrics），像点击数(clicks)、观看量(views)、展示次数(impressions)之类的数字。我觉得那些都是扯淡的。
text_es: Muchas métricas de marketing acaban siendo métricas de vanidad (vanity metrics): el número de clics (clicks), de vistas (views), de impresiones (impressions). Para mí, son simplemente números que no sirven para nada.
fullContext: During her introduction, Krithika discusses the common problem with marketing measurement and focus. She argues against focusing on surface-level engagement metrics like clicks, views, and impressions, calling them meaningless. Instead, she advocates for measuring the actual customer experience and the lasting impression that interactions with your brand create. This reflects her philosophy that marketing should focus on meaningful outcomes rather than vanity metrics that look good in reports but don't drive real business value.

vocabulary.definition: Metrics are quantitative measures used to assess, compare, and track performance or progress in various areas.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, metrics are essential for evaluating the effectiveness of strategies, campaigns, and operations, often guiding decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: While metrics provide valuable insights, they must be relevant and actionable to be truly effective; otherwise, they may lead to misguided conclusions.

vocabulary.definition: Vanity metrics are superficial data points that may look impressive but do not provide meaningful insights into the performance or success of a business.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing, vanity metrics such as likes and shares can mislead stakeholders into believing a campaign is successful when it lacks real engagement or conversion.

insight.nuance: While vanity metrics can be useful for brand visibility, they should not be the sole focus of performance evaluation, as they often do not correlate with business growth.

speaker: Krithika Shankarraman
text: So I was an engineer before I became a marketer, and so I have brought a little bit of an engineer's framework to the marketing side of the house.
keySentence: I have brought a little bit of an engineer's framework to the marketing side of the house.
text_ko: 마케터가 되기 전에 엔지니어로 일했어요. 그래서 엔지니어식 사고방식을 마케팅 쪽에 조금 적용해왔어요.
text_zh: 我原来是工程师，后来才转做营销，所以把工程师那套思维方式带到营销这边了。
text_es: Antes de dedicarme a la mercadotecnia (marketing) era ingeniero, así que traje algo de la mentalidad de ingeniero al equipo de marketing (marketing).
fullContext: Lenny asks Krithika what people should do instead of copying successful marketing playbooks from other companies. Krithika explains her engineering background and how it shaped her systematic approach to marketing. She introduces her four-step framework that starts with diagnosis - systematically identifying the real problem before jumping to solutions. This methodical approach contrasts with the common tendency to immediately implement tactics that worked for other companies without understanding the underlying context and challenges.

vocabulary.definition: A framework is a structured system or set of guidelines that provides a foundation for understanding or developing something. It serves as a conceptual structure that helps organize and analyze complex information or processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a framework often refers to a set of best practices or methodologies that guide project management, software development, or strategic planning. It helps teams align their efforts and ensures consistency in execution.

insight.nuance: While 'framework' suggests a supportive structure, it may imply rigidity; thus, it is important to clarify when flexibility is allowed within the framework.

vocabulary.definition: To engineer means to design, create, or develop something using scientific principles and technical skills. It often involves problem-solving and innovation to produce effective solutions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, engineers play a critical role in developing software, hardware, and systems, driving innovation and ensuring that products meet user needs and industry standards. Their expertise is essential in translating ideas into functional products.

insight.nuance: While 'engineer' typically refers to technical professionals, it can also imply a level of creativity and ingenuity, especially in contexts where innovative solutions are required.

speaker: Krithika Shankarraman
text: And then, this is the critical step. The next one is you have to intentionally take a different path than what everyone else is doing. And so driving a strategy that sort of sets the company apart is really critically important.
keySentence: Taking a different path is core to the discipline of marketing.
text_ko: 그리고 이건 정말 중요한 단계예요. 다음으로는 다른 사람들처럼 그냥 따라가지 말고 의도적으로 다른 길을 가야 해요. 즉 회사를 돋보이게 하는 전략(strategy)을 세우고 그것을 밀고 나가는 것이 정말 중요해요.
text_zh: 这一步至关重要。接下来你得有意识地走别人不走的路——推动一套能让公司脱颖而出的策略(strategy)非常关键。
text_es: Y este es el paso crítico: a continuación tienes que, deliberadamente, tomar un camino distinto al que sigue todo el mundo. Por eso impulsar una estrategia que realmente diferencie a la empresa es fundamental.
fullContext: Krithika is explaining the third step of her DATE framework (Diagnose, Analyze, Take a different path, Experiment). After diagnosing the problem and analyzing what competitors are doing, she emphasizes that the crucial step is deliberately choosing a different approach. She argues that differentiation isn't just nice to have - it's fundamental to effective marketing. Rather than trying to execute the same strategies as competitors but slightly better, successful companies must find unique positioning and approaches that set them apart in the marketplace.

vocabulary.definition: Of great importance; essential for the success or functioning of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a critical step often refers to a pivotal action or decision that significantly influences the outcome of a project or strategy.

insight.nuance: While 'critical' can imply urgency, it also conveys a sense of necessity, making it suitable for discussions about key decisions or milestones.

vocabulary.definition: Done with purpose or intention; deliberately.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, acting intentionally means making strategic decisions that are purposeful and aligned with the company's goals, rather than reacting passively.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes the need for conscious decision-making, which is important in leadership and strategic planning discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, strategy refers to the comprehensive plan that outlines how a company will achieve its objectives and compete effectively in the market.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of careful planning and foresight, making it appropriate for discussions about competitive positioning and resource allocation.

speaker: Krithika Shankarraman
text: Really, what you want to be looking at is your impact on either signups if you're a self-serve product, PLG, or in terms of a B2B company, sales leads and revenue that you're driving, pipeline and opportunity that you're driving.
keySentence: what you want to be looking at is your impact on either signups if you're a self-serve product
text_ko: 사실 진짜로 봐야 할 건 당신이 끼치는 영향이에요. 셀프 서비스(self-serve) 제품이나 PLG(Product-Led Growth) 모델이라면 가입(signups)에 미치는 영향이고, B2B라면 당신이 만들어내는 영업 리드(sales leads)와 매출(revenue), 그리고 파이프라인(pipeline)과 기회(opportunity)에 미치는 영향이에요.
text_zh: 其实你要看的是你产生的实际影响：如果你是自助产品（self-serve product）或走产品驱动增长（PLG），就看对注册量（signups）的推动；如果你是面向企业的公司（B2B），就看你带来的销售线索（sales leads）、营收（revenue），以及你推动的销售管道（pipeline）和商机（opportunity）。
fullContext: Krithika is sharing a case study from Retool where she applied her diagnostic framework. She had just criticized vanity metrics like clicks and impressions, emphasizing that marketers should focus on business outcomes that actually matter. In this example, she explains how they discovered their paid social channels weren't generating meaningful sales leads or revenue despite potentially showing good engagement numbers. This diagnostic step revealed they needed to invest in completely new marketing engines rather than just scaling existing channels.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that one thing has on another.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'impact' often refers to the measurable outcomes of strategies or initiatives, such as customer acquisition or revenue growth.

insight.nuance: While 'impact' can denote positive effects, it can also refer to negative consequences, so context is essential.

vocabulary.definition: A product or service that allows customers to independently access and utilize its features without direct assistance from a sales representative.
vocabulary.businessContext: Self-serve products are common in SaaS (Software as a Service) models, where users can sign up, configure, and use the product on their own.

insight.nuance: This term emphasizes user autonomy and is often associated with lower customer acquisition costs but may require robust user support resources.

vocabulary.definition: Potential customers who have shown interest in a company's products or services and have the potential to become paying clients.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales and marketing, generating and nurturing sales leads is crucial for driving revenue and growth, often tracked through CRM systems.

insight.nuance: The term 'sales leads' can vary in quality; not all leads are equally likely to convert into sales, so qualification processes are important.

vocabulary.definition: A visual representation or systematic process that outlines the stages a potential sale goes through from initial contact to closing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales management, the pipeline helps teams track progress, forecast revenue, and identify bottlenecks in the sales process.

insight.nuance: While 'pipeline' typically refers to a sales context, it can also apply to project management and product development stages.

speaker: Krithika Shankarraman
text: you have to spend the hours and the time to really understand your customer, and there is no replacement for that.
keySentence: you have to spend the hours and the time to really understand your customer
text_ko: 정말로 고객을 제대로 이해하려면 충분한 시간과 노력을 들여야 해요. 그걸 대신할 방법은 없어요.
text_zh: 你得花时间和精力去真正了解你的客户，这事没有捷径。
text_es: Tienes que dedicar las horas necesarias para entender de verdad a tu cliente; no hay atajo para eso.
fullContext: This is Krithika's closing advice to listeners, summarizing her main philosophy about marketing. Throughout the conversation, she has consistently argued against following generic playbooks and frameworks, instead advocating for deep, first-hand customer understanding. She emphasizes that despite the availability of countless marketing frameworks and the emergence of AI tools, there is no substitute for investing significant time and effort in truly comprehending your customers' needs, problems, and behaviors. This hands-on approach forms the foundation of effective marketing strategy.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something; to comprehend.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding customer needs and preferences is crucial for developing effective marketing strategies and products.

insight.nuance: While 'understand' implies a basic comprehension, it can also suggest a deeper insight into complex issues when used in a business context.

vocabulary.definition: The act of substituting one thing for another; an item that takes the place of another.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development, identifying a suitable replacement for outdated technology can be critical for maintaining competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: While 'replacement' suggests a direct substitution, it can also imply an improvement or upgrade in quality or functionality.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: I think CRED's insight was actually quite simple. We realized that unfortunately the value of time and per capita income is concentrated with 25 million families and therefore focusing on them is important.
keySentence: Focusing on 25 million families is important due to concentrated per capita income.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 CRED가 얻은 통찰은 사실 꽤 단순했어요. 우리가 깨달은 건, 안타깝게도 시간의 가치와 1인당 소득(per capita income)이 2,500만 가구에 집중되어 있어서 그들에게 초점을 맞추는 게 중요하다는 점이었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得CRED的洞察其实挺简单的：可惜时间的价值和人均收入都集中在大约2500万户家庭身上，所以把重心放在他们身上很重要。
text_es: Creo que la visión de CRED fue bastante simple: nos dimos cuenta de que, lamentablemente, el valor del tiempo y el ingreso per cápita se concentran en 25 millones de familias, así que tiene sentido centrarse en ellas.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kunal what he's learned during his journey building CRED over the past six years compared to his previous startups. Kunal explains that CRED's core strategy was to focus on India's wealthiest 25 million families rather than trying to serve the entire Indian market. He recognized that this demographic has higher per capita income and values time differently than the broader Indian population, making them more similar to global consumers in their behavior and spending patterns.

vocabulary.definition: Having a high density or intensity in a specific area or among a particular group.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'concentrated' often refers to market segments where a significant share of resources, wealth, or consumer demand is focused, impacting strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: While 'concentrated' can imply strength in a specific area, it may also suggest vulnerability if over-reliance on a small segment is present.

vocabulary.definition: The average income earned per person in a given area, typically used to gauge economic health and living standards.
vocabulary.businessContext: Per capita income is a crucial metric for businesses when assessing market potential, consumer purchasing power, and economic disparities in different regions.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in economic analyses and reports; however, it may not fully capture income distribution disparities within a population.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: I often tell people that entrepreneurs are uncertainty absorbers for everybody- for employees, for investors, for customers- and therefore they get rewarded for being those people who remove uncertainty from people's lives. But the kind of expectations keep changing at companies of scale.
keySentence: Entrepreneurs are uncertainty absorbers, rewarded for removing uncertainty in companies of scale.
text_ko: 저는 종종 사람들에게 기업가(entrepreneurs)는 직원들이나 투자자들, 고객들처럼 모두의 불확실성을 흡수해 주는 존재, 즉 불확실성 흡수자(uncertainty absorbers)라고 말해요. 그래서 사람들 삶의 불확실성을 제거해 주는 사람들이 그에 대한 보상을 받는다고요. 다만 규모가 큰 회사들(companies of scale)에서는 그런 기대치가 계속 바뀌어요.
text_zh: 我经常跟人说，创业者其实就是帮所有人消化不确定性的——帮员工、帮投资人、帮客户消化，所以他们能拿到回报，就是因为他们把别人生活中的不确定性给解决了。但是公司做大了以后，大家对你的期待就一直在变。
text_es: Siempre les digo a las personas que los emprendedores son como esponjas de incertidumbre para todos - para los empleados, para los inversionistas, para los clientes - y por eso se les recompensa por ser esas personas que le quitan la incertidumbre a la vida de la gente. Pero el tipo de expectativas sigue cambiando en las empresas grandes.
fullContext: Kunal is discussing the lessons he's learned while scaling CRED from a startup to a larger company. He's explaining how the founder's role evolves as the company grows, and how different stakeholders (seed investors vs growth investors) have different tolerance levels for uncertainty. This insight comes from his experience managing expectations across different stages of company growth and different types of investors on CRED's cap table.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who start and manage businesses, often taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, entrepreneurs are seen as innovators who drive economic growth by creating new products and services, often in startup environments.

insight.nuance: The term carries a connotation of creativity and risk-taking, and is often used positively to highlight individuals who challenge the status quo.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or entities that mitigate or manage unpredictability in business environments, providing stability to stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and corporate settings, uncertainty absorbers are crucial as they help navigate market fluctuations and instill confidence among employees and investors.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes a proactive role in managing risk, and is often used in discussions about leadership and strategic decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Beliefs or assumptions about what will happen in the future, often related to performance or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate context, managing stakeholder expectations is vital for maintaining relationships and ensuring alignment on goals and deliverables.

insight.nuance: Expectations can shift based on market conditions or company performance, making it important to communicate clearly to avoid misunderstandings.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: One of the things I've learned is that profit pools of a country tell you a lot about what the country values.
keySentence: profit pools of a country tell you a lot about what the country values.
text_ko: 제가 배운 것 중 하나는 한 나라의 수익 풀(profit pools)을 보면 그 나라가 무엇을 가치 있게 여기는지 많은 걸 알 수 있다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我发现，从一个国家的利润池（profit pools）就能看出它到底重视什么。
text_es: Una de las cosas que he aprendido es que las fuentes de beneficio (profit pools) de un país te dicen mucho sobre lo que ese país valora.
fullContext: Kunal is sharing insights from building CRED about understanding different markets. A 'profit pool' refers to where the most profitable companies and business models exist in an economy. He's explaining that entrepreneurs shouldn't simply copy successful business models from other countries because what's profitable reflects cultural values - for example, India has fewer profitable retail companies compared to Western markets due to different consumption patterns and cultural factors like low divorce rates.

vocabulary.definition: Profit pools refer to the total profits earned in a particular industry or market segment, often highlighting the most lucrative areas within that space.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, understanding profit pools helps companies identify where to focus their resources and efforts to maximize profitability.

insight.nuance: The term implies a strategic approach to analyzing market dynamics, often used in competitive analysis and market entry strategies.

vocabulary.definition: Values are the principles or standards of behavior that are considered important by an individual or organization, guiding decision-making and actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, company values shape corporate culture and influence employee behavior, customer relations, and brand identity.

insight.nuance: The term often carries emotional weight and reflects deeper beliefs, making it essential for leaders to align organizational practices with stated values.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: So when you're not paid an hourly salary, the concept of time is not the same. And when the concept of time is not the same, paying for time is hard to do.
keySentence: The concept of time differs when not paid hourly; paying for time is hard to do.
text_ko: 시간당 급여(hourly salary)를 받지 않으면 시간에 대한 인식이 달라져요. 그러면 시간을 기준으로 비용을 지불하기가 어려워요.
text_zh: 不按小时拿工资的话，对时间的看法就不一样。时间观念一变，按时间付酬就很难办。
text_es: Si no te pagan por horas, el tiempo no se percibe igual. Y cuando el tiempo no se percibe igual, cobrar por él resulta complicado.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the difference between DAUs (daily active users) and ARPUs (average revenue per user) in India - why it's easy to get users but hard to make money per user. Kunal explains that Indians have never been paid hourly wages, unlike Americans who typically start with hourly jobs. This cultural difference means Indians don't mentally calculate the value of their time in the same way, making them less willing to pay for time-saving services or convenience.

vocabulary.definition: A concept is an abstract idea or a general notion that represents something in the mind. It serves as a foundational element for understanding complex theories or systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, concepts are often used to develop new products, services, or strategies, guiding innovation and decision-making processes.

insight.nuance: While 'concept' is often used in formal discussions, it can also imply a theoretical or untested idea, so it should be used with care in practical applications.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: What happens is there is concentration of trust. So you will see that super apps, superstars, super companies all exist in low trust markets because the lack of trust creates concentration of trust, and therefore you will see one app can do 400 things.
keySentence: Concentration of trust leads to super apps in low trust markets.
text_ko: 결국 일어나는 건 신뢰의 집중(concentration of trust)이에요. 신뢰가 낮은 시장일수록 슈퍼앱(super apps)이나 슈퍼스타(superstars), 슈퍼 기업(super companies)이 등장하죠. 신뢰가 부족하니까 신뢰가 한곳으로 쏠리고, 그 결과 한 앱이 400가지 일을 하게 되는 걸 보게 돼요.
text_zh: 其实就是这样，信任会集中到少数几个地方。所以你会发现，超级应用(super apps)、超级明星、超级公司，这些都出现在信任度比较低的市场里，因为大家普遍不信任，反而会把信任都集中给少数几个，所以你看一个应用能做四百件事情。
text_es: Lo que pasa es que se concentra la confianza. Entonces vas a ver que las súper apps, las empresas estrella, las súper compañías, todas existen en mercados donde hay poca confianza, porque justamente esa falta de confianza hace que la confianza se concentre, y por eso ves que una sola app puede hacer 400 cosas diferentes.
fullContext: Lenny asks why focus is considered a curse in Asian markets, contrary to the common US advice of building one thing well. Kunal explains the concept of 'low trust markets' - developing countries where institutions aren't strong enough to protect consumers from bad business practices. In these markets, consumers concentrate their trust in a few proven brands rather than trying new ones, which is why super apps (like WeChat) and conglomerate companies (like Tata in India) are successful there.

vocabulary.definition: The action or power of focusing one's attention or mental effort on a particular object or activity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, concentration often refers to the aggregation of resources, market share, or decision-making power within a limited number of entities, which can influence market dynamics.

insight.nuance: While concentration can imply efficiency and strength, it may also suggest monopolistic tendencies or reduced competition.

vocabulary.definition: A firm belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, trust is crucial for building relationships with customers, partners, and employees, influencing brand loyalty and collaboration.

insight.nuance: Trust can be fragile and is often built over time; its absence can lead to skepticism and reduced engagement.

vocabulary.definition: Applications that provide multiple services and functionalities within a single platform, often integrating various aspects of users' digital lives.
vocabulary.businessContext: Super apps are particularly prevalent in markets with low trust, where users prefer a single, trusted platform for diverse needs rather than multiple, potentially unreliable services.

insight.nuance: While super apps can enhance user convenience, they may also raise concerns regarding data privacy and monopolistic practices.

vocabulary.definition: Economic environments characterized by a general lack of trust among consumers and businesses, often leading to skepticism about products and services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In low trust markets, companies may need to invest heavily in building credibility and reputation, often resulting in the emergence of super apps that consolidate trust in one platform.

insight.nuance: The term highlights the challenges businesses face in gaining consumer confidence and the strategies they may adopt to navigate these environments.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: I think a curious person is somebody who is constantly demonstrating that they are not proud of their expertise, and they will demonstrate extraordinary amounts of excitement when they face a problem which they have no clue how to solve.
keySentence: Curious people are not proud of their expertise and demonstrate extraordinary amounts of excitement.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 호기심 많은 사람은 자신의 전문성을 앞세우지 않는다는 걸 항상 보여주는 사람이에요. 그리고 어떻게 해결해야 할지 전혀 감이 안 오는 문제를 만나면 정말 신나해요.
text_zh: 我觉得，好奇的人就是那种会不断用行动证明自己并不会因为当了专家就自满；遇到自己根本不知道该怎么解决的问题时，反而会兴奋不已。
text_es: Creo que una persona curiosa es alguien que demuestra constantemente que no presume de su experiencia (expertise) y que se entusiasma de forma extraordinaria cuando se enfrenta a un problema para el que no tiene ni idea de cómo resolverlo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Kunal why curiosity is so important to him, noting that he has a show called CRED Curious and often talks about the power of curiosity. Kunal explains that curious people aren't focused on showing off what they already know, but instead get excited about problems they can't solve. He contrasts this with people who prioritize demonstrating their existing expertise, which he believes limits their growth and ability to adapt to new challenges.

vocabulary.definition: To show or prove something clearly through evidence or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, demonstrating can refer to showcasing a product's features during a presentation or providing evidence of a strategy's effectiveness through data.

insight.nuance: While 'demonstrate' implies a clear and observable action, it can also suggest a level of teaching or guiding others in understanding a concept.

vocabulary.definition: Remarkably unusual or exceptional; going beyond what is ordinary.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, extraordinary performance may refer to achieving results that significantly exceed industry standards or expectations.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting not just uniqueness but also a level of admiration or respect for the achievement.

vocabulary.definition: To confront or deal with a challenge or difficulty directly.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, facing a problem often involves analyzing the issue, brainstorming solutions, and implementing a plan to overcome obstacles.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies a proactive approach, suggesting that one is willing to engage with the issue rather than avoiding it.

speaker: Kunal Shah
text: I recently asked the question: which species or animals have survived for more than 100 million years without changing too much and what is common in all of them?
keySentence: which species or animals have survived for more than 100 million years without changing too much
text_ko: 최근에 제가 한 질문이 있어요: 1억 년(100 million years) 넘게 크게 변하지 않고 살아남은 종(species)이나 동물(animals)들은 어떤 게 있고, 그들 모두의 공통점은 무엇일까요?
text_zh: 我最近在想一个问题：哪些物种(species)或动物已经存活超过一亿年，而且几乎没怎么变？它们有什么共同点？
text_es: Hace poco me hice la pregunta: ¿qué especies o animales han sobrevivido más de 100 millones de años sin cambiar casi nada y qué tienen en común?
fullContext: Kunal is explaining how he uses ChatGPT to explore random questions that satisfy his curiosity. He shares an example where he asked about long-surviving animal species and discovered they share three traits: ability to reduce metabolism at will, high conversion rates when hunting for food, and strong adaptation skills. He draws parallels between these survival traits and successful business principles, showing how curiosity-driven questions can lead to useful insights.

vocabulary.definition: To continue to live or exist, especially in spite of danger or hardship.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'survived' often refers to a company or product that has managed to remain viable despite market challenges or competition.

insight.nuance: While 'survived' implies endurance, it can also suggest a lack of growth or improvement, so it’s important to consider the context in which it is used.

vocabulary.definition: Occurring frequently or widely; shared by many.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'common' can refer to practices, trends, or challenges that are prevalent across an industry or among competitors.

insight.nuance: While 'common' suggests familiarity, it can also imply a lack of uniqueness, so it is often used to highlight areas where differentiation is needed.

vocabulary.definition: A group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, 'species' can metaphorically refer to different categories of products or services that share common characteristics.

insight.nuance: The term 'species' is generally used in biological contexts, but its metaphorical use in business should be clear to avoid confusion.

vocabulary.definition: Undergoing alteration or transformation; becoming different.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'changing' often describes market dynamics, consumer preferences, or technological advancements that require companies to adapt.

insight.nuance: While 'changing' indicates progress or evolution, it can also imply instability, so it’s important to clarify whether the change is viewed positively or negatively.

speaker: Lane Shackleton
text: Moments that stretch you or moments that you feel uncomfortable in or you find yourself saying, "Oh shit. I shouldn't be here," or, "I'm under qualified to be here," those are the moments you should be seeking out.
keySentence: Seek moments that stretch you, even if you feel under qualified.
text_ko: 나를 성장시키는 순간이나 불편해서 ‘아, 여기 있으면 안 되겠다’ ‘여기 있을 자격이 없어’라고 스스로 말하게 되는 순간들—딱 그런 순간들을 일부러 찾아야 해요.
text_zh: 那些能逼你成长、让你不舒服、甚至会冒出“我不该在这儿”或“我不够格”这种念头的时刻，正是你该主动去争取的。
text_es: Los momentos que te sacan de tu zona de confort, en los que te sientes incómodo o en los que te sorprendes diciéndote "vaya, no debería estar aquí" o "no estoy lo bastante cualificado para estar aquí", son precisamente los momentos que deberías buscar.
