vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, being humbled can foster resilience and adaptability, as leaders and employees learn from failures and setbacks, ultimately leading to personal and professional growth.

insight.nuance: While 'humbled' often has a positive connotation of growth, it can also imply a loss of confidence, so context is crucial when using the term.

speaker: Sachin Monga
text: writers are in control over being able to deliver their best work on their terms to their audience, make money directly from their subscribers, and also that readers should be in control over their experience.
keySentence: Writers are in control of delivering their best work on their terms.
text_ko: 작가들은 자신이 원하는 방식으로 최고의 작품을 독자들에게 전달할 주도권을 가지고, 구독자(subscribers)에게서 직접 수익을 얻을 수 있어야 해요. 동시에 독자들(readers)도 자신의 경험을 스스로 선택하고 통제할 수 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 作者可以自己掌控，按自己的方式把最好的作品呈现给受众、直接从订阅者(subscribers)那里赚钱；同时读者也能掌控自己的阅读体验。
text_es: Que los escritores puedan ofrecer lo mejor de su trabajo en sus propias condiciones a su audiencia, generar ingresos directamente de sus suscriptores y que, además, los lectores tengan el control de su experiencia.
fullContext: Lenny asks how Substack prioritizes what to work on and what their North Star is. Sachin explains that Substack's founders start from core principles about how the internet should work, with people having control over their own destiny rather than being subject to algorithmic feeds. This principle of user control - both for writers and readers - guides their product decisions and prioritization framework.

vocabulary.definition: The power to influence or direct behavior or the course of events.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, control can refer to management's ability to steer operations, maintain quality standards, and ensure compliance with regulations.

insight.nuance: While control implies authority, it can also suggest a balance between oversight and empowerment, particularly in collaborative environments.

speaker: Sachin Monga
text: What if we just ask writers, who do you recommend? What if we just put that in the subscribe flow and just made it as simple as possible?
keySentence: What if we just ask writers, who do you recommend?
text_ko: 작가분들한테 그냥 ‘누구 추천하세요?’라고 물어보면 어떨까요? 그걸 구독 플로우(subscribe flow)에 넣고 최대한 단순하게 만들면 어떨까요?
text_zh: 要不我们直接问作者：“你推荐谁？”然后把这件事放到订阅流程(subscribe flow)里，尽量简化，怎么样？
text_es: ¿Y si simplemente les preguntamos a los escritores: "¿A quién nos recomiendan?" ¿Y si lo incluimos en el flujo de suscripción (subscribe flow) y lo dejamos lo más sencillo posible?
fullContext: Sachin is explaining how Substack's recommendation feature came to be. Rather than building an algorithmic system like Facebook's 'People You May Know', they decided to give writers full control by simply asking them who they recommend. Chris initially worried this approach would be difficult to execute because it required multiple steps - writers opting in, making good choices, and the system generating enough exposure for the recommendations to be meaningful.

vocabulary.definition: To suggest or endorse a course of action, product, or service based on one's judgment or experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, recommending products or services can influence customer decisions and enhance sales strategies, often seen in marketing and customer service interactions.

insight.nuance: While 'recommend' implies a positive endorsement, it should be used carefully to avoid overstepping into manipulation or bias.

vocabulary.definition: A structured process through which users can sign up for a service or content, often involving a series of steps or prompts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, optimizing the subscribe flow is crucial for user acquisition and retention, as it directly impacts conversion rates.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a seamless and user-friendly experience; a poorly designed subscribe flow can deter potential users.

speaker: Sachin Monga
text: My first piece of advice would be to just start it and see what happens. Start it. Have a way to start gathering subscribers. Put a link to it somewhere. Write one or two things.
keySentence: just start it and see what happens.
text_ko: 제 첫 번째 조언은 그냥 시작해 보고 어떻게 되는지 지켜보라는 거예요. 일단 시작하세요. 구독자(subscribers)를 모을 수 있는 방법을 마련해 두고, 어딘가에 링크를 걸어 두세요. 그리고 한두 개 정도 글을 써 보세요.
text_zh: 我的第一个建议就是先开始，别想太多，看看会怎样。先上线，想办法开始拉订阅者(subscribers)。把链接放到某个地方，先写一两篇内容就行。
text_es: Mi primer consejo sería: simplemente ponlo en marcha y ve qué pasa. Ponlo en marcha. Ten alguna forma de empezar a captar suscriptores. Pon un enlace en algún sitio. Escribe una o dos cosas.
fullContext: Lenny asks what advice Sachin has for writers thinking about starting a newsletter or joining Substack. Sachin emphasizes the importance of simply beginning rather than overthinking the process. He suggests that people experiment with different content formats and leverage any existing audience they might have on other platforms, viewing it as a way to gain more control over their relationship with their audience.

vocabulary.definition: The act of collecting or assembling items, people, or information together for a specific purpose.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, gathering often refers to the collection of data, feedback, or resources necessary for decision-making or project development.

insight.nuance: While 'gathering' can imply a casual collection, in a business context it often suggests a structured approach to collecting valuable insights or resources.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or entities that have opted to receive regular updates, content, or services from a provider, often in exchange for a fee or free of charge.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, subscribers are crucial for building a customer base and generating revenue through subscription models or newsletters.

insight.nuance: The term 'subscribers' carries a connotation of commitment, suggesting that these individuals have a vested interest in the content or services offered.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: You get the name and you say, "Great, can you make me an e-intro? Actually even better. Can you connect me over text?" So one tip that I have for all founders, all sales leaders, everyone out there, stop using email.
keySentence: stop using email.
text_ko: 이름을 받으면 "좋아요, 저한테 e-인트로(e-intro) 만들어주실 수 있어요? 아, 사실 더 좋은 건 문자(text)로 바로 연결해주실 수 있어요?"라고 말하죠. 그래서 창업자분들, 영업 리더분들, 그리고 모든 분들께 드리는 팁 하나예요 — 이메일(email)은 이제 그만 쓰세요.
text_zh: 你拿到名字就会说：“太好了，能帮我发个引荐邮件(e-intro)吗？其实更好的是，你能发条短信把我们连上吗？” 我给所有创始人、销售负责人和所有人的建议是：别再发电子邮件(email)了。
text_es: Te pasan el nombre y dices: "Genial, ¿me haces una presentación por correo electrónico (e-intro)? Mejor aún, ¿puedes conectarme por mensaje de texto (text)?" Un consejo para fundadores, líderes de ventas y cualquiera que esté ahí fuera: dejen de usar el correo electrónico (email).
fullContext: Lenny asks Sahil for tactical advice on closing deals during turbulent market conditions. Sahil is explaining his strategy for leveraging existing customers to get warm introductions to new prospects. He emphasizes that instead of just collecting names of potential customers from existing clients, salespeople should push for immediate text message introductions rather than traditional email introductions, arguing that email creates friction while text messages create urgency and accountability.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: setting up a really conservative plan and then having milestones, short term milestones that unlock the ability to lean into growth and spend based on hitting those targets.
keySentence: Set a conservative plan with milestones to lean into growth despite limited visibility.
text_ko: 처음엔 아주 보수적으로 계획을 세우고, 단기 마일스톤(short-term milestones)을 설정해 두어서 그 목표들(targets)을 달성할 때마다 성장에 더 과감하게 투자하고 지출할 수 있는 여지를 만들어둬요.
text_zh: 先做个很保守的计划，然后定几个里程碑( milestones )，主要是短期的；只有达标了，才放手去投入、花钱推动增长。
text_es: Empezar con un plan muy conservador y fijar hitos a corto plazo que, cuando se cumplen, permiten apostar por el crecimiento (lean into growth) e invertir más en función de esos objetivos.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sahil about how founders should approach forecasting and quota setting during uncertain market conditions. Sahil has just shared data showing that 76% of companies missed their Q3 targets and over 80% are expected to miss Q4 goals. He's explaining his recommended approach to planning for 2023 when traditional forecasting becomes nearly impossible due to market volatility and limited visibility into future performance.

vocabulary.definition: A conservative plan is a strategy that prioritizes caution and risk aversion, often involving minimal investment or aggressive growth projections.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a conservative plan is often employed to ensure stability and sustainability, particularly in uncertain market conditions or during initial stages of a project.

insight.nuance: This term suggests a preference for safety over boldness, making it suitable for discussions about risk management but potentially viewed as overly cautious in dynamic environments.

vocabulary.definition: Milestones are specific, measurable goals or checkpoints that mark significant progress in a project or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management, milestones help teams track progress, assess performance, and make necessary adjustments to stay on schedule.

insight.nuance: While milestones indicate progress, they can also imply pressure to meet deadlines, making them a double-edged sword in project discussions.

vocabulary.definition: To lean into growth means to actively embrace and pursue opportunities for expansion and development, often by reallocating resources or increasing investment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, leaning into growth is a proactive approach that encourages companies to capitalize on favorable market conditions or emerging trends.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of optimism and readiness to take calculated risks, making it ideal for discussions about strategic planning and investment.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: Sales comp plans are stuck in the stone ages. They're stuck in the world of Glengarry Glen Ross, Boiler Room, Wolf of Wall Street, get the dollar in through the door.
keySentence: Sales comp plans are stuck in the stone ages, failing to align needs and incentives.
text_ko: 영업 보상 플랜(sales comp plans)이 아직 석기시대에 머물러 있어요. 마치 Glengarry Glen Ross, Boiler Room, Wolf of Wall Street 같은 영화 속 세계에 갇혀서 ‘일단 돈만 들여오면 된다’ 식이에요.
text_zh: 现在的销售提成方案还停留在石器时代，活在那种《格伦加里·格伦·罗斯》(Glengarry Glen Ross)、《锅炉房》(Boiler Room)、《华尔街之狼》(The Wolf of Wall Street)式的世界，思路就是先把钱弄进来（get the dollar in through the door）。
text_es: Los planes de compensación de ventas siguen en la Edad de Piedra. Son los mismos que en Glengarry Glen Ross, Boiler Room o El lobo de Wall Street: lo que importa es cerrar la venta a toda costa.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sahil about compensation plans for salespeople during the current market downturn. Sahil has just explained how traditional sales compensation rewards short-term revenue generation without considering customer retention or long-term value. He argues that sales compensation plans haven't evolved to match modern business priorities, particularly the recent shift from growth-at-all-costs to sustainable, profitable growth with high retention rates.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: So something interesting we saw is that from November until March of last year, companies were basically blowing out their quota, sales reps were blowing out their quota.
keySentence: companies were basically blowing out their quota, sales reps were blowing out their quota.
text_ko: 흥미롭게 본 건, 작년 11월부터 3월까지 회사들이 사실상 쿼터(quota)를 가뿐히 뛰어넘었고, 영업사원들도 쿼터를 훌쩍 초과했다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 有意思的是，我们看到从去年11月到去年3月，公司基本上都在大幅超额完成配额(quota)，销售代表也是一样。
text_es: Algo interesante que vimos es que, de noviembre a marzo del año pasado, las empresas estaban superando con creces sus cuotas (quota) y los representantes de ventas (sales reps) también.
fullContext: Lenny asks about forecasting and quotas during market uncertainty. Sahil is sharing real-time data from Bravado's 300,000-member sales community to illustrate how dramatically and unpredictably market conditions changed throughout 2022. He's explaining the challenge of planning when performance can shift so quickly, as companies went from exceeding targets to missing them within months, making traditional annual forecasting nearly impossible.

vocabulary.definition: A fixed share or portion of a total that is expected to be achieved or produced within a specific timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales, quotas are established to set performance benchmarks for sales representatives, motivating them to meet or exceed targets.

insight.nuance: Quotas can sometimes create pressure, leading to a focus on short-term results rather than long-term customer relationships.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: Take your best sales people and make them CSMs. There's no point. There's no point in having your best salespeople sell. What's the point if people aren't going to buy anyway?
keySentence: There's no point in having your best salespeople sell.
text_ko: 가장 실력 좋은 영업사원들을 고객 성공 매니저(Customer Success Manager, CSM)로 전환하세요. 그들을 계속 영업만 시키는 건 의미가 없어요. 어차피 사람들이 안 살 거라면 최고의 영업사원에게 팔기만 하게 하는 게 무슨 소용이에요?
text_zh: 把你最优秀的销售调去做客户成功经理(CSM)？根本没意义。让最好的销售去卖东西有什么用？客户反正根本不会买。
text_es: Pon a tus mejores comerciales como responsables de éxito del cliente (Customer Success Managers, CSMs). No tiene sentido que tus mejores comerciales sigan vendiendo. ¿Para qué sirve si la gente no va a comprar de todas formas?
fullContext: Lenny asks Sahil about strategies for retaining existing customers during the market downturn. Sahil has just explained that cold outreach response rates are at historic lows and enterprise sales cycles are dramatically longer. He's making his most controversial recommendation - moving top sales talent from new business acquisition to customer success management (CSM) roles, arguing that retaining existing customers is more valuable than pursuing difficult-to-close new deals in the current market.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: You got to change the rules of the game and start to think about the problem differently. I think that not enough founders do that.
keySentence: You got to change the rules of the game and start to think about the problem differently.
text_ko: 판을 바꿔서 문제를 다르게 봐야 해요. 그런데 그렇게 하는 창업가가 충분히 많지 않다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 你得改变游戏规则，换个角度去看问题。我觉得很多创始人还没做到这一点。
text_es: Hay que cambiar las reglas del juego y empezar a verlo de otra manera. Creo que pocos fundadores lo hacen.
fullContext: Lenny asks about the importance of continued growth during tough market conditions. Sahil is explaining how Bravado innovated by creating "Bravado Flex," a commission-only sales model that worked during the downturn when traditional full-time hiring stopped. He's arguing that companies need fundamental innovation rather than minor optimizations when market conditions change dramatically, using his own company's pivot as an example of successful rule-changing.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who establish a company or organization, often responsible for its initial vision, strategy, and operational framework.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, founders are critical in driving innovation, securing funding, and building a company culture that aligns with their vision.

insight.nuance: The term 'founders' carries a sense of entrepreneurial spirit and leadership, but it can also imply a level of responsibility and risk associated with starting a new venture.

speaker: Sahil Mansuri
text: Sales when done well doesn't feel weird, okay? If it ever feels weird, you're a bad salesperson. I've been selling now for 14 years. I've sold literally hundreds, millions of dollars worth of deals.
keySentence: Sales done well doesn't feel weird; if it does, you're a bad salesperson.
text_ko: 영업(sales)은 잘하면 전혀 어색하지 않아요. 어색하게 느껴진다면 그건 영업을 못하는 사람이 하는 방식이에요. 저는 14년째 영업을 해왔고, 실제로 수백 건, 수백만 달러 규모의 거래(deals)를 성사시켰어요.
text_zh: 做好了的销售一点也不会让人觉得别扭，懂吗？要是你觉得别扭，那说明你不是个好销售。我做销售已经14年了，真的是卖过上百单，成交额加起来有好几百万美元。
text_es: Vender, cuando lo haces bien, no tiene por qué sentirse raro, ¿vale? Si alguna vez te parece raro, eres un mal vendedor. Llevo 14 años vendiendo. He vendido literalmente cientos de millones de dólares en tratos.
fullContext: Lenny asks for more tactical advice on closing deals during difficult market conditions. Sahil is about to tell the story of how he sold to Facebook at Glassdoor, but first he's establishing his philosophy that great salespeople build genuine friendships, not just transactional relationships. He's explaining that successful sales should feel natural and valuable to both parties, setting up the context for his Facebook story which demonstrates this principle in action.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: I really enjoy things at the intersection of hilarious and useful. You kind of need both. And hilarious just because you should have fun in life. We should be working on things that are fun and interesting.
keySentence: I really enjoy things at the intersection of hilarious and useful.
text_ko: 저는 웃기면서도 쓸모 있는 것들에 정말 끌려요. 둘 다 필요하거든요. 그리고 웃긴 건 인생에서 즐거움을 느껴야 하니까요. 우리는 재미있고 흥미로운 일들을 해야 해요.
text_zh: 我特别喜欢那种既好笑又实用的东西，两个都得有。好笑这点很重要——人生总得有点乐子。我们应该做的，是那些既好玩又有意义的事。
text_es: Me encantan las cosas que son a la vez divertidas y útiles. Se necesitan ambas. Y lo divertido, porque hay que disfrutar la vida. Deberíamos trabajar en cosas que sean divertidas e interesantes.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sam why he decided to focus on teaching proper etiquette and why people should pay attention to this topic. Sam explains his philosophy for choosing projects - he looks for things that are both entertaining and practically valuable. He believes that in today's noisy information environment, humor is essential for getting people's attention, but it must be paired with genuine utility to have lasting impact.

vocabulary.definition: The point or area where two or more things meet or cross each other.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'intersection' often refers to the convergence of different ideas, markets, or disciplines that can lead to innovative solutions or products.

insight.nuance: While it can imply a physical crossing, in a business context it often suggests a blending of concepts or strategies that can create unique opportunities.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: Understanding how to meet people, where they're at, build trust, mirror kind of expected behaviors. These are all tools. And so that's the deep truth. The shallow truth is it's kind of funny to teach Silicon Valley people etiquette.
keySentence: Meeting people where they're at builds trust and mirrors expected behaviors.
text_ko: 사람들을 어떻게 만나고, 그들이 어떤 상태인지 파악하고, 신뢰를 쌓고, 상대가 기대하는 행동을 맞춰 보여 주는 법을 이해하는 것 — 이 모든 게 도구예요. 그게 진짜 핵심이에요. 반면에 겉으로 보이는 얘기는 실리콘밸리 사람들에게 예절(etiquette)을 가르치는 게 좀 웃기다는 거예요.
text_zh: 要懂得怎么结识别人、了解他们处在哪儿、建立信任，并按对方期望的方式表现自己——这些都是工具。这才是更深层的道理。表面上看，教硅谷 (Silicon Valley) 的人礼仪 (etiquette) 有点好笑。
text_es: Saber cómo conectar con la gente, en qué punto están, generar confianza y reflejar los comportamientos que esperan. Todo eso son herramientas. Esa es la verdad de fondo. La verdad superficial es que resulta un poco curioso enseñar etiqueta a la gente de Silicon Valley.
fullContext: Sam continues explaining why etiquette matters for founders in 2025. He argues that as technology becomes more central to business and people worry about job displacement, understanding social skills becomes crucial for building trust with partners and customers. He contrasts the 'deep truth' (etiquette genuinely matters for business success) with the 'shallow truth' (it's amusing to teach etiquette to tech people who've traditionally dismissed social conventions).

vocabulary.definition: To establish a reliable and dependable relationship based on honesty and integrity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, building trust is essential for fostering strong partnerships, enhancing team collaboration, and improving customer loyalty.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies a gradual process that requires consistent actions and transparency over time.

vocabulary.definition: Actions or conduct that are anticipated or deemed appropriate in a given context or environment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, understanding expected behaviors helps employees align with company culture and enhances team dynamics.

insight.nuance: This term often carries an implication of social norms and may vary significantly across different cultures or organizations.

vocabulary.definition: The customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, understanding etiquette is vital for maintaining professionalism and fostering respectful interactions among colleagues and clients.

insight.nuance: This term often conveys a sense of formality and can vary widely between cultures, making it important to be culturally aware.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: You're at the Kleiner Perkins holiday party. You have all the venture capitalists in the world and all the CEOs. You're at your first company, you're young, maybe you're from a different country. You're like, 'Oh my God, this is my shot.
keySentence: Oh my God, this is my shot.
text_ko: 클라이너 퍼킨스(Kleiner Perkins) 연말 파티에 와 있어요. 세상에 있는 모든 벤처 투자자들과 수많은 CEO들이 한자리에 모여 있죠. 당신은 첫 회사에 다니는 젊은 직원이고, 어쩌면 다른 나라에서 온 사람일 수도 있어요. 그래서 ‘오 마이 갓, 이게 내 기회다!’라고 생각하게 돼요.
text_zh: 你在 Kleiner Perkins 的年终派对上，全世界的风险投资人(venture capitalists)和各种 CEO(CEOs) 都在场。你那会儿还在第一家公司，年纪轻，可能来自别的国家。你会想，天哪，这是我的机会。
text_es: Estás en la fiesta de fin de año de Kleiner Perkins. Tienes a todos los capitalistas de riesgo (venture capitalists) y a todos los CEOs del mundo. Estás en tu primera empresa, eres joven y quizá seas de otro país. Y piensas: «¡Dios mío, ésta es mi oportunidad!»
fullContext: Sam describes a scenario where a young founder attends a high-profile networking event filled with important investors and executives. He explains how the pressure and excitement can cause someone to approach networking in the wrong way - being overly eager and transactional rather than building genuine relationships. The 'energizer bunny' reference describes someone who is hyperactive and overwhelming in social situations.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or firms that invest in startup companies and small businesses with high growth potential in exchange for equity or convertible debt.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, venture capitalists provide essential funding that allows companies to scale quickly and innovate, often taking on significant risks in the process.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a focus on high-risk, high-reward investments, and is typically used in discussions about funding rounds and investment strategies.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: I think understanding how to show up, take a beat, come in with a mindset, not of scarcity, but of abundance, understand how to give more than you take, understand how to build a relationship, not collect business cards.
keySentence: Adopt an abundance mindset to give more than you take and build relationships.
text_ko: 저는 어떻게 나서야 할지, 한 박자 쉬어가며 부족함의 마인드셋(scarcity mindset)이 아니라 풍요의 마인드셋(abundance mindset)으로 접근하는 법을 알고, 받는 것보다 더 많이 주는 법을 알고, 명함을 수집하는 게 아니라 관계를 쌓는 법을 아는 게 중요하다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 我觉得关键在于你怎么出场：先缓一缓，调整心态，不要带着匮乏心态(scarcity)，而是带着丰盛心态(abundance)。要懂得先给出价值，多付出而不是只想着拿，是真正去建立关系，而不是在收集名片。
text_es: Creo que se trata de saber presentarte: tomarte un momento y acercarte con una mentalidad de abundancia, no de escasez; dar más de lo que recibes y buscar construir relaciones, no coleccionar tarjetas de visita.
fullContext: Sam continues his advice about networking events, contrasting the wrong approach with the right one. Instead of desperately trying to extract value from every interaction, he advocates for an abundance mindset - believing there will be more opportunities and focusing on building genuine relationships rather than just gathering contacts. 'Take a beat' means to pause and calm yourself before entering a social situation.

vocabulary.definition: A mindset refers to a set of beliefs or attitudes that shape how an individual thinks and behaves. It influences decision-making and problem-solving approaches.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a positive mindset can foster innovation and resilience, enabling teams to adapt to challenges and pursue opportunities effectively.

insight.nuance: While often associated with a growth-oriented perspective, 'mindset' can also imply rigidity in thinking, so it's important to specify the type of mindset being referenced.

vocabulary.definition: Abundance refers to a plentiful quantity or a mindset characterized by the belief that there are ample resources available to achieve goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, an abundance mindset encourages collaboration and sharing of resources, which can lead to greater innovation and partnership opportunities.

insight.nuance: This term often contrasts with scarcity, and using it can evoke a sense of optimism and potential, making it suitable for motivational discussions.

vocabulary.definition: To build a relationship means to establish and develop a connection or rapport with others over time, often based on trust and mutual benefit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, building relationships is crucial for networking, partnerships, and customer loyalty, as it fosters collaboration and long-term success.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the importance of genuine interaction over superficial connections, making it ideal for discussions on networking strategies.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: I'd also say that, look, this goes back to technical differentiation where things are at.
keySentence: this goes back to technical differentiation where things are at.
text_ko: 저도 그렇게 말하고 싶어요. 결국 이건 기술적 차별화(technical differentiation), 즉 지금 상황이 어떤지에 달려 있어요.
text_zh: 我还想说，这又回到技术差异化(technical differentiation)的问题——看现在到底到了哪一步。
text_es: Yo también diría que, mira, esto nos remite a la diferenciación técnica (technical differentiation) y en qué punto están las cosas.
fullContext: Lenny asks whether someone can be successful without knowing etiquette rules, and Sam acknowledges this is possible in rare cases. He uses the biblical reference 'manna from heaven' (meaning an unexpected gift or blessing) to describe startups that create something so revolutionary that social skills become irrelevant. However, he emphasizes this applies to very few companies - those that build truly groundbreaking products like Google.

vocabulary.definition: Technical differentiation refers to the unique features or capabilities of a product or service that set it apart from competitors. It emphasizes the distinct technological aspects that provide a competitive advantage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in technology and startups, technical differentiation is crucial for attracting customers and investors by showcasing how a product solves problems more effectively than others in the market.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in discussions about innovation and product development, and it implies a level of sophistication that may not be present in more generic offerings.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: You kind of want to show up with the self-confidence and the calm of abundance, being like, 'This is not going to be my only opportunity. This is an opportunity. I'm excited to be here. I'm engaged. This is part of the story.
keySentence: Show up with the calm of abundance; this is part of the story.
text_ko: 어떻게 보면 당당하면서도 넉넉함에서 오는 차분함을 가지고 나타나는 게 좋아요. "이건 제 유일한 기회가 아니에요. 그냥 하나의 기회예요. 여기 오게 되어 기대돼요. 적극적으로 참여하고 있어요. 이건 제 이야기의 일부예요."
text_zh: 你要带着自信和从容不迫的底气出场，心里想着：这不会是我唯一的机会。这只是一个机会。我很高兴能来，也很投入——这只是我这段经历的一部分。
text_es: Lo ideal es que te presentes con la confianza y la tranquilidad de quien sabe que hay más oportunidades, como si dijeras: "Esto no va a ser mi única oportunidad. Es una oportunidad. Me entusiasma estar aquí. Estoy presente y comprometido. Forma parte de mi historia."
fullContext: Sam explains how to mentally approach important networking opportunities or meetings. Rather than treating each interaction as a make-or-break moment (like the Eminem song lyric 'one shot, one opportunity'), he advises projecting confidence that comes from believing you'll have future chances. This abundance mindset helps you stay calm and build better relationships because you're not desperately trying to extract maximum value from every single interaction.

vocabulary.definition: The belief in one's own abilities and judgment; a sense of assurance that one can handle challenges effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, self-confidence is crucial for leadership, decision-making, and effective communication, as it influences how individuals present ideas and negotiate.

insight.nuance: While self-confidence is generally positive, excessive self-confidence can lead to arrogance, which may alienate colleagues or clients.

vocabulary.definition: A favorable circumstance or situation that presents a chance for advancement or progress.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, recognizing and seizing opportunities is essential for growth, innovation, and competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a temporary window for action, suggesting that opportunities should be acted upon promptly to avoid missing out.

vocabulary.definition: Being actively involved or participating in an activity or process; showing commitment and interest.
vocabulary.businessContext: Employee engagement is a key metric in organizations, reflecting how invested workers are in their roles and the overall mission of the company.

insight.nuance: While 'engaged' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply a level of obligation or pressure to perform, depending on the context.

speaker: Sam Lessin
text: The reality is etiquette ironically matters a lot. There is a deep truth to this. Especially when you're asking people to trust you with their data, trust you with their business.
keySentence: Etiquette ironically matters a lot, especially when asking for trust with data.
text_ko: 사실 에티켓(etiquette)은 의외로 정말 중요해요. 이 말에는 중요한 진실이 담겨 있어요. 특히 사람들이 자신의 데이터(data)나 비즈니스(business)를 믿고 맡기게 하려면 더더욱 그렇죠.
text_zh: 说实话，礼节反而很重要，这话里有很深的道理。尤其是当你要别人信任你，把他们的数据(data)和业务(business)交给你时。
text_es: La realidad es que, irónicamente, las formas importan mucho. Hay una verdad profunda detrás de esto. Sobre todo cuando les pides a tus clientes que te confíen sus datos y su negocio.
fullContext: Sam makes his core argument for why etiquette has become crucial for modern founders and tech professionals. As technology has moved from being a niche interest to something that affects everyone's livelihood, the stakes have gotten much higher. When you're asking people to trust you with sensitive business data or critical systems, your social presentation and trustworthiness become essential factors in their decision-making process.

vocabulary.definition: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, etiquette encompasses professional conduct, communication norms, and the respectful treatment of colleagues and clients, which can significantly impact relationships and trust.

insight.nuance: While etiquette is often associated with formal settings, it is equally important in informal interactions, as it reflects one's professionalism and respect for others.

vocabulary.definition: Trust is a firm belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, trust is foundational for building strong relationships with clients, partners, and employees, influencing collaboration and loyalty.

insight.nuance: Trust can be fragile and is often built over time through consistent actions and transparency; it is essential to maintain it to foster a positive business environment.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: I call these why-not questions. People ask these why-not questions a lot.
keySentence: I call these why-not questions.
text_ko: 저는 이런 걸 '왜 안 돼요?'라는 질문들(why-not questions)이라고 불러요. 사람들이 그런 질문을 정말 많이 해요.
text_zh: 我把这类问题叫“为什么不”问题（why-not questions）。很多人都会这么问。
text_es: Yo las llamo preguntas "¿por qué no?" (why-not questions). La gente las hace con mucha frecuencia.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sam about disruptive innovation and why it's important to him. Sam explains that everything new feels threatening at first, and people react with either acceptance or rejection. He describes how people who aren't ready to receive a new innovation will ask 'why-not' questions - essentially finding reasons why the innovation won't work rather than considering its potential.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: I think the more interesting ones are the what-if questions, like, what if this does work? Just use your imagination. Think about, how far can I extend the curve? What are the implications of that? I'm an engineer, and engineers are fundamentally pessimistic people.
keySentence: What-if questions extend the curve of imagination despite engineers' fundamentally pessimistic nature.
text_ko: 더 흥미로운 건 '만약에' 질문들(what-if questions)인 것 같아요. 예를 들어, 이게 실제로 된다면 어떨까요? 그냥 상상해 보세요. 이 곡선을 얼마나 더 확장할 수 있을까요(extend the curve)? 그게 어떤 의미를 갖게 될까요? 저는 엔지니어고, 엔지니어들은 근본적으로 비관적인 사람들이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得更有意思的是那些假设性的问题，比如说，要是这个真的行得通呢？发挥一下想象力嘛。想想看，这个增长曲线我能推多远？这会带来什么影响？我是工程师出身，我们工程师骨子里都是悲观主义者。
text_es: Creo que las más interesantes son las preguntas de "¿y si...?", como ¿y si esto sí funciona? Solo usa tu imaginación. Piensa en hasta dónde puedes estirar la curva. ¿Cuáles son las implicaciones de eso? Soy ingeniero, y los ingenieros somos básicamente gente pesimista.
fullContext: Sam contrasts 'why-not' questions with 'what-if' questions when evaluating new technologies or innovations. He explains that instead of focusing on why something might fail, it's more valuable to imagine what would happen if it succeeds and to think about extending the possibilities. Sam notes that engineers tend to be naturally pessimistic, always looking at problems to solve.

vocabulary.definition: Implications refer to the possible effects or consequences that may arise from a particular action, decision, or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, understanding the implications of a decision is crucial for strategic planning and risk management.

insight.nuance: While often used to denote negative consequences, implications can also refer to positive outcomes, making it important to clarify the context.

vocabulary.definition: Fundamentally means in a basic or essential way; it refers to the core principles or underlying aspects of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, discussing something fundamentally often involves addressing core values, principles, or the foundational aspects of a strategy or product.

insight.nuance: This term can imply a deep-seated belief or characteristic, so it is often used to emphasize the importance of foundational elements in discussions.

vocabulary.definition: To extend means to increase the length, range, or scope of something; it can also refer to making something last longer.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, extending a product line or service offering can be a strategy for growth and market expansion.

insight.nuance: While often used in a positive context of growth, extending can also imply stretching resources or capabilities beyond their limits.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: It's much better to be optimistic and wrong than pessimistic and right, I think. So I don't know. And I'm an impatient person. I'm a creative person. I'm a messy person. I just like to create and explore and find stuff.
keySentence: Being optimistic and wrong seems natural to a messy person like me.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 틀리더라도 낙관적인 편이 맞아도 비관적인 것보다 훨씬 낫다고 봐요. 그래서 잘 모르겠어요. 저는 좀 성격이 급하고, 창의적인 사람이고, 정리정돈은 잘 못해요. 그냥 만들고 탐구하고 새로운 걸 찾아내는 걸 좋아해요.
text_zh: 我觉得，宁可乐观但错，也不要悲观却对。说实话我也说不准。我比较没耐心，是个有创造力、做事有点乱的人。我就喜欢创造、折腾、去探索、去发现新东西。
text_es: Creo que es mucho mejor ser optimista y equivocarse que ser pesimista y tener razón. No lo sé. Soy una persona impaciente, creativa y algo desordenada; simplemente me gusta crear, explorar y descubrir cosas.
fullContext: Sam shares his philosophy on optimism versus pessimism in innovation. He argues that there's not much reward for being pessimistic and correct, especially in moments of significant technological change. Sam describes his personal approach to innovation, explaining that his impatient and creative nature naturally leads him toward disruptive innovation work.

vocabulary.definition: Having a hopeful and positive outlook on future outcomes or situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an optimistic approach can drive innovation and motivate teams to pursue ambitious goals, even in uncertain environments.

insight.nuance: While optimism can foster creativity and resilience, excessive optimism may lead to underestimating risks or challenges.

vocabulary.definition: Having a negative or doubtful outlook on future outcomes or situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a pessimistic attitude may hinder decision-making and stifle innovation, as it often focuses on potential failures rather than opportunities.

insight.nuance: While a degree of pessimism can be useful for risk assessment, excessive pessimism can lead to missed opportunities and a lack of motivation.

vocabulary.definition: To investigate, examine, or analyze something in depth to gain new insights or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, exploring new markets, technologies, or ideas is vital for identifying opportunities and driving growth.

insight.nuance: Exploration often implies a willingness to take risks and venture into the unknown, which can be both rewarding and challenging.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: Every new idea looks dumb at first. Unfortunately, the dumb ideas also look dumb at first. It's not a perfect [inaudible]. But the more disruptive they are, the more dumb you're going to feel they are.
keySentence: Every new idea looks dumb at first, especially disruptive ones.
text_ko: 새로운 아이디어는 처음엔 다 어리석어 보여요. 안타깝게도 진짜 어리석은 아이디어들도 처음엔 똑같이 어리석어 보이고요. 이건 완벽한 판별법은 아니에요. 다만, 그 아이디어가 더 파괴적(disruptive)일수록 더 어리석게 느껴질 거예요.
text_zh: 每个新点子刚出来都显得很傻。不幸的是，确实很蠢的点子起初也看起来一样。这个判断并不完美。但越有颠覆性的（disruptive）点子，起初你就越会觉得它们很傻。
text_es: Toda idea nueva parece una tontería al principio. Y, lamentablemente, las ideas realmente malas también parecen tonterías al principio. No es una regla perfecta. Pero cuanto más disruptivas (disruptive) sean, más ridículas te van a parecer.
fullContext: Lenny discusses first-principles thinking and mentions Steve Jobs' quote about everything being designed by people no smarter than you. Sam responds by explaining that truly innovative ideas often appear foolish initially, though he acknowledges this isn't a perfect filter since bad ideas also look dumb. He suggests listening for specific dismissive language like 'toy' as potential indicators of disruptive innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Causing significant change or disturbance in an industry or market, often by introducing a new product or service that displaces established competitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'disruptive' often refers to innovations that create new markets and value networks, ultimately displacing existing market leaders.

insight.nuance: While 'disruptive' generally has a positive connotation in innovation contexts, it can also imply negative consequences for established players.

vocabulary.definition: Concepts or proposals that are initially perceived as impractical, unfeasible, or lacking merit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and innovation, what may seem like 'dumb ideas' can sometimes lead to breakthrough innovations if pursued with the right mindset.

insight.nuance: While often dismissed, 'dumb ideas' can serve as a catalyst for creative thinking and should not be overlooked in brainstorming sessions.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: And that bifurcation of love it, hate it, is really how you have an idea of whether you have impact in what you're building.
keySentence: that bifurcation of love it, hate it, is really how you have an idea of whether you have impact
text_ko: 그리고 사람들이 '좋아해' 아니면 '싫어해'로 갈라지는 그 분기(bifurcation)가 바로 당신이 만드는 것이 실제로 영향력(impact)이 있는지 판단하는 방법이에요.
text_zh: 用户要么很爱要么很讨厌——这种两极分化，恰好能让你判断自己在做的东西有没有影响力。
text_es: Que la gente lo ame o lo odie te da una idea clara de si lo que estás construyendo está teniendo impacto.
fullContext: Sam explains how to identify whether a product is truly disruptive by observing people's reactions to it. He describes how Google Docs created a strong binary reaction - some people loved it intensely while others wanted it to fail completely. This bifurcation (split) of reactions, rather than moderate responses across a bell curve, indicates genuine disruption and impact.

vocabulary.definition: The division of something into two branches or parts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, bifurcation can refer to the splitting of a market or product line into two distinct categories, often to target different customer segments more effectively.

insight.nuance: Bifurcation often implies a significant decision point or a strategic choice that can lead to divergent paths.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that something has on a situation or person.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, impact is often used to measure the effectiveness of a product, service, or initiative on stakeholders and the market.

insight.nuance: Impact can carry a positive or negative connotation depending on the context, emphasizing the importance of understanding the outcomes of business decisions.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: I think products almost follow these thermodynamic rules where if you add a little bit of value, your adoption goes slowly and if you add a lot of value, your adoption goes really quickly, right?
keySentence: if you add a lot of value, your adoption goes really quickly
text_ko: 제 생각엔 제품들도 거의 이런 열역학 법칙(thermodynamic rules)을 따르는 것 같아요. 가치를 조금만 더하면 도입(adoption)이 천천히 늘고, 많이 더하면 훨씬 빠르게 늘어요, 그렇죠?
text_zh: 我觉得产品差不多也遵循那套热力学规律(thermodynamic rules)：你只增加一点点价值，用户采纳会很慢；一旦你增加很多价值，采纳速度就会飞快，对吧？
text_es: Creo que los productos tienden a obedecer estas leyes termodinámicas (thermodynamic rules): si aportas poco valor, la adopción (adoption) va despacio; si aportas mucho valor, la adopción se dispara, ¿no?
fullContext: Sam discusses the principle that people are lazy and only adopt products that make their lives significantly easier. He explains that product adoption follows patterns similar to thermodynamic rules - small amounts of added value lead to slow adoption, while substantial value creation results in rapid, explosive growth. He uses ChatGPT as an example of a product that added tremendous value and achieved explosive adoption.

vocabulary.definition: The act of accepting or starting to use something new, such as a product or technology.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'adoption' refers to the rate at which consumers or organizations begin to use a new product or service, often influenced by its perceived value and usability.

insight.nuance: While 'adoption' can imply a positive acceptance, it may also carry the connotation of a gradual process rather than immediate uptake.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something, often measured in terms of benefits it provides to users or customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'value' is crucial as it determines how much customers are willing to pay for a product or service and influences their purchasing decisions.

insight.nuance: The term 'value' can also imply subjective perceptions, varying significantly among different customer segments or markets.

speaker: Sam Schillace
text: We tend to undervalue the things we're good at. We tend to think work has to be unpleasant. And so if something is easy and fun, we don't tend to think it's valuable.
keySentence: We tend to undervalue easy and fun work, gravitating towards unpleasant tasks.
text_ko: 우리는 잘하는 것들의 가치를 과소평가하는 경향이 있어요. 일은 힘들어야 한다고 생각하는 편이죠. 그래서 뭔가 쉽고 재미있으면 그게 가치 있다고 잘 안 느껴져요.
text_zh: 我们常常低估自己擅长的事情，总觉得工作就该辛苦。所以一旦某件事既简单又有趣，我们往往就觉得它没什么价值。
text_es: Solemos no valorar lo que se nos da bien. También pensamos que el trabajo tiene que ser duro. Por eso, si algo es fácil y divertido, no lo consideramos valioso.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Sam's philosophy on career success and taking risks. Sam explains a common misconception people have about work - that it must be difficult and unpleasant to be valuable. He argues that people often undervalue their natural talents and gravitate toward grinding through unpleasant work, thinking this is the path to career success, when actually they should focus on what comes easily and enjoyably to them.

vocabulary.definition: To regard something as less important or less valuable than it actually is.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, undervaluing skills or contributions can lead to missed opportunities for innovation and employee engagement.

insight.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of appreciation or recognition.

vocabulary.definition: Having worth or significance, often in terms of monetary, practical, or intellectual benefits.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, valuable assets can include intellectual property, skilled personnel, and innovative products that drive competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: While often associated with monetary value, 'valuable' can also refer to intangible qualities like employee morale or brand reputation.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: My biggest advice to people is, oftentimes the analysis paralysis of dotting every eye, crossing every tee sometimes chokes you out of opportunities. When you find something that gives you energy, just jump in with both feet.
keySentence: Analysis paralysis chokes you out of opportunities; jump in with both feet.
text_ko: 제일 드리고 싶은 조언은, 모든 걸 다 맞추려고 하다 보면 분석 마비(analysis paralysis)에 걸려 기회를 놓치는 경우가 많다는 거예요. 어떤 일이 나한테 에너지를 주고 해보고 싶다는 생각이 들면, 망설이지 말고 과감히 두 발로 뛰어들어요.
text_zh: 我给大家最重要的建议就是，有时候你把每个细节都分析得过于透彻，反而会错失良机。当你发现某个事情能让你充满干劲的时候，就别犹豫了，直接全身心投入进去。
text_es: Mi mejor consejo es que muchas veces el quedarse paralizado analizando cada detalle hasta el cansancio te hace perder oportunidades increíbles. Cuando encuentres algo que te llene de energía, lánzate de cabeza sin pensarlo tanto.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sanchan for advice on how someone starting out could follow a similar trajectory to work at incredible companies like Instagram, Airbnb, and Coinbase. Sanchan reflects on his own career path, noting that he never had a detailed plan but instead stumbled upon opportunities. He emphasizes that over-planning can prevent people from seizing opportunities when they arise.

vocabulary.definition: A state of overthinking or excessive deliberation that prevents decision-making or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, analysis paralysis can hinder progress on projects or initiatives, as teams may become bogged down in details rather than moving forward with implementation.

insight.nuance: This phrase often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that excessive caution can lead to missed opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Favorable circumstances or situations that present the potential for advancement or success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, opportunities can refer to market openings, partnership possibilities, or new avenues for growth that organizations can capitalize on.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a sense of urgency or the need for proactive engagement to take advantage of the situation.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: You take little bets, you try them out. If they don't work out, you build rapid recovery and start to do something else. And that is the meta story connecting all the dots in my life, in all the career opportunities that I've had.
keySentence: Little bets and rapid recovery connect all the dots in my career.
text_ko: 작은 시도(little bets)를 해보고, 잘 안되면 빠른 회복(rapid recovery)을 마련해서 다른 걸 시도해요. 그게 제 인생과 모든 커리어 기회들을 잇는 메타 스토리(meta story)이에요.
text_zh: 你就是要小试牛刀，试着做一些小的尝试。如果不行的话，就赶紧调整过来，换个方向继续干。这其实就是我人生的主线，把我所有的职业机会都串起来的那条线。
text_es: Haces pequeñas apuestas, las pruebas. Si no funcionan, te recuperas rápido y empiezas a hacer otra cosa. Y esa es la historia que conecta todos los puntos de mi vida, en todas las oportunidades profesionales que he tenido.
fullContext: Sanchan continues explaining his career philosophy, referencing a book called 'Little Bets' that validated his approach to life. He describes how taking small risks and quickly recovering from failures has been the underlying theme throughout his career moves from aerospace engineering to startups to major tech companies.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to quickly return to a previous state or condition after experiencing a setback or failure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, rapid recovery is crucial for maintaining momentum after a project fails or a market changes, allowing companies to pivot and adapt swiftly.

insight.nuance: This term often implies not just bouncing back, but doing so in a way that minimizes disruption and maximizes learning from the experience.

vocabulary.definition: Possibilities for professional advancement or employment that align with an individual's skills and aspirations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, career opportunities often arise from networking, skill development, and organizational growth, providing pathways for employees to advance.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a positive connotation, suggesting potential for growth, but may also imply competition among candidates.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: My advice to people is go get a job which will make you the fastest learner in the field of product management. That is what will help you a lot. No course, no degree, none of those things will help.
keySentence: No course, no degree, none of those things will help.
text_ko: 제 조언은 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management) 분야에서 가장 빨리 배우게 해줄 직업을 구하라는 거예요. 그게 정말 큰 도움이 돼요. 어떤 강좌나 학위 같은 건 별로 도움이 되지 않아요.
text_zh: 我的建议是：找一份能让你在产品管理(product management)这个领域学得最快的工作。那才是最有用的。任何课程、任何学位都帮不了你太多。
text_es: Mi consejo: busca un trabajo que te haga aprender lo más rápido posible en el campo de la gestión de producto (product management). Eso es lo que de verdad te va a ayudar. Ningún curso ni ningún título te va a servir.
fullContext: Lenny asks for advice on getting into product management. Sanchan explains that product management requires learning both the art (intuition, community insights) and science (data, methodology) aspects. He emphasizes that formal education can't replace hands-on experience in learning product management skills.

vocabulary.definition: An individual who quickly grasps new concepts and skills, often adapting to new information or environments with ease.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, being the fastest learner is crucial for adapting to rapidly changing markets and technologies, allowing professionals to stay competitive and innovative.

insight.nuance: This phrase often implies not just speed, but also efficiency in understanding and applying knowledge, making it a compliment in professional settings.

vocabulary.definition: A specialized area within business that focuses on the development, marketing, and lifecycle management of products.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, the field of product management is essential for aligning product development with market needs and ensuring successful product launches.

insight.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of expertise and specialization, often used to denote a career path that requires both technical and managerial skills.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: The way to think about this is let's say you want to get to a destination, whichever destination it is, you probably want to get on the faster ship. You don't want to get on a slower ship.
keySentence: Choose the faster ship to reach your destination.
text_ko: 이걸 이렇게 생각해보면, 가고 싶은 목적지가 어디든 보통은 더 빠른 배를 타고 싶어요. 느린 배를 타고 싶지는 않을 거예요.
text_zh: 可以这么想：比方说你要去某个目的地，不管是哪儿，你肯定会选更快的那艘船，没人会选慢船。
text_es: La forma de verlo es: imagina que quieres llegar a un destino, sea cual sea. Probablemente prefieras ir en el barco más rápido; no en uno más lento.
fullContext: Lenny asks what people should look for when choosing a company to join to accelerate their learning and career. Sanchan uses a ship metaphor to explain how to think about company selection - you want to join companies that are moving quickly toward success because your career growth is tied to the company's trajectory.

vocabulary.definition: A specific place or goal to which one is traveling or aiming to reach.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'destination' often refers to the ultimate objective of a project, strategy, or customer journey, emphasizing the importance of clear goals.

insight.nuance: The term can carry both literal and figurative meanings, making it suitable for discussions about both physical locations and abstract goals.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: What I found is that at Airbnb, I learned a bunch of different things. One, I learned how to build products where software is just one part of the product. Let me explain that a little bit. The product of Airbnb isn't the app.
keySentence: The product of Airbnb isn't the app.
text_ko: 제가 알게 된 건 에어비앤비에서 정말 여러 가지를 배웠다는 거예요. 먼저, 소프트웨어(software)가 제품의 일부에 불과한 프로덕트(product)를 만드는 법을 배웠어요. 그걸 좀 더 설명해볼게요. 에어비앤비의 프로덕트(product)는 단순한 앱(app)이 아니에요.
text_zh: 我在 Airbnb 学到了很多东西。第一，我学会了怎么把软件（software）只当成产品的一部分来做。让我稍微解释一下：Airbnb 的产品不是那个 app（app）。
text_es: En Airbnb aprendí muchas cosas distintas. Primero, aprendí a crear productos en los que el software (software) es solo una pieza del conjunto. Déjame explicarlo un poco: el producto de Airbnb no es la aplicación (app).
fullContext: Lenny asks where Sanchan learned the most in his career. Sanchan explains that Airbnb taught him the most, particularly how to build products that extend beyond software into real-world experiences. He distinguishes between pure software products and products where software enables a physical experience.

vocabulary.definition: To create or develop items or services that fulfill specific customer needs or solve particular problems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, 'building products' often involves a collaborative process that includes design, engineering, and user feedback to ensure market fit and functionality.

insight.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the active role of teams in the product development lifecycle, distinguishing it from merely selling or marketing existing products.

vocabulary.definition: A collection of instructions, data, or programs that enable a computer or device to perform specific tasks or functions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, software is a fundamental component of products, often serving as the backbone for applications and services that drive user engagement and business operations.

insight.nuance: While 'software' typically refers to digital applications, it can also imply a broader ecosystem of tools and platforms that enhance user experience.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: I felt like it all compressed into three years something that you will learn in 30. I definitely didn't think that is what happened, but that's what ended up happening.
keySentence: Compressed into three years what you learn in 30; crazy, crazy times.
text_ko: 모든 게 30년 동안 배워야 할 걸 3년에 다 압축된 느낌이었어요. 전혀 그렇게 될 줄은 몰랐는데, 결국 그렇게 됐어요.
text_zh: 感觉这三年把本来得花三十年才能学会的东西都压缩了。我当时根本没想到会这样，但最后真就是这样。
text_es: Tuve la sensación de que todo se condensó en tres años: aprendí en ese tiempo lo que normalmente llevaría 30 años. No pensé que fuera a ser así, pero al final fue justo eso.
fullContext: Sanchan describes his learning experience at Airbnb, which included hypergrowth, scaling the product organization from 30-40 people to 200 people, and crisis management during COVID-19 when travel essentially stopped. He reflects on how these compressed experiences provided decades worth of learning in just three years.

vocabulary.definition: Compressed refers to something that has been reduced in size, volume, or duration, often resulting in a denser or more concentrated form.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, compressed timelines or processes can indicate a situation where tasks or learning experiences are significantly shortened, often leading to increased intensity and urgency.

insight.nuance: While 'compressed' can imply efficiency, it may also suggest a lack of thoroughness or depth, making it important to consider the context in which it is used.

speaker: Sanchan Saxena
text: The real genius isn't to dot every eye, to cross every team before you get started. The real genius is, what do you do when shit goes wrong? And I believe rapid recovery is the key to success.
keySentence: The real genius is, what do you do when shit goes wrong?
text_ko: 진짜 영리한 사람은 시작하기 전에 모든 걸 다 완벽하게 해놓으려 하는 사람이 아니에요. 진짜 중요한 건 일이 엉망이 됐을 때 어떻게 대응하느냐예요. 저는 신속한 회복(rapid recovery)이 성공의 핵심이라고 믿어요.
text_zh: 真正的聪明不是在开始前把每个细节都弄得滴水不漏，而是在事情出岔子的时候你怎么应对。我相信，快速恢复才是成功的关键。
text_es: La verdadera genialidad no está en dejar todo impecable ni en revisar cada detalle antes de empezar. Está en saber qué hacer cuando las cosas se tuercen. Creo que recuperarse rápido es la clave del éxito.
fullContext: Sanchan shares lessons from navigating Airbnb through the COVID-19 crisis, when the company had to lay off 1,900 employees and revenue dropped to single digits of the previous year. He explains that success isn't about perfect planning but about how quickly you can adapt and recover when unexpected challenges arise.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to quickly return to a normal state after experiencing a setback or disruption.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, rapid recovery is crucial for minimizing downtime and maintaining operational efficiency after unexpected challenges, such as market fluctuations or technical failures.

insight.nuance: This phrase often conveys a sense of agility and preparedness, suggesting that an organization is resilient and capable of bouncing back swiftly.

vocabulary.definition: A fundamental factor or element that is essential for achieving desired outcomes or goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, identifying the key to success often involves recognizing critical strategies, resources, or practices that drive growth and profitability.

insight.nuance: This phrase implies that while there may be multiple factors contributing to success, there is one or a few that are particularly pivotal.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: AI guardrails do not work. I'm going to say that one more time. Guardrails do not work. If someone is determined enough to trick GPT-5, they're going to deal with that guardrail. No problem.
keySentence: AI guardrails do not work.
text_ko: AI 가드레일(guardrails)은 효과가 없어요. 다시 한 번 말할게요. 가드레일은 효과가 없어요. 누군가 GPT-5를 속일 만큼 결심했다면 그 가드레일을 우회하거나 무력화할 거예요. 문제없어요.
text_zh: AI 那些所谓的安全护栏（guardrails）根本不管用。我再说一遍：安全护栏（guardrails）根本不管用。如果有人铁了心要骗过 GPT-5（GPT-5），他们总能把这些护栏绕过去，完全没问题。
text_es: Las medidas de contención para la IA (AI guardrails) no funcionan. Lo voy a repetir: no funcionan. Si alguien está tan decidido a burlar a GPT‑5, va a saltarse esa medida sin problema.
fullContext: At the opening of this podcast, Sander makes his most provocative statement about AI security. AI guardrails are large language models trained to classify whether inputs and outputs to AI systems are valid or malicious, essentially acting as security filters. Sander, who runs AI red teaming competitions and works with leading AI labs on model defenses, has found through extensive testing that these guardrails are easily bypassed by determined attackers and provide a false sense of security.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: Studies have shown that using bad prompts can get you down to 0% on a problem, and good prompts can boost you up to 90%.
keySentence: Good prompts can boost you up to 90%, while bad ones get you to 0%.
text_ko: 연구에 따르면, 부적절한 프롬프트(bad prompts)를 사용하면 문제 해결률이 0%까지 떨어질 수 있고, 좋은 프롬프트(good prompts)는 해결률을 90%까지 끌어올릴 수 있어요.
text_zh: 研究表明，提示词(prompts)如果用得不好，解决问题的成功率可能降到0%；用得好，成功率可以提升到90%。
text_es: Los estudios han demostrado que usar instrucciones (prompts) pobres puede dejarte en un 0% a la hora de resolver un problema, mientras que unas buenas instrucciones pueden llevarte hasta un 90%.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sander whether prompt engineering is worth investing time in, given that some people believe AI will become so advanced that prompting skills won't matter. Sander argues that prompt engineering remains crucial and provides evidence of its dramatic impact on performance. He addresses the common misconception that each new model release will eliminate the need for good prompting techniques.

vocabulary.definition: To increase or improve something significantly, often in terms of performance or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'boost' is frequently used to describe enhancements in productivity, sales, or user engagement through various strategies or tools.

insight.nuance: While 'boost' conveys a positive increase, it may imply a temporary or artificial enhancement rather than a sustainable change.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: You can patch a bug, but you can't patch a brain. If you find some bug in your software and you go and patch it, you can be maybe 99.99% sure that bug is solved. Try to do that in your AI system.
keySentence: You can patch a bug, but you can't patch a brain with 99.99% surety.
text_ko: 버그는 패치할 수 있지만, 뇌는 패치할 수 없어요. 소프트웨어(software)에서 버그(bug)를 찾아 패치(patch)하면 그 버그가 거의 99.99% 해결됐다고 확신할 수 있어요. 그걸 AI 시스템(AI system)에서 해보세요.
text_es: Puedes parchear un fallo (bug), pero no un cerebro. Si encuentras un fallo en tu software y lo parcheas, puedes estar prácticamente 99,99% seguro de que está solucionado. Intenta hacer eso en tu sistema de IA (AI).
fullContext: Sander explains why AI security is fundamentally different from traditional cybersecurity. In traditional software, when you identify and fix a bug, you can be confident it's permanently resolved. However, AI systems based on neural networks don't work like traditional code - they're more like 'brains' that can be tricked in countless unpredictable ways, making it nearly impossible to definitively solve security vulnerabilities.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: A set of techniques that we call self-criticism. You ask the LLM, "Can you go and check your response?" It outputs something, you get it to criticize itself and then to improve itself.
keySentence: Get it to criticize itself to improve its responses.
text_ko: 우리가 '자기비판(self-criticism)'이라고 부르는 일련의 기법이에요. 대형 언어 모델(LLM)에게 "네 답변을 한 번 확인해 줄래?"라고 물어보고, 모델이 뭔가를 출력하면 그 답을 스스로 비판하게 해서 그 피드백으로 다시 개선하게 만드는 방식이에요.
text_zh: 我们有一套技术叫做自我批评。你问大语言模型(LLM)："你能不能检查一下自己的回答？"它输出内容后，你让它自己找毛病，然后自己改进。
text_es: Un conjunto de técnicas que llamamos autocrítica. Le preguntas al LLM: "¿Puedes revisar tu respuesta?" Genera algo, haces que se critique a sí mismo y después que se mejore.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sander to recommend a few specific prompt engineering techniques that people should start implementing. Sander explains the self-criticism method, where you first get the AI to generate a response, then ask it to review and critique its own work, and finally have it implement those improvements. This is presented as one of his recommended advanced techniques for better AI performance.

vocabulary.definition: Methods or approaches used to accomplish a specific task or achieve a desired outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, techniques refer to systematic methods employed to enhance productivity, solve problems, or innovate processes.

insight.nuance: While 'techniques' can imply a level of skill or expertise, it may also suggest a more mechanical or formulaic approach, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: The act of evaluating one's own performance or behavior critically, often with the aim of improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, self-criticism can foster a culture of continuous improvement and accountability, encouraging employees to reflect on their work and identify areas for growth.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: I found through running these events is that they are terribly, terribly insecure and frankly, they don't work. They just don't work.
keySentence: These events are terribly, terribly insecure and frankly, they don't work.
text_ko: 제가 이런 이벤트들을 직접 운영해 보면서 알게 된 건, 정말 심각하게 불안정하고 솔직히 말해서 제대로 작동하지 않는다는 거예요. 그냥 안 돼요.
text_zh: 我办这些活动下来发现，效果真的是很不稳定，说白了就是不管用。就是不行。
text_es: Lo que descubrí organizando estos eventos es que son terriblemente, pero terriblemente inseguros y, siendo honestos, simplemente no funcionan. No funcionan y ya.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sander about the problem he discovered with AI security defenses. Sander has been running AI red teaming competitions for years, studying various defense mechanisms including AI guardrails. Through these competitions, where teams attempt to break AI systems, he has consistently found that guardrails - which are supposed to detect and block malicious inputs and outputs - are easily defeated by attackers.

vocabulary.definition: Lacking confidence or assurance; uncertain and anxious about oneself or one's abilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being insecure can refer to a lack of confidence in one's decisions, strategies, or the stability of a company, which can hinder effective leadership and innovation.

insight.nuance: While 'insecure' often has a negative connotation, it can also indicate a level of self-awareness that prompts individuals to seek improvement.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: Getting AIs to do or say bad things. So we see people saying things like, "My grandmother used to work as a munitions engineer. She always used to tell me bedtime stories about her work. She recently passed away.
keySentence: My grandmother was a munitions engineer who told me stories about her work.
text_ko: AI에게 유해한 행동을 하거나 유해한 말을 하게 만드는 거예요. 그래서 사람들이 '제 할머니가 예전에 탄약 엔지니어(munitions engineer)로 일하셨어요. 그분은 항상 일에 관한 이야기를 자기 전에 들려주시곤 했어요. 최근에 돌아가셨어요.'라고 말하는 걸 보게 돼요.
text_zh: 让 AI 做或说不当的事情。所以我们会看到有人说类似的话：“我奶奶以前是弹药工程师 (munitions engineer)。她总在睡前给我讲她工作的故事。她最近去世了。”
text_es: Conseguir que las inteligencias artificiales (AIs) hagan o digan cosas malas. Por eso vemos a gente diciendo cosas como: "Mi abuela trabajaba como ingeniera de municiones (munitions engineer). Siempre me contaba historias para dormir sobre su trabajo. Hace poco falleció."
fullContext: Lenny asks Sander to explain what prompt injection and red teaming are. Sander defines it as the practice of tricking AI systems into producing harmful or inappropriate content. He provides a specific example of how attackers use emotional manipulation and storytelling to bypass AI safety measures, demonstrating how seemingly innocent requests can be crafted to elicit dangerous information.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: The number of possible attacks against another LLM is equivalent to the number of possible prompts. Each possible prompt could be an attack. And for a model like GPT-5, the number of possible attacks is one followed by a million zeros.
keySentence: The number of possible attacks is equivalent to one followed by a million zeros.
text_ko: 다른 대형 언어 모델(LLM)을 겨냥한 가능한 공격의 수는 가능한 프롬프트(prompt)의 수와 똑같아요. 가능한 각 프롬프트가 공격이 될 수 있고, GPT-5 같은 모델에서는 그 수가 1 뒤에 0이 백만 개나 붙는 엄청난 수예요.
text_zh: 对另一个LLM的潜在攻击数量，基本上就等于可能的提示词(prompt)数量。每个提示词都有可能成为攻击手段。像GPT-5这种模型，可能的攻击方式简直是天文数字，后面得跟上百万个零。
text_es: El número de posibles ataques contra otro modelo de lenguaje (LLM) es equivalente al número de prompts posibles. Cualquier prompt podría ser un ataque. Y para un modelo como GPT-5, estamos hablando de un número de ataques posibles que es un uno seguido de un millón de ceros.
fullContext: Sander explains why measuring the effectiveness of AI guardrails is fundamentally flawed. When guardrail companies claim they catch "99% of attacks," they're working with a virtually infinite attack space. Since every possible text prompt could potentially be crafted as an attack, the search space for potential exploits is astronomically large - far beyond what any security system can realistically test against or defend.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: It is not a solvable problem. That's one of the things that makes it so different from classical security. If we can't even trust chatbots to be secure, how can we trust agents to go and manage our finances?
keySentence: We can't trust chatbots for security; how can we trust them to go and manage finances?
text_ko: 해결 가능한 문제가 아니에요. 그게 기존의 보안(classical security)과 확연히 다른 점 중 하나예요. 챗봇(chatbot)조차 안전하다고 믿기 어려운데, 에이전트(agent)에게 우리 자금 관리를 맡겨도 믿을 수 있겠어요?
text_zh: 这个问题根本就解决不了。这也是它跟传统安全完全不一样的地方。连聊天机器人(chatbot)我们都信不过，更别说让智能代理(agent)去管我们的钱了，那不是开玩笑吗？
text_es: No es un problema que se pueda resolver. Esa es una de las cosas que lo hace tan diferente de la seguridad clásica. Si ni siquiera podemos confiar en que los chatbots sean seguros, ¿cómo vamos a confiar en que los agentes vayan y manejen nuestras finanzas?
fullContext: Lenny asks whether prompt injection attacks are a solvable problem from the perspective of founders and product teams building AI applications. Sander explains that unlike traditional cybersecurity where you can patch specific bugs, AI security vulnerabilities cannot be completely eliminated. He emphasizes the broader implications for autonomous AI agents that will have real-world capabilities and responsibilities.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: The smartest artificial intelligence researchers in the world are working at Frontier Labs like OpenAI, Google, Anthropic. They can't solve this problem. They haven't been able to solve this problem in the last couple years of large language models being popular.
keySentence: Frontier Labs researchers can't solve this problem with large language models.
text_ko: 세계에서 가장 똑똑한 인공지능 연구자들이 OpenAI, Google, Anthropic 같은 최첨단 연구소에서 일하고 있어요. 그런데 그들도 이 문제를 못 풀고 있어요. 대규모 언어 모델(large language models)이 인기 있었던 지난 몇 년 동안에도 해결하지 못했어요.
text_zh: 全世界最顶尖的AI研究人员都在那些前沿实验室工作，比如OpenAI、谷歌、Anthropic这些公司。连他们都搞不定这个问题。大语言模型(large language models)火了这么几年，他们到现在还是没能解决这个问题。
text_es: Los investigadores de inteligencia artificial más brillantes del mundo están trabajando en laboratorios de vanguardia como OpenAI, Google, Anthropic. Y no han podido resolver este problema. En estos últimos años, con todo el boom de los modelos de lenguaje grandes (large language models), siguen sin encontrarle la vuelta.
fullContext: Sander is explaining why enterprise AI security companies' claims to solve prompt injection and jailbreaking don't make sense. He argues that if the most advanced AI research teams at leading companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic - who have the best researchers and unlimited resources - cannot solve adversarial robustness, it's unrealistic to expect smaller enterprise security companies to have cracked this fundamental problem.

insight.nuance: While AI can imply advanced machine learning capabilities, it is important to specify the type of AI being discussed, as the term can encompass a wide range of technologies from basic automation to sophisticated neural networks.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: We have recognized the need for a similar thing, but with communicating with AIs and understanding the best way to talk to them, understanding what their responses mean, and then how to adapt, I guess, your next prompts to that response.
keySentence: Understand responses to adapt your next prompts effectively when communicating with AIs.
text_ko: 우리는 비슷한 필요성을 인지하고 있어요. 다만 인공지능(AI)과 소통할 때 어떻게 말해야 가장 효과적인지, 그들의 응답(response)이 어떤 의미인지 파악하고 그에 맞춰 다음 프롬프트(prompt)를 어떻게 조정할지 알아야 해요.
text_zh: 我们也意识到需要类似的东西，但是要跟AI沟通，要懂得怎么和它们对话，理解它们回复的意思，然后根据回复来调整你下一轮的提示词(prompts)。
text_es: Nos hemos dado cuenta de que necesitamos algo parecido, pero para comunicarnos con las IAs y entender cuál es la mejor manera de hablarles, entender qué significan sus respuestas, y luego cómo adaptar, digamos, tus siguientes prompts a esa respuesta.
fullContext: Sander explains his concept of "artificial social intelligence" - a term he created to describe the skills needed for effective human-AI communication. Just as social intelligence describes how people communicate with each other, artificial social intelligence encompasses understanding how to communicate with AI systems, interpret their responses, and adapt your approach accordingly. He presents this as evidence that prompt engineering skills remain important despite AI advances.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: There's not an incredible amount of value in just doing AI red teaming. And I suppose there'll be... I don't know if I want to say that. It's possible that there will be less value in just doing classical cybersecurity work.
keySentence: There's not an incredible amount of value in just doing AI red teaming.
text_ko: 그냥 AI 레드팀(AI red teaming)만 하는 것으로는 엄청난 가치가 나오진 않아요. 그리고 이 말을 해도 되나 싶긴 한데요, 어쩌면 전통적인 사이버보안 업무(classical cybersecurity work)만으로 얻는 가치도 줄어들 수 있어요.
text_zh: 光做AI红队测试(AI red teaming)本身，价值其实不大。我也不知道该不该这么说，但光做传统网络安全工作(classical cybersecurity work)的价值可能也会更低。
text_es: No aporta mucho valor limitarse únicamente al red teaming de IA (AI red teaming). Y supongo que... no sé si quiero decirlo, pero puede que también haya menos valor en ceñirse al trabajo clásico de ciberseguridad (classical cybersecurity work).
fullContext: Sander discusses career opportunities in AI security, specifically addressing where he sees the most valuable work happening. While pure AI red teaming (attacking AI systems) and traditional cybersecurity remain important, he believes the intersection of these fields - understanding both classical security principles and AI-specific vulnerabilities - represents the most critical and valuable skill set for future security professionals.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: My main advice on how to improve your prompting skills is actually just trial and error. You will learn the most from just trying and interacting with chatbots, and talking to them, than anything else, including reading resources, taking courses, all of that.
keySentence: Trial and error is the best way to improve your prompting skills with chatbots.
text_ko: 프롬프트(prompting) 능력을 키우는 데 대한 제 핵심 조언은 사실 그냥 시행착오예요. 자료를 읽거나 강의를 듣는 것보다도, 직접 시도해보고 챗봇(chatbot)과 상호작용하면서 대화해보는 것에서 가장 많이 배우게 돼요.
text_zh: 关于怎么提升你的提示词(prompting)技巧，我最主要的建议其实就是多试多练。你直接跟聊天机器人对话、互动，从中学到的东西，比看什么资料、上什么课程都管用得多。
text_es: Mi consejo principal para mejorar tus habilidades con prompts es simplemente probar y equivocarse. Vas a aprender mucho más solo probando e interactuando con los chatbots, hablando con ellos, que con cualquier otra cosa, incluyendo leer recursos, tomar cursos, todo eso.
fullContext: Lenny asks Sander for his best advice on how people can improve their prompting skills and what often has the most impact. Sander emphasizes that hands-on practice and experimentation is more valuable than formal learning methods. He advocates for direct engagement with AI systems as the most effective way to develop prompting expertise, prioritizing practical experience over theoretical knowledge.

speaker: Sander Schulhoff
text: It is not a solvable problem, which I think is very difficult for a lot of people to hear. And we've seen historically a lot of folks saying, "Oh, this will be solved in a couple of years."
keySentence: It is not a solvable problem, which is difficult for a lot of folks to accept.
text_ko: 이건 완전히 해결할 수 있는 문제가 아니에요. 많은 분들이 그 얘기를 듣기 힘들어하시더라고요. 그리고 역사적으로도 "몇 년 안에 해결될 거예요"라고들 많이 말해왔어요.
text_zh: 这个问题根本就解决不了，我觉得很多人听到这话会很难接受。而且我们也看到，历史上有不少人总是说"哦，这个问题再过两年就能解决了。"
text_es: No es un problema que se pueda resolver, y creo que eso es muy difícil de escuchar para mucha gente. Y hemos visto históricamente a un montón de personas diciendo: "Ah, esto se va a resolver en un par de años."
fullContext: Lenny asks whether AI security vulnerabilities like prompt injection will eventually be completely solved or if it's an endless arms race. Sander delivers the sobering reality that these security issues cannot be fully eliminated, unlike traditional software bugs. He notes that this is a hard truth for many in the industry to accept, as there's often optimism that technical solutions will emerge to completely solve these problems within a few years.

vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'solvable' often refers to challenges or issues that can be effectively managed or overcome through strategic planning or innovation.

insight.nuance: While 'solvable' implies a potential resolution, it can also suggest that the solution may require significant effort or resources.
