vocabulary.businessContext: In project management, activities are often outlined in plans to ensure that objectives are met within designated timelines.

insight.nuance: While 'activity' can refer to productive work, it may also imply a lack of focus if used to describe tasks that do not contribute to strategic goals.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: Make sure you go somewhere where you have a good engineering partner. Because if you have great ideas of what to build but you can't get them built, then you go nowhere.
keySentence: if you have great ideas of what to build but you can't get them built, then you go nowhere.
text_ko: 꼭 좋은 엔지니어링 파트너(engineering partner)가 있는 곳으로 가세요. 만들 아이디어가 아무리 좋아도 그걸 실제로 구현하지 못하면 아무런 진전이 없어요.
text_zh: 一定要去有靠谱的工程伙伴(engineering partner)的地方。要不然你想法再好，落实不了也走不远。
text_es: Asegúrate de ir a un lugar donde cuentes con un buen socio de ingeniería (partner). Porque si tienes grandes ideas sobre qué construir pero no puedes hacerlas realidad, no llegas a ninguna parte.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tamar about building stronger cross-functional relationships, especially between product managers and engineers. Tamar explains that having a strong engineering partnership is crucial for product success - great ideas mean nothing if they can't be executed. She emphasizes the importance of alignment between product and engineering leaders, where both parties understand their roles and responsibilities and don't undermine each other by giving conflicting direction to their teams.

vocabulary.definition: An organization or individual that collaborates with another entity to provide technical expertise and support in the development of products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, an engineering partner is crucial for startups seeking to leverage specialized skills and resources to bring innovative ideas to fruition.

insight.nuance: This term implies a collaborative relationship that goes beyond mere vendor-client dynamics, emphasizing shared goals and mutual investment in success.

vocabulary.definition: Innovative and valuable concepts that have the potential to solve problems or create opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and business development, great ideas are often the foundation for new products or services, driving creativity and strategic planning.

insight.nuance: While 'great ideas' suggests high potential, it is important to recognize that execution and implementation are equally critical for success.

vocabulary.definition: The process of constructing or developing a product, system, or structure from initial concept to final implementation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, 'built' often refers to the actual creation of software, hardware, or services that are ready for market launch or operational use.

insight.nuance: This term conveys a sense of completion and functionality, implying that the product is not just conceptual but has been realized in a tangible form.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: One of the things that I think is overlooked is do a really good job at whatever your job is at that point. People have a tendency ...
keySentence: do a really good job at whatever your job is at that point.
text_ko: 제가 생각하기에 간과되는 것 중 하나는 그때 맡은 일을 정말 제대로 잘하는 거예요. 사람들은 ...
text_zh: 我觉得常被忽视的一点是，先把当下的工作做好。人们往往会……
text_es: Una de las cosas que creo que se pasa por alto es hacer muy bien el trabajo que tengas en ese momento. La gente tiende a...
fullContext: Lenny asks Tamar about the specific skills or habits that contributed most to her successful career. Tamar explains that one of the most overlooked but important factors is excelling at your current role rather than constantly focusing on the next promotion. She argues that ambitious product managers often make the mistake of always looking ahead instead of delivering exceptional results in their present position, which is actually the key to advancement.

vocabulary.definition: To fail to notice or consider something, often leading to missed opportunities or insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, overlooked aspects can include market trends, employee contributions, or potential risks that may affect decision-making.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of negligence or lack of attention, suggesting that the oversight could have significant consequences.

vocabulary.definition: An inclination or predisposition to behave in a certain way or to have a particular characteristic.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding tendencies within consumer behavior or team dynamics can help businesses tailor their strategies and improve performance.

insight.nuance: This word suggests a pattern that may not be absolute but is observable over time, making it useful in predictive analyses.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: One of the things that I caution product managers about is that you don't want to be too overly reliant on metrics and you want to also have an intuition.
keySentence: Don't be overly reliant on metrics; trust your intuition.
text_ko: 제가 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)들에게 자주 당부하는 것 중 하나는 지표(metrics)에만 너무 의존하지 말고 직감도 중요하게 여겨야 한다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我常提醒产品经理(product managers)：别过度依赖指标(metrics)，也要保留自己的直觉判断。
text_es: Una de las cosas que les advierto a los responsables de producto (product managers) es que no conviene fiarse únicamente de las métricas; también hace falta tener intuición.
fullContext: Lenny asks for an example of understanding people in product development. Tamar discusses the balance between data-driven decisions and product intuition. She explains that while metrics are important, product managers shouldn't rely on them exclusively - they need to develop intuitive understanding of their customers and products. This intuition, when properly developed through deep product knowledge, can guide correct decisions even when data might not provide clear direction.

vocabulary.definition: Dependent on someone or something for support or assistance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being reliant often refers to a company's dependence on specific metrics, technologies, or personnel to make decisions or drive performance.

insight.nuance: While reliance can indicate trust in a system or process, being overly reliant may suggest a lack of critical thinking or adaptability.

vocabulary.definition: Quantitative measures used to assess performance, progress, or quality in various contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, metrics are crucial for evaluating success, guiding strategy, and making informed decisions based on data analysis.

insight.nuance: While metrics provide valuable insights, an overemphasis on them can lead to a narrow focus that overlooks qualitative factors.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product management and decision-making, intuition plays a key role in complementing data analysis, allowing leaders to make quick judgments based on experience and gut feelings.

insight.nuance: Intuition can be powerful, but it may also be subjective and less reliable than data-driven approaches, warranting a balanced use of both.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: I love working at well-run companies. It's more fun, your people are happier. I like running a well-run team, so I aspire to have a very well run team and to work at a well run company.
keySentence: I love working at well-run companies.
text_ko: 저는 운영이 잘되는 회사에서 일하는 걸 좋아해요. 훨씬 더 재미있고 구성원들도 더 행복해요. 저는 팀을 잘 운영하는 걸 좋아해서 아주 잘 운영되는 팀을 만들고 그런 회사에서 일하고 싶어요.
text_zh: 我喜欢在管理得好的公司工作，工作氛围更轻松、大家也更开心。我也喜欢把团队带得井井有条，所以我希望能打造一个高效运作的团队，也希望能在这样管理到位的公司里工作。
text_es: Me encanta trabajar en empresas bien gestionadas. Se trabaja mejor: es más divertido y la gente está más contenta. Me gusta dirigir un equipo que funcione bien, así que aspiro a tener un equipo muy bien gestionado y a trabajar en una empresa así.
fullContext: Lenny asks about Tamar's insight that companies don't need to be well-run to win. Tamar explains this seemingly contrarian view by distinguishing between what makes companies pleasant to work at versus what makes them successful. She acknowledges preferring well-run organizations for personal satisfaction, but observes that operational dysfunction - like broken IT systems, poor marketing, inadequate HR, and high turnover - doesn't necessarily prevent business success, while she's also seen well-run companies that fail to grow.

vocabulary.definition: Effectively managed or organized, resulting in efficient operations and positive outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a well-run company is often characterized by strong leadership, clear processes, and high employee morale, which can lead to increased productivity and profitability.

insight.nuance: While 'well-run' conveys a sense of efficiency and success, it may imply a lack of flexibility or innovation if overemphasized.

vocabulary.definition: To have a strong desire or ambition to achieve something, typically requiring effort and determination.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, individuals may aspire to leadership positions, innovative projects, or company-wide goals that align with their career ambitions.

insight.nuance: The term 'aspire' often carries a positive connotation of hope and ambition, but it can also imply a gap between current status and future goals.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: Really recently I was talking to somebody in their twenties who was asking me for career advice. Should I be a product manager, et cetera.
keySentence: Should I be a product manager, et cetera.
text_ko: 정말 최근에 20대인 분이랑 얘기했는데 커리어 조언을 물어보시더라고요. '프로덕트 매니저(product manager)가 돼야 할까요?' 이런 식의 질문이었어요.
text_zh: 就在最近，我跟一个二十多岁的年轻人聊，他在向我请教职业建议，比如要不要做产品经理（product manager）之类的。
text_es: Hace muy poco hablé con alguien de veintitantos que me pidió consejo sobre su carrera: "¿Debería ser responsable de producto (product manager) o algo así?"
fullContext: Lenny asks about Tamar's belief that you don't need to plan your career. Tamar shares a recent conversation with someone in their twenties seeking career advice about becoming a product manager and creating a five-year plan. She reveals that she has never had a five-year career plan throughout her successful career, which immediately relieved the anxiety of the person she was advising. This challenges the conventional wisdom that successful careers require detailed long-term planning.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance provided to individuals regarding their professional paths, including choices about education, job opportunities, and career development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, career advice often comes from mentors or HR professionals who help employees navigate their career trajectories and align their skills with organizational needs.

insight.nuance: While career advice is generally constructive, it can sometimes carry an implicit bias based on the advisor's own experiences or industry trends.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for overseeing the development and lifecycle of a product, ensuring it meets market needs and aligns with business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers play a crucial role in coordinating between engineering, marketing, and sales teams to deliver successful products to market.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a blend of technical, business, and interpersonal skills, and is often associated with leadership and strategic thinking.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: What I believe, and I've always believed is that you follow people. You learn the most from people. I don't look for domains.
keySentence: You learn the most from people.
text_ko: 제가 늘 믿어온 건 사람을 따라가는 거예요. 사람에게서 가장 많이 배워요. 저는 특정 분야(domain)를 찾아다니지는 않아요.
text_zh: 我一直相信，跟对人走最重要。你从人身上学到的最多，我不会去刻意找哪个领域。
text_es: Lo que creo —y siempre he creído— es que hay que seguir a las personas. Se aprende más de la gente. No me fijo en sectores.
fullContext: Continuing the discussion about career planning, Tamar explains her philosophy for career progression without formal plans. Instead of focusing on specific industries or domains, she advocates following exceptional people - those who are genuinely the best at their craft, whether in product thinking, engineering, or sales. She emphasizes that personal likability isn't enough; you need to work with people who excel at their skills so you can learn how to become exceptional yourself.

vocabulary.definition: Specific areas of knowledge, expertise, or activity within a broader field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, domains often refer to specialized sectors such as finance, healthcare, or software development, guiding strategic decisions and innovations.

insight.nuance: The term 'domains' can imply a level of specialization, suggesting that expertise in one area may not translate to others.

speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
text: I got a piece of advice from a friend that I thought was amazing advice as a leader.
keySentence: I got a piece of advice from a friend that I thought was amazing advice as a leader.
text_ko: 친구가 해준 조언이 하나 있는데, 리더로서 들으니 정말 인상 깊었어요.
text_zh: 有位朋友给了我一句建议，作为领导我觉得特别受用。
text_es: Un amigo me dio un consejo que, como líder, me pareció increíble.
fullContext: Lenny discusses the concept of companies having gravitational pull for talent. Tamar shares advice she received from a friend about leadership job selection. When she was considering various leadership roles, including some turnaround situations, her friend suggested she only take positions where hiring people would advance their careers. This advice made her realize she should evaluate opportunities not just for her own benefit, but for whether she could genuinely help the people she'd recruit to learn and grow.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance or recommendations offered with regard to prudent future action, often based on experience or expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, advice can come from mentors, consultants, or peers and is vital for decision-making and strategic planning.

insight.nuance: Advice can carry varying degrees of weight depending on the source's credibility and the context in which it is given; it is often seen as subjective.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: The company has a tendency to over-invest. Startups have the benefit of starving, and so you need to create scarcity. What we try to do is remind everyone things are going to fail, let's not drag the rest of the company into it.
keySentence: The company tends to over-invest; startups benefit from starving and creating scarcity.
text_ko: 회사에는 과도하게 투자(over-invest)하는 경향이 있어요. 스타트업(startup)은 '배고픔'(starving)이 주는 이점이 있어서 의도적으로 희소성(scarcity)을 만들어야 해요. 우리는 모두에게 일이 실패할 수 있다는 걸 상기시키고, 실패하면 회사 전체를 끌어들이지 않도록 해요.
text_zh: 我们公司有个毛病，就是容易投入过度。初创公司其实挺好的，因为资源紧张，所以你得人为制造一种紧迫感。我们现在就是要时刻提醒大家，有些项目肯定会失败，别让整个公司都跟着陪葬。
text_es: La empresa tiende a invertir de más. Las startups tienen la ventaja de que están con el agua al cuello, así que necesitas crear esa escasez. Lo que tratamos de hacer es recordarle a todo el mundo que las cosas van a fallar, no arrastremos al resto de la empresa con nosotros.
fullContext: Lenny asks why it's so hard to start new products within large companies. Tanguy explains one of the key challenges: large companies have resources but lack the natural constraints that help startups focus. He advocates for artificially creating scarcity and setting expectations that new bets will likely fail to prevent the broader organization from over-investing too early.

vocabulary.definition: To allocate more resources, such as capital or time, to a project or venture than is justified by its potential return.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in startups, over-investing can lead to financial strain and misallocation of resources, especially when the market does not support such levels of investment.

insight.nuance: While over-investing may stem from optimism about a project, it often indicates a lack of strategic planning and can result in significant losses.

vocabulary.definition: The state of being in short supply; a situation in which resources are limited relative to demand.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, scarcity can drive innovation and efficiency, compelling teams to prioritize essential tasks and make the most of available resources.

insight.nuance: Scarcity often fosters a sense of urgency and creativity, but it can also create stress and competition among team members if not managed properly.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: Be very clear about what we're testing, doing that with data, doing that with personal customer stories, give people a sense of velocity and speed. No one wants to fuck with a high-speed train.
keySentence: Provide a sense of velocity; no one wants to fuck with a high-speed train.
text_ko: 우리가 무엇을 테스트하는지 아주 분명히 하세요. 그걸 데이터로 보여주고, 실제 고객의 개인적인 이야기로 뒷받침하세요. 사람들에게 속도(velocity)를 체감하게 해 주세요. 아무도 고속열차를 건드리고 싶어 하지 않아요.
text_zh: 要明确我们在测什么，用数据说话，用客户的真实故事说话，让大家感受到我们的速度和冲劲。没人愿意去撞高铁，对吧？
text_es: Sé muy claro sobre lo que estamos probando, hazlo con datos, hazlo with historias reales de clientes, dale a la gente una sensación de velocidad y momentum. Nadie se va a meter con un tren de alta velocidad.
fullContext: Lenny discusses the challenge companies face when leadership wants to kill new products after six months of slow progress. Tanguy shares his strategy for protecting new initiatives by maintaining clear communication about what's being tested, backing it up with both data and compelling customer stories, and demonstrating consistent momentum to discourage interference from other parts of the organization.

vocabulary.definition: Velocity refers to the speed of something in a given direction, often used to indicate the rate of progress or change.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, velocity is commonly used to measure the speed at which teams deliver products or features, particularly in agile development environments.

insight.nuance: While velocity implies speed, it also carries the connotation of purposeful movement towards a goal, distinguishing it from mere rapidity.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: My track record at Atlassian has been 50/50 at best. Jira Project Discovery is actually my first, what I would call big success here.
keySentence: Jira Project Discovery is actually my first, what I would call big success here.
text_ko: 아틀라시안(Atlassian)에서의 실적은 잘해야 반반이에요. 사실 지라 프로젝트 디스커버리(Jira Project Discovery)가 여기서 제가 말하자면 첫 번째로 거둔 큰 성공이에요.
text_zh: 我在 Atlassian 的成绩顶多也就是五五开，Jira Project Discovery 算是我在这儿第一个真正的大成功。
text_es: Mi historial en Atlassian ha sido, como mucho, un 50/50. Jira Project Discovery es, de hecho, mi primer éxito importante aquí.
fullContext: Tanguy shares his honest assessment of building zero-to-one products at Atlassian over 10 years. He's worked on products like HipChat, Stride, and Statuspage with mixed results. Jira Product Discovery represents his first major success, but he emphasizes that even successful outcomes in large companies involve significant struggles and setbacks along the way.

vocabulary.definition: A documented history of someone's or something's performance or achievements over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a track record is often used to evaluate the reliability and success of an individual, team, or company based on past results, which can influence hiring decisions and investment opportunities.

insight.nuance: While a strong track record is generally viewed positively, a poor track record may raise concerns about future performance.

vocabulary.definition: A significant achievement that results in notable positive outcomes or recognition.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech, a big success often refers to a product launch or project that exceeds expectations in terms of revenue, user adoption, or market impact.

insight.nuance: The term is subjective and can vary based on individual or organizational goals, making it important to clarify what constitutes 'big' in specific contexts.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: we can apply this playbook to this market... The thing is we didn't, in my opinion, do enough to validate that assumption early enough.
keySentence: We made the bet to apply this playbook, but didn't validate that assumption early enough.
text_ko: 이 플레이북(playbook)을 이 시장에 적용할 수 있다고 봐요. 근데 제 생각에는 그 가정을 초기에 충분히 검증하지 못했어요.
text_zh: 我们本可以把这套打法(playbook)用到这个市场上……问题是，我觉得我们没能在早期充分验证那个假设。
text_es: Podemos aplicar este plan de acción (playbook) a este mercado... La cuestión es que, en mi opinión, no hicimos lo suficiente para validar esa hipótesis a tiempo.
fullContext: Tanguy explains Atlassian's failed strategy with HipChat, their enterprise communication product that competed with Slack. Atlassian assumed their successful bottom-up adoption model from developer tools would work for business communication tools. However, they didn't adequately test whether their existing customer base in tech teams would actually drive adoption in business teams, leading to strategic missteps.

vocabulary.definition: To confirm the accuracy or legitimacy of something through evidence or testing.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, validation often refers to the process of ensuring that a product or concept meets market needs and is feasible before full-scale implementation.

insight.nuance: While 'validate' suggests a thorough examination, it can imply a level of skepticism about initial assumptions or proposals.

vocabulary.definition: A belief or statement taken for granted without proof, often serving as a basis for further reasoning or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, assumptions underpin decisions and projections; they must be tested to ensure sound planning and risk management.

insight.nuance: Assumptions can carry a negative connotation if they are unfounded or overly optimistic, leading to potential pitfalls in decision-making.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: At some point, the Slack was really gaining round and gaining round and capturing more of the mindshare. And everyone on Twitter was always loving them. Even when they had outrages, they were getting congratulated.
keySentence: Slack was gaining round, capturing more of the mindshare despite their outrages.
text_ko: 어느 순간 슬랙은 계속 세를 넓히며 마인드셰어(mindshare)를 더 많이 차지하고 있었어요. 트위터에선 늘 사람들이 그들을 좋아했고, 논란이 생겨도 오히려 칭찬을 받곤 했어요.
text_zh: 有一段时间，Slack 真的是越做越火，越来越抢占用户心智(mindshare)。在推特（Twitter）上大家都很爱他们，就算闹出风波，反而还被夸。
text_es: Hubo un momento en que Slack empezó a ganar terreno de verdad y a captar cada vez más atención (mindshare). En Twitter todo el mundo los elogiaba; incluso cuando surgían polémicas o indignación, seguían recibiendo felicitaciones.
fullContext: Tanguy describes the competitive dynamics between HipChat and Slack, warning against 'competitive myopia.' He explains how Slack gained significant mindshare and customer love, even during outages. This led Atlassian to fall into a trap of reactive feature development, constantly trying to match Slack's features rather than focusing on serving their own customers' unique needs.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of consumer awareness or attention a brand or product commands in the marketplace.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing and branding, 'mindshare' reflects how well a brand is recognized and remembered by consumers, influencing their purchasing decisions.

insight.nuance: While often used positively to denote strong brand presence, it can also suggest that a brand is competing for attention in a crowded market.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: Everyone was excited, thought it made sense, lots of encouragement. I pitched it to every level of the organization from business leaders, to the CTO that we had at the time, to the CEOs. No one said no, no one said yes. For months.
keySentence: I pitched it to every level; no one said no, no one said yes.
text_ko: 다들 기대했고, 말이 된다고 생각했으며, 응원도 많이 받았어요. 비즈니스 리더들(business leaders)부터 당시 우리 최고기술책임자(CTO), CEO들(CEOs)에 이르기까지 조직의 모든 레벨에 제안했어요. 그런데 아무도 반대하지도, 찬성하지도 않았어요. 몇 달 동안요.
text_zh: 大家都很兴奋，觉得这想法挺靠谱的，给了我不少鼓励。我把这个方案推给了公司各个层级的人——业务负责人、当时的CTO、还有CEO们。结果呢，没人说不行，也没人拍板说行。就这么拖了好几个月。
text_es: Todo el mundo estaba emocionado, pensaban que tenía sentido, me daban mucho apoyo. Se lo presenté a todos los niveles de la organización, desde los líderes de negocio hasta el CTO que teníamos en ese momento, hasta los CEOs. Nadie dijo que no, nadie dijo que sí. Durante meses.
fullContext: Tanguy describes his frustrating experience trying to get approval for an IT operations business case at Atlassian before their internal incubator program existed. Despite positive feedback from all levels of leadership including CTOs and CEOs, the project remained in limbo for months without clear approval or rejection, highlighting the challenge of getting new initiatives prioritized in large organizations.

vocabulary.definition: To present an idea or proposal in a persuasive manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'pitching' often refers to the act of presenting a product, service, or concept to potential investors, clients, or stakeholders to gain support or approval.

insight.nuance: While 'pitched' implies a proactive approach to sharing ideas, it can also suggest a level of informality or enthusiasm that may not be present in more formal presentations.

vocabulary.definition: Support or motivation provided to someone to help them achieve a goal or pursue an idea.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, encouragement can come from leadership or peers to foster innovation, boost morale, and enhance team performance.

insight.nuance: Encouragement carries a positive connotation and is often associated with constructive feedback, but it may also imply a need for reassurance in uncertain situations.

vocabulary.definition: A structured group of individuals working together towards common goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, an organization can refer to a company, nonprofit, or any formal entity that operates with a defined structure and purpose.

insight.nuance: The term 'organization' can imply a level of formality and hierarchy, and it is often used to distinguish between different types of entities or groups within the business landscape.

speaker: Tanguy Crusson
text: What we needed is to create this area where we could experiment that's away from Jira while being inside Jira. That part was a bit tough. It's possible to do. In fact, I came across an article from Ben Weiss.
keySentence: We needed to create an area to experiment away from Jira while being inside Jira.
text_ko: 우리가 필요했던 건 지라(Jira) 내부에 있으면서도 지라에서 벗어나 실험해볼 수 있는 공간을 만드는 거였어요. 그 부분이 좀 까다로웠어요. 그래도 가능하긴 해요. 사실 Ben Weiss의 글을 우연히 접했어요.
text_zh: 我们需要在 Jira（Jira）里搭个能做实验的独立空间，既在 Jira 里又能跟主环境隔离开来。那块挺棘手的，不过是可以做到的。事实上，我还看到 Ben Weiss 写过一篇文章。
text_es: Lo que necesitábamos era crear un espacio donde pudiéramos experimentar, apartado del Jira habitual pero dentro de la propia herramienta. Esa parte fue algo complicada. Sí se puede hacer; de hecho me topé con un artículo de Ben Weiss.
fullContext: Tanguy explains how they approached building Jira Product Discovery for product managers without disrupting Jira's existing user base of 120,000 customers. He references Noah Weiss's framework of 'incubate, iterate, integrate' - starting with isolated experiments, refining them separately, then integrating successful features back into the main product. This approach allowed them to reimagine Jira's experience for a specific audience without breaking existing workflows.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic procedure undertaken to make a discovery, test a hypothesis, or demonstrate a known fact.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, experiments are often conducted to test new ideas, products, or processes in a controlled environment to gather data and insights for decision-making.

insight.nuance: While 'experiment' implies a degree of uncertainty and risk, it is often viewed positively as a means of innovation and improvement.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: So first of all, it's just a really simple visual. It's funny how simple it looks, because using it in practice is really complex. I definitely have a new appreciation for that, trying to teach it over and over again and seeing where people struggle.
keySentence: I have a new appreciation for its complexity, teaching it over and over again.
text_ko: 먼저, 보기에는 정말 단순한 비주얼이에요. 이렇게 단순해 보이는 게 신기한데, 실제로 현장에서 써보면 훨씬 복잡해요. 계속 반복해서 가르치다 보니 사람들이 어디서 어려워하는지 보이더라고요, 그래서 그 복잡함을 새삼 더 인정하게 됐어요.
text_zh: 首先吧，这个图表看起来特别简单。挺有意思的是，看着简单，但真正用起来其实挺复杂的。我现在是真的体会到了这一点，因为我反复教了好多次，也看到大家都在哪些地方容易卡住。
text_es: Bueno, antes que nada, es una imagen súper sencilla. Es curioso lo simple que se ve, porque cuando lo pones en práctica es realmente complejo. Definitivamente ahora lo valoro más, después de intentar enseñarlo una y otra vez y ver dónde se traba la gente.
fullContext: Lenny asks Teresa to explain the opportunity solution tree framework and what problem it solves for product teams. Teresa begins by describing the framework as a visual tree structure that starts with an outcome and branches into opportunities and solutions. She emphasizes that while the framework appears deceptively simple, implementing it effectively requires significant skill and deep thinking.

vocabulary.definition: The recognition and enjoyment of the good qualities of someone or something; a feeling of gratitude or thankfulness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, appreciation can refer to recognizing the value of employees' contributions or the importance of customer feedback in improving products and services.

insight.nuance: While appreciation often implies a positive acknowledgment, it can also suggest a deeper understanding of complexities involved in a situation or process.

vocabulary.definition: Consisting of many different and connected parts; not simple or straightforward.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business or tech environment, complex systems or processes may require advanced understanding and problem-solving skills to navigate effectively.

insight.nuance: The term 'complex' often carries a connotation of difficulty and may imply that a solution requires significant effort or expertise.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to seeing or sight; designed to be seen, often involving images or graphics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business presentations and marketing, visual elements are crucial for effectively communicating ideas and engaging audiences, often enhancing understanding and retention.

insight.nuance: The term 'visual' can imply creativity and innovation, but it may also suggest a reliance on imagery that could oversimplify complex information.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: But it's the opposite of how our brains are wired. And so, teaching people to be comfortable with that discomfort of staying there is hard.
keySentence: Teaching comfort with discomfort is the opposite of how our brains are wired.
text_ko: 하지만 그건 우리 뇌가 작동하는 방식과 정반대예요. 그래서 사람들이 그 불편함 속에 머무르는 것에 편해지도록 가르치는 건 어려워요.
text_zh: 但这跟我们大脑的运作方式正好相反，所以要教人们在那种持续的不舒服里也能感到自在，真的很难。
text_es: Pero va en contra de cómo funciona nuestro cerebro. Por eso es difícil enseñar a la gente a tolerar esa incomodidad y a permanecer en ella.
fullContext: Teresa explains why the opportunity solution tree framework is challenging to implement correctly. She discusses how product teams struggle to distinguish between problems (opportunities) and solutions, with 98% of people incorrectly writing opportunities as solutions. The core difficulty is that humans naturally want to jump to solutions rather than spend time properly understanding and framing problems.

vocabulary.definition: Discomfort refers to a state of unease or lack of comfort, often associated with physical or emotional distress.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, discomfort can arise during change management processes, requiring leaders to help employees navigate through uncertainty and resistance.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a necessary but unpleasant experience; it is useful in discussions about growth, resilience, and adaptation in challenging situations.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: The challenge with that is we know from human psychology and cognitive psychology that we're not very good at answering those questions out of context. Actually, that sounds weird. We're very good at answering them.
keySentence: we're not very good at answering those questions out of context.
text_ko: 문제는 인간 심리학(human psychology)과 인지 심리학(cognitive psychology)에서 보면 우리가 그런 질문들을 문맥 없이 받으면 잘 못 답한다는 거예요. 아, 이렇게 말하니까 좀 이상하게 들리네요. 사실은 우리는 그런 질문에 되게 잘 답해요.
text_zh: 问题在于，从心理学，尤其是认知心理学的研究我们知道，把这些问题脱离具体情境去问时，我们通常答得不太好。等等，这听起来怪怪的——其实我们反而很擅长回答它们。
text_es: El problema es que, según la psicología humana (human psychology) y la psicología cognitiva (cognitive psychology), no se nos da bien responder a esas preguntas fuera de contexto. Bueno, eso suena raro: en realidad se nos da muy bien responderlas.
fullContext: Teresa explains why traditional interviewing approaches fail when trying to understand customer opportunities. She contrasts asking direct questions like 'What do you like to watch on Netflix?' with collecting specific stories about recent experiences. The key insight is that while people readily provide answers to direct questions, these responses often don't accurately reflect their actual behavior because they lack the context and nuance of real situations.

vocabulary.definition: Cognitive psychology is the branch of psychology that studies mental processes such as perception, memory, reasoning, and decision-making. It focuses on how people understand, think, and remember information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, cognitive psychology informs user experience design, marketing strategies, and decision-making processes by understanding how consumers think and behave.

insight.nuance: This term is often used in discussions about user behavior and product design, but may not be familiar to those outside of psychological or academic fields.

vocabulary.definition: Context refers to the circumstances or setting surrounding an event, statement, or idea that helps to clarify its meaning. It is essential for understanding the nuances of communication and behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, context is crucial for interpreting data, making informed decisions, and understanding customer feedback, as it provides the background necessary for effective analysis.

insight.nuance: While context is often implied in discussions, explicitly stating it can enhance clarity and understanding, particularly in complex or ambiguous situations.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: So there's a lot of skill involved. I wish I could just say, 'Hey, Lenny. It's super easy. Everybody should do it. I think it's really powerful, and I've seen it be a game-changer for teams. It's hard.
keySentence: It's a game-changer, but there's a lot of skill involved.
text_ko: 그래서 많은 기술이 필요해요. 그냥 "레니, 정말 쉬워요. 누구나 해야 해요. 저는 이게 정말 강력하다고 생각하고 팀들에게는 판도를 바꿔놓는(game-changer) 경우도 봤어요."라고 말할 수 있으면 좋겠어요. 그런데 어려워요.
text_zh: 这里面有很多技巧。我真希望能直接跟你说，"嘿，Lenny，这超简单的，人人都能做。"但实际上这真的很有用，我见过它彻底改变团队的表现。只是确实不容易。
text_es: Entonces sí requiere mucha habilidad. Ojalá pudiera simplemente decir, 'Oye, Lenny. Es súper fácil. Todo el mundo debería hacerlo.' Creo que es realmente poderoso, y he visto que puede cambiar completamente la dinámica de los equipos (game-changer). Pero es difícil.
fullContext: Teresa responds to Lenny's question about how product managers can create their own opportunity solution trees. She explains that the process requires multiple complex skills: interviewing well to collect customer stories, being able to identify opportunities versus solutions, framing opportunities specifically, and structuring the opportunity space using experience maps. Despite the difficulty, she emphasizes that teams willing to invest in developing these skills see transformational results.

vocabulary.definition: A game-changer is a person, idea, or event that significantly alters the existing state of affairs or creates a new paradigm.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a game-changer often refers to an innovation or strategy that disrupts the market and provides a competitive advantage.

insight.nuance: This term carries a positive connotation and is often used to highlight breakthroughs that lead to substantial improvements or transformations.

vocabulary.definition: Powerful describes something that has great strength, influence, or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, powerful can refer to a product, strategy, or leader that has a significant impact on performance or market dynamics.

insight.nuance: While often used positively, it can also imply overwhelming force or control, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: Skill is the ability to perform tasks and solve problems effectively, often acquired through training and experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, skills are critical for employee performance and are often a focus in hiring, training, and development initiatives.

insight.nuance: While 'skill' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply a need for continuous improvement and learning.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: we're going to focus on structuring an opportunity space, and I'm probably going to make you think harder than you've ever had to think in your job.
keySentence: I'm probably going to make you think harder than you've ever had to think in your job.
text_ko: 우리는 기회 영역(opportunity space)을 체계화하는 데 집중할 거예요. 그리고 아마 제가 여러분을 직장 생활에서 지금까지 해보신 것보다 훨씬 더 깊게 고민하게 만들 거예요.
text_zh: 我们会专注把一个机会空间(opportunity space)搭建起来，我可能会让你比在这份工作里任何时候都更费脑筋。
text_es: Nos vamos a centrar en cómo estructurar un espacio de oportunidades (opportunity space), y probablemente les pida que piensen más a fondo que nunca en su trabajo.
fullContext: Teresa continues explaining the difficulty of implementing the opportunity solution tree framework effectively. She describes how the deep thinking required for structuring opportunity spaces is unlike typical work activities. Most professionals spend their days in meetings and surface-level discussions, but this framework demands intensive critical thinking and analysis to properly understand customer needs and frame problems correctly.

vocabulary.definition: The process of organizing or arranging elements in a systematic way to achieve a specific goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, structuring often refers to the design of processes, teams, or projects to optimize efficiency and effectiveness.

insight.nuance: While structuring implies a deliberate and thoughtful arrangement, it can also suggest rigidity if not balanced with flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: A conceptual area where potential business opportunities exist, often identified through market analysis and strategic planning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and innovation, defining an opportunity space helps teams focus their efforts on areas with the highest potential for growth and impact.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a proactive approach to identifying and capitalizing on market gaps, rather than merely reacting to existing conditions.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: So we overthink it. We think we have to go through these proper channels and we have to get permission from sales. A lot of us, especially if we work on a consumer product, just go find somebody that's like your user.
keySentence: We overthink it, believing we need proper channels for permission.
text_ko: 우리는 그걸 너무 복잡하게 생각해요. 정해진 절차를 밟아야 하고 영업(sales) 쪽의 허락을 받아야 한다고 생각하죠. 근데 많은 사람들, 특히 소비자용 제품(consumer product)을 다루는 사람들은 그냥 사용자(user)랑 비슷한 사람을 찾아가서 직접 얘기해봐요.
text_zh: 所以我们就想多了。我们觉得必须走正规渠道，必须得到销售那边的批准。其实我们很多人，特别是做消费产品的，直接去找个跟你们用户差不多的人就行了。
text_es: Entonces le damos demasiadas vueltas. Pensamos que tenemos que seguir todos los canales oficiales y que necesitamos el visto bueno del equipo de ventas. Muchos de nosotros, sobre todo si trabajamos en un producto de consumo, simplemente vamos y buscamos a alguien que sea como nuestro usuario.
fullContext: Lenny asks how individual contributors can use discovery frameworks even in feature factory environments. Teresa advises focusing on changing individual work habits rather than trying to force organizational change. She addresses the common excuse that people aren't 'allowed' to talk to customers, suggesting they can start by talking to people in their personal networks who resemble their users, rather than getting caught up in formal approval processes.

vocabulary.definition: The established procedures or protocols that are followed to ensure compliance and communication within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'proper channels' often refer to the hierarchical pathways through which information, requests, or approvals must flow to maintain order and accountability.

insight.nuance: Using 'proper channels' can imply a sense of formality and adherence to rules, which may be seen as bureaucratic in fast-paced environments.

vocabulary.definition: The approval or consent granted by an authority or individual to take a specific action or make a decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, obtaining 'permission' is often necessary before proceeding with projects, initiatives, or changes that may impact the organization.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a connotation of hierarchy, suggesting that one must seek approval from superiors, which may be viewed as stifling in innovative cultures.

vocabulary.definition: A tangible item that is produced for sale to individuals for personal use, as opposed to business or industrial use.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and businesses, 'consumer products' are often the focus of marketing and sales strategies aimed at meeting the needs and preferences of end-users.

insight.nuance: The term emphasizes the end-user aspect, distinguishing these products from industrial goods, and suggests a focus on usability and customer satisfaction.

speaker: Teresa Torres
text: That's not our business environment. Our businesses are expecting us to deliver continuous value, so we need to look at how do we match that cadence.
keySentence: our businesses are expecting us to deliver continuous value, so we need to look at how do we match that cadence.
text_ko: 그건 우리 비즈니스 환경(business environment)이 아니에요. 우리 사업부들은 우리가 지속적인 가치(continuous value)를 계속 제공하길 기대하고 있어서, 그 페이스(cadence)에 어떻게 맞출지 살펴봐야 해요.
text_zh: 那不适合我们的业务环境。业务方期待我们持续输出价值，所以我们得想办法跟上这个节奏(cadence)。
text_es: Eso no es nuestro entorno empresarial. Las empresas para las que trabajamos nos piden que entreguemos valor de forma continua, así que tenemos que ver cómo adaptarnos a ese ritmo.
fullContext: Teresa responds to a common objection from leaders who say there's no time for discovery work. She explains that continuous discovery is designed to match the fast-paced business environment, unlike traditional project-based research methods that require stopping work to conduct lengthy studies. The key insight is that discovery can be done sustainably with just one customer interview per week, making it feasible even in time-constrained environments.

vocabulary.definition: Continuous value refers to the ongoing delivery of benefits or improvements that meet customer needs over time. It emphasizes the importance of sustained performance and innovation in products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in tech and startups, delivering continuous value is crucial for maintaining customer satisfaction and loyalty, as it reflects a commitment to evolving offerings based on user feedback and market demands.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a proactive approach to customer engagement and product development, contrasting with a one-time transactional mindset.

vocabulary.definition: The business environment encompasses all external and internal factors that affect a company's operations, including economic, social, technological, and competitive elements. It shapes the strategic decisions and performance of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the business environment is essential for organizations to adapt their strategies, identify opportunities, and mitigate risks in a dynamic market landscape.

insight.nuance: This term can imply both challenges and opportunities, and it is often used in discussions about strategic planning and market analysis.

vocabulary.definition: To match means to correspond or align with something in a way that meets expectations or requirements. It often involves finding compatibility or equivalence between two elements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, matching can refer to aligning products with customer needs, ensuring that services meet market demands, or synchronizing team efforts to achieve common goals.

insight.nuance: While 'match' suggests a positive alignment, it can also imply a lack of differentiation if used inappropriately, such as in competitive analyses.

vocabulary.definition: Cadence refers to the rhythm or pace at which activities occur, particularly in a business context. It can denote the frequency of meetings, project updates, or product releases.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, establishing a consistent cadence is vital for maintaining momentum in project execution and ensuring timely communication among teams.

insight.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of regularity and predictability, which can be crucial for effective team dynamics and project management.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: The other thing to me is bringing an outside in perspective, really benchmarking against your competitors and your competitive set. Don't get me wrong, I think Etsy is a unique marketplace. Our sellers are independent sellers. They sell unique items.
keySentence: Benchmarking against competitors provides an outside in perspective for Etsy.
text_ko: 또 한 가지는 외부 시각을 들여와서 경쟁사(competitors)와 경쟁군(competitive set)에 대해 정말 벤치마킹(benchmarking)하는 거예요. 오해하지 마세요. 저는 Etsy가 정말 독특한 마켓플레이스라고 생각해요. 우리 판매자들은 독립적인 개인 판매자들이고, 각자 고유한 상품을 팔아요.
text_zh: 对我来说还有一点，就是要把外部视角带进来，真的要把自己跟竞争对手以及行业内其他可比公司(competitive set)做标杆比较(benchmarking)。别误会，我觉得Etsy确实是个独特的市场，我们的卖家都是独立卖家，卖的都是独特的商品。
text_es: Una cosa importante para mí es aportar una perspectiva externa y, de verdad, comparar (benchmarking) cómo te estás posicionando frente a tus competidores y con tu conjunto competitivo (competitive set). No me malinterpretes: creo que Etsy es un mercado único. Nuestros vendedores son independientes y venden productos únicos.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tim what Josh Silverman did well to help Etsy transition from a consensus-driven culture to a more business-focused approach in 2017. Tim explains that one key change was adopting an outside-in perspective by benchmarking against competitors. While Etsy is unique as a marketplace for independent sellers offering unique items, Tim emphasizes that buyers still shop across many different platforms and retailers, so Etsy needs to understand the broader competitive landscape to make better strategic decisions.

vocabulary.definition: Benchmarking is the process of comparing one's business processes and performance metrics to industry bests or best practices from other companies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, benchmarking is often used to identify areas for improvement and to set performance standards based on competitors' successes.

insight.nuance: While benchmarking is a valuable tool for improvement, it is important to ensure that comparisons are relevant and that unique company circumstances are taken into account.

vocabulary.definition: A competitive set refers to a group of companies or products that compete against each other in the same market or industry segment.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the competitive set is crucial for market analysis, allowing businesses to position themselves effectively and strategize against rivals.

insight.nuance: The term implies a focus on direct competitors, and it is important to define the competitive set carefully to ensure relevant comparisons.

vocabulary.definition: A unique marketplace is a distinct environment where specific products or services are offered, often characterized by specialized offerings that differentiate it from broader markets.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and tech, a unique marketplace can attract niche audiences and create opportunities for specialized business models.

insight.nuance: The term suggests exclusivity and differentiation, making it important to highlight what makes the marketplace distinct from others.

vocabulary.definition: Perspective refers to a particular attitude or way of considering something, often shaped by individual experiences and insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, bringing an outside-in perspective can provide fresh insights and innovative ideas that challenge the status quo.

insight.nuance: The term can imply a broader or more holistic view, and it is often used to encourage diverse viewpoints in decision-making processes.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: And having that be part of the day-to-day conversation, it seems like such a small thing, but it adds up to having clarity on goal, the KPI point, and then clarity on why, the narrative point.
keySentence: it adds up to having clarity on goal, the KPI point, and then clarity on why, the narrative point.
text_ko: 그걸 일상 대화의 일부로 만드는 건 별거 아닌 것처럼 보여도, 쌓이면 목표와 핵심성과지표(KPI)에 대한 명확성은 물론 왜 하는지에 대한 내러티브(narrative)도 분명해져요.
text_zh: 把这件事当成日常沟通的一部分，表面上看像小事，但久而久之会让大家对目标(goal)、关键绩效指标(KPI)更清晰，也更明白背后的原因和叙事(narrative)。
text_es: Hacer que forme parte de la conversación diaria puede parecer algo pequeño, pero suma: da claridad sobre el objetivo, sobre el indicador clave de rendimiento (KPI) y, sobre todo, sobre el porqué, la narrativa detrás.
fullContext: Lenny asks what Tim learned about making organizational change from watching Josh Silverman's leadership transition at Etsy. Tim explains that effective change requires both a clear KPI that teams can rally around and a consistent narrative explaining why the change matters. He notes that leaders need to repeat messages multiple times before people truly understand and internalize them, making day-to-day reinforcement critical for successful transformation.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being clear and easy to understand, particularly in communication or thought.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, clarity is crucial for effective communication among team members, ensuring that objectives and expectations are well understood.

insight.nuance: While clarity often refers to straightforwardness, it can also imply transparency in decision-making and processes.

vocabulary.definition: A specific target or desired outcome that an individual or organization aims to achieve within a certain timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business environment, goals guide strategic planning and performance measurement, helping teams align their efforts towards common objectives.

insight.nuance: Goals can be short-term or long-term and may vary in specificity; it's important to differentiate between goals and broader aspirations.

vocabulary.definition: Key Performance Indicator; a measurable value that demonstrates how effectively an organization is achieving key business objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: KPIs are used in business to evaluate success at reaching targets, often guiding decision-making and strategic adjustments.

insight.nuance: KPIs should be relevant and actionable; they can vary significantly between industries and organizations, making their selection critical.

vocabulary.definition: A structured account or story that conveys a particular message or perspective, often used to explain or contextualize information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a narrative can be used in marketing, branding, and internal communications to create a compelling story that resonates with stakeholders.

insight.nuance: The term often implies a persuasive or strategic angle, as opposed to merely presenting facts; it's important to ensure authenticity in the narrative.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: Our sellers are incredibly astute business people. And if you had been making wedding dresses, and you know how to sew, and you've got material, and you've got a bit of time, making a mask is quite a simple task.
keySentence: Sellers are incredibly astute business people responding to a huge surge of demand.
text_ko: 우리 판매자분들은 사업 감각이 정말 뛰어나요. 웨딩드레스를 만들던 분이고 재봉을 할 줄 아시며, 재료와 시간이 조금만 있으면 마스크 만드는 건 꽤 간단한 일이에요.
text_zh: 我们的卖家都很精明。要是你本来做婚纱、会缝、手头有布料、还有点空闲，做个口罩其实很简单。
text_es: Nuestros vendedores son muy perspicaces. Si te dedicabas a hacer vestidos de novia, sabes coser, tienes tela y un poco de tiempo, hacer una mascarilla es bastante sencillo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tim about Etsy's experience during COVID-19, particularly the massive growth in face mask sales. Tim explains how when the CDC mandated face masks in April 2020, Etsy experienced overnight Black Friday-level traffic and sales. He describes how Etsy's sellers quickly pivoted their skills - for example, wedding dress makers using their sewing abilities and materials to create face masks, demonstrating the marketplace's ability to rapidly adapt supply to meet urgent demand.

vocabulary.definition: Having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being astute refers to the capability of making sound judgments and strategic decisions that lead to competitive advantages.

insight.nuance: While 'astute' conveys intelligence and insight, it can sometimes imply shrewdness or cunning, so it should be used carefully to avoid negative connotations.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: And we did something that far as I know we've never done an Etsy's past, which is we put out a call to our sellers to say, 'Now's the time.
keySentence: We put out a call to help sellers shine and meet buyer needs.
text_ko: 그리고 제가 알기로는 Etsy 역사상 한 번도 해본 적이 없는 일을 했어요. 판매자들에게 '지금이 바로 그때예요'라고 공개적으로 요청을 보낸 거예요.
text_zh: 就我所知，这是Etsy以前从没做过的事——我们向卖家发出号召，说：“现在就是时候了。”
text_es: Y hicimos algo que, hasta donde sé, nunca se había hecho antes en Etsy: lanzamos un llamado a nuestros vendedores para decirles «ahora es el momento».
fullContext: Tim continues describing Etsy's response during the early COVID-19 pandemic when face masks became mandatory. He explains that Etsy took the unprecedented step of actively encouraging their sellers to pivot and start making face masks. This was apparently the first time in Etsy's history that they had directly called on sellers to focus on a specific product category, showing how the company stepped up during a crisis to help both sellers maintain income and buyers access essential items.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: And so using a favorite as an example, you favorite an item. That's a pretty strong ish... Of course, adding it to your cart or maybe purchasing it, that's the strongest of signals, but you've shown intent. So what can we do with that information?
keySentence: You've shown intent by favoriting an item; we can encourage you to check it out.
text_ko: 예를 들어 즐겨찾기(favorite)를 한 경우를 보면, 아이템을 즐겨찾기에 추가하는 건 꽤 강한 신호예요. 물론 장바구니(cart)에 넣거나 실제로 구매하면 가장 강한 신호지만, 이미 구매 의도(intent)를 보인 셈이에요. 그 정보를 가지고 우리는 뭘 할 수 있을까요?
text_zh: 打个比方，你把某个商品收藏（favorite）了。这本身就是一个挺明显的信号。更进一步，把它加到购物车或者直接下单，信号就更强，但至少你已经表现出购买意向。那我们能用这些信息做什么？
text_es: Si tomamos como ejemplo marcar un producto como favorito (favorite): cuando lo marcas, ya es una señal bastante relevante. Claro, añadirlo al carrito (cart) o comprarlo sería la señal más fuerte, pero ya has mostrado intención. ¿Qué podemos hacer con esa información?
fullContext: Lenny asks Tim about what Etsy has learned works effectively for user retention. Tim explains their approach to creating habit loops - when users take actions like favoriting items (similar to 'liking' on other platforms), Etsy uses this behavioral data to create meaningful follow-up touchpoints. For example, if a user favorites an item and the seller later puts it on sale, Etsy can send targeted notifications to bring the user back to complete the purchase, turning initial interest into actual sales.

vocabulary.definition: Intent refers to a person's purpose or aim in a given situation, particularly regarding their actions or decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, understanding user intent is crucial for tailoring marketing strategies and enhancing user experience, as it helps predict customer behavior and preferences.

insight.nuance: While 'intent' often implies a deliberate decision, it can also encompass subconscious motivations that influence consumer choices.

vocabulary.definition: Signals are indicators or cues that suggest a particular trend, behavior, or action, often used to infer intentions or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, signals can refer to user actions, such as clicks or purchases, that provide insights into customer preferences and market trends.

insight.nuance: The term 'signals' can imply varying degrees of strength; stronger signals are more indicative of user behavior, while weaker signals may require further analysis.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: But I think that it maybe misses the point in some changes or some areas where you are working towards a bigger net new thing or this specific change won't really be indicative of the greater whole you're building towards.
keySentence: Some changes miss the point of the net new thing you're building towards.
text_ko: 제가 보기에는 어떤 변화들이나 더 큰 완전히 새로운 것(net new thing)을 향해 나아가고 있는 몇몇 영역에서는 이 특정 변화만으로는 여러분이 만들어가고 있는 전체를 잘 보여주지 못해서 핵심을 놓칠 수 있어요.
text_zh: 不过我觉得这样可能有点偏了，特别是在一些变化中，或者当你在朝着一个更大的全新项目努力的时候，这种具体的小改变其实看不出你要搭建的整个大框架是什么样的。
text_es: Pero creo que tal vez se está perdiendo el punto en algunos cambios o en ciertas áreas donde estás trabajando hacia algo completamente nuevo y más grande, o donde este cambio específico realmente no va a ser representativo del conjunto más amplio que estás construyendo.
fullContext: Lenny asks Tim about Etsy's philosophy on experimentation and whether everything runs as an A/B test. Tim acknowledges that while A/B testing provides near absolute certainty about causal relationships between changes and KPIs, it has limitations. He explains that experimentation might not be the best approach when building toward larger, net-new initiatives where individual changes don't represent the full value of what you're creating, suggesting that Etsy is exploring additional validation methods beyond traditional A/B testing.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a sign or indication of something; suggestive of a particular condition or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'indicative' is often used to describe metrics or data points that reflect broader trends or outcomes, helping stakeholders understand the implications of specific actions.

insight.nuance: While 'indicative' suggests a relationship or correlation, it does not imply causation, so it should be used carefully to avoid misinterpretation.

speaker: Tim Holley
text: The thing that I do a lot, that we do as my team, that others do to some degree is a simple exercise of weekly focus. What are you focused on this week?
keySentence: What are you focused on this week?
text_ko: 제가 자주 하는 일이고 우리 팀도, 다른 사람들도 어느 정도 하는 건 매주 하는 '주간 집중(weekly focus)' 연습이에요. 이번 주엔 뭐에 집중하고 있어요?
text_zh: 我常做的一件事——我们团队也在做，别人也常做的——就是个简单的每周聚焦练习：确定本周重点(weekly focus)。你这周在聚焦什么？
text_es: Algo que hago mucho, que hacemos en mi equipo y que otros practican en cierta medida, es un ejercicio semanal muy sencillo: ¿en qué te vas a centrar esta semana?
fullContext: Lenny asks Tim about frameworks or processes he finds particularly useful that listeners might find valuable. Tim describes a simple but effective weekly focus exercise where team members identify their key priorities for the week and then reflect on whether they accomplished the previous week's focus areas. He emphasizes that while this seems basic, the act of writing down priorities and sharing them publicly creates accountability and helps people recognize patterns in their work habits and time estimation over time.

vocabulary.definition: Focus refers to the concentration of attention or effort on a specific task or objective. It is essential for achieving clarity and direction in work.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, maintaining focus is crucial for prioritizing tasks, aligning team efforts, and ensuring that resources are effectively utilized to meet strategic goals.

insight.nuance: The term 'focus' can imply a deliberate choice to concentrate on one area while potentially neglecting others, making it important to balance focus with broader perspectives.

vocabulary.definition: Exercise refers to the act of engaging in a specific activity or practice to develop a skill or reinforce a concept. It often involves structured tasks aimed at improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, exercises can take the form of team-building activities, training sessions, or strategic planning workshops designed to enhance skills, collaboration, and focus among team members.

insight.nuance: The term 'exercise' can carry a connotation of practice or training, suggesting a proactive approach to skill development, but it may also imply a lack of seriousness if not framed appropriately.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: Hot take. I would say, paid is for everyone. If you look at the way each platform is doing, Google introducing AI, plus with paid taking up the first four spots, you have to scroll pretty far down to get to an organic listing.
keySentence: paid is for everyone.
text_ko: 솔직히 말하면요, 제 생각엔 유료 광고(paid)는 이제 누구나 하는 거예요. 각 플랫폼이 어떻게 돌아가는지 보면, 구글이 AI를 도입한 데다 상위 네 자리를 유료 광고가 차지하고 있어서 오가닉(organic) 노출을 보려면 꽤 아래까지 스크롤해야 해요.
text_zh: 大胆说一句：我觉得付费（paid）适合每个人。你看看各个平台现在的做法——Google 推出了人工智能（AI），而且前四个位置都被付费广告（paid）占了，想看到自然结果（organic listing）得往下翻很久。
text_es: Una opinión polémica: yo diría que la publicidad de pago (paid) es para todos. Si miras cómo se están moviendo las plataformas —Google metiendo inteligencia artificial (AI), y con los espacios pagados (paid) ocupando las cuatro primeras posiciones— tienes que bajar bastante para encontrar un resultado orgánico (organic listing).
fullContext: Lenny asks whether performance marketing is something every company should be doing or if certain business models should focus on other growth channels like SEO, sales, or word of mouth instead. Timothy argues that the digital landscape has shifted dramatically, making paid advertising essential for virtually all businesses. He explains that organic reach has become increasingly difficult as platforms prioritize paid content, forcing companies to invest in paid channels just to maintain visibility.

vocabulary.definition: An organic listing refers to a webpage that appears in search engine results due to its relevance to the search query, rather than through paid advertising.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of digital marketing, businesses strive to improve their organic listings through search engine optimization (SEO) techniques to increase visibility without incurring advertising costs.

insight.nuance: Organic listings are often perceived as more credible by users compared to paid advertisements, making them a valuable asset for long-term brand trust.

vocabulary.definition: Introducing AI refers to the process of integrating artificial intelligence technologies into business operations or products to enhance efficiency and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, companies are increasingly introducing AI to automate processes, analyze data, and improve customer experiences, often leading to competitive advantages.

insight.nuance: The phrase conveys a sense of innovation and forward-thinking, but may also imply challenges related to implementation and ethical considerations.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: Instead of thinking about being on top of the page, and that's like ego marketing, I want to be number one. I want to be there all the time. It's about showing to the right person as often as possible.
keySentence: It's about showing to the right person as often as possible.
text_ko: 페이지 맨 위에만 올라가는 걸 목표로 하는, 이른바 에고 마케팅(ego marketing) 식 사고 대신에 저는 1위를 하고 싶어요. 항상 그 자리에 있고 싶고요. 중요한 건 적절한 사람에게 가능한 한 자주 보이는 거예요.
text_zh: 别老想着要排在搜索结果第一位，那就像是自我炫耀式的营销，什么"我要当老大，我要一直霸占榜首"。关键是要尽可能多地出现在对的人面前。
text_es: En lugar de obsesionarse con estar en la primera posición, que es como marketing de ego, "quiero ser el número uno, quiero estar ahí siempre", se trata de aparecer ante la persona correcta con la mayor frecuencia posible.
fullContext: Lenny asks Timothy about common mistakes he finds when taking over performance marketing accounts from agencies. Timothy explains that many marketers focus on vanity metrics like ranking position rather than targeting effectiveness. He describes 'ego marketing' as the misguided desire to always appear first in search results, when the real goal should be reaching qualified prospects who are likely to convert.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: Each platform is different. The user behavior is different. Make sure you're not too hard on yourself if it doesn't work. It's okay to fail because we're either winning or we're learning.
keySentence: Don't be too hard on yourself; failing means we're winning or we're learning.
text_ko: 플랫폼(platform)마다 다르고 사용자 행동(user behavior)도 달라요. 잘 안 되면 자신을 너무 몰아붙이지 마세요. 실패해도 괜찮아요, 우리는 이기고 있거나 배우고 있는 거예요.
text_zh: 每个平台都不一样，用户行为也不同。如果效果不好，别对自己太苛刻。失败没关系的，反正我们要么赢，要么学到东西。
text_es: Cada plataforma es distinta. El comportamiento de los usuarios es diferente. Asegúrate de no ser muy duro contigo mismo si no funciona. Está bien fallar porque o estamos ganando o estamos aprendiendo.
fullContext: Lenny asks for tips on experimenting with new advertising platforms to test for signs of life. Timothy advises that marketers should expect some experiments to fail when testing new platforms, as each has unique user behaviors and requirements. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a learning mindset rather than expecting immediate success, explaining that failed experiments still provide valuable insights for future optimization.

vocabulary.definition: The patterns and actions of individuals when interacting with products, services, or platforms, often analyzed to improve user experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding user behavior is essential for businesses to tailor their marketing strategies, enhance product design, and increase customer satisfaction.

insight.nuance: The term suggests a focus on empirical data and analytics, emphasizing the importance of observing actual user interactions rather than relying solely on assumptions.

vocabulary.definition: To be unsuccessful in achieving a desired goal or outcome, often leading to a reassessment of strategies or approaches.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup world, failure is often viewed as a stepping stone to success, providing valuable lessons that can inform future endeavors and innovations.

insight.nuance: While 'fail' carries a negative connotation, in entrepreneurial contexts it is frequently reframed as an opportunity for growth and learning.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: I always say, where are your users? You will have some data that will allow you to understand that say right now, you're doing really well on TikTok. Some would argue that's an emerging channel right now. Great.
keySentence: Identify where your users are; TikTok is an emerging channel for engagement.
text_ko: 저는 항상 '사용자들이 어디에 있나요?'라고 말해요. 어떤 데이터(data)를 보면 지금 틱톡에서 꽤 잘하고 있다는 걸 알 수 있어요. 어떤 사람들은 지금 틱톡이 신흥 채널(emerging channel)이라고 보기도 해요. 좋아요.
text_zh: 我常说，你的用户在哪儿？数据会告诉你这一点，比如现在你在抖音（TikTok）上做得很不错。有人会说那是个新兴渠道(channel)，很好。
text_es: Siempre digo: ¿dónde están tus usuarios? Vas a tener datos (data) que te permitan ver que, por ejemplo, ahora mismo te está yendo muy bien en TikTok. Algunos dirían que ahora es un canal emergente (emerging channel). Genial.
fullContext: Lenny asks about signs that indicate a company has potential for paid marketing to become most of their growth, rather than just a small percentage. Timothy explains his data-driven approach to identifying promising channels by analyzing existing user behavior patterns. He suggests looking at current traffic sources and user engagement to determine which platforms warrant increased investment, then testing similar platforms that might work with repurposed content.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to something that is in the process of coming into existence or becoming prominent.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'emerging' often describes new markets, trends, or technologies that are gaining traction and may present future opportunities.

insight.nuance: The term carries a sense of novelty and potential, suggesting that while something is not yet fully established, it is on the verge of significant growth.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'understand' often refers to comprehending market dynamics, consumer behavior, or data insights that inform strategic decisions.

insight.nuance: The term implies a deeper level of comprehension beyond surface-level knowledge, often requiring analysis and critical thinking.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: The number one thing I tell people all the time is use your own data, start with your own data. So take the existing customer base you have, load that up into the platform to build lookalikes. From there, you can do...
keySentence: Use your own data to build lookalikes; load that up into the platform.
text_ko: 제가 사람들에게 늘 제일 먼저 하는 말은 자사 데이터부터 활용하라는 거예요. 보유한 고객 데이터를 플랫폼에 올려 유사 고객(lookalikes)을 만드세요. 거기서부터 여러 가지를 해볼 수 있어요...
text_zh: 我常跟人强调的第一点就是：先用自己的数据。把你现有的客户数据导入平台(platform)，用来做相似受众(lookalikes)。接下来你就可以……
text_es: Lo primero que siempre les digo es: usen sus propios datos; empiecen por los suyos. Tomen la base de clientes que ya tienen y súbanla a la plataforma para crear audiencias similares (lookalikes). A partir de ahí pueden...
fullContext: Lenny asks for advice on running effective 'signs of life' tests when experimenting with new advertising platforms. Timothy recommends starting with lookalike audiences based on existing customer data rather than broad targeting. Lookalike audiences use platform algorithms to find users who behave similarly to a company's current customers, with percentages indicating how closely matched the targeting is - 1% being the most similar and 10% being broader.

vocabulary.definition: A framework or environment that enables the development and deployment of applications, services, or technologies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, a platform can refer to software or hardware that provides the necessary tools for developers and businesses to build and operate their products.

insight.nuance: The term 'platform' often suggests scalability and integration capabilities, making it essential to use in contexts where these features are highlighted.

vocabulary.definition: Currently in place or available; not new or created recently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'existing' often refers to current customers, products, or systems that are already operational and can be utilized for further development or analysis.

insight.nuance: While 'existing' is neutral, it can imply a limitation in innovation or growth if overemphasized, so it should be used in contexts that appreciate both current and potential future states.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: The biggest thing I want to focus on is what is your thought process when it comes to data? Because I can teach anyone how to do Google ads. I can teach anyone how to do Meta ads. That is not the hard part.
keySentence: The biggest thing I want to focus on is what is your thought process when it comes to data?
text_ko: 제가 가장 집중하고 싶은 건 데이터(data)를 다룰 때 어떤 생각을 하는지예요. 구글 광고(Google Ads) 하는 법은 누구에게나 가르쳐줄 수 있고, 메타 광고(Meta Ads)도 마찬가지예요. 그건 어려운 부분이 아니에요.
text_zh: 我最想关注的是：你看待数据的思路是什么？因为谷歌广告(Google ads)、Meta广告(Meta ads)我都能教会任何人，这并不是难点。
text_es: Lo más importante en lo que quiero centrarme es: ¿cómo piensas a la hora de trabajar con los datos? Porque puedo enseñar a cualquiera a hacer anuncios en Google (Google Ads). Puedo enseñar a cualquiera a hacer anuncios en Meta (Meta Ads). Esa no es la parte difícil.
fullContext: Lenny asks what type of person Timothy looks for when hiring the first performance marketing specialist. Timothy explains his philosophy around hiring data-driven people over those with specific platform experience. He references the book 'The Signal and the Noise' to illustrate how advertising platforms provide overwhelming amounts of metrics, making it crucial to hire someone who can distinguish meaningful insights from irrelevant data points.

vocabulary.definition: The mental procedure or sequence of ideas that an individual follows to arrive at a conclusion or decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, understanding someone's thought process can reveal their decision-making style and problem-solving approach, which is crucial for collaboration and innovation.

insight.nuance: This term often implies a deeper analysis of reasoning rather than just the outcome, making it suitable for discussions about strategy or critical thinking.

speaker: Timothy Davis
text: I'm a big believer in hiring smart people and then getting out of their way. But each week having one-on-ones with them, just spot checking things, just saying, 'Hey, I looked at this. This doesn't look right.
keySentence: Hire smart people and get out of their way while spot checking things.
text_ko: 저는 유능한 사람을 뽑아 놓고는 그들이 알아서 일하게 놔두는 걸 정말 믿어요. 다만 매주 일대일 미팅(one-on-one)을 하면서 가볍게 스폿체크(spot checking)를 하고, "이거 제가 봤는데 좀 이상해 보여요"라고 말하곤 해요.
text_zh: 我很赞同招聪明人，然后放手让他们去做。不过我每周还是会和他们做一对一(one-on-ones)，顺便抽查一下，随口说一句：“我看了这个，好像不太对。”
text_es: Creo firmemente en contratar a personas inteligentes y luego darles espacio para trabajar. Pero cada semana tengo reuniones uno a uno (one-on-ones) con cada persona, hago revisiones puntuales (spot checking) y les digo: "Oye, miré esto y no me cuadra."
fullContext: Lenny asks Timothy to explain why he consistently outperforms agencies when taking over performance marketing accounts. Timothy describes his management philosophy of empowering team members while maintaining oversight through regular check-ins. He contrasts this with agencies that often spread their attention too thin across multiple clients, preventing them from diving deep into account optimization and maintaining consistent quality control.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of randomly reviewing or inspecting a small portion of work or data to ensure quality and compliance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, spot checking is often used to maintain standards in processes, products, or employee performance without requiring exhaustive reviews.

insight.nuance: Spot checking suggests a balance between oversight and trust; however, excessive reliance on it may overlook systemic issues.

speaker: Tobi Lütke
text: My energy source is dissatisfaction with status quo. My fundamental belief is all this talk about technology where all... So many books are about just technology leading to dystopia. You know what dystopia is?
keySentence: My energy source is dissatisfaction with status quo.
text_ko: 제 에너지원은 현상 유지에 대한 불만이에요. 제 근본적인 신념은, 기술 얘기가 넘쳐나는 요즘에 많은 책들이 기술이 곧 디스토피아(dystopia)로 이어진다고만 말한다는 거예요. 디스토피아가 뭔지 아세요?
text_zh: 我的动力来自于对现状（status quo）的不满。我的基本看法是，大家对技术的讨论太多、太片面了——很多书都把技术说成会把我们带向反乌托邦（dystopia）。你知道反乌托邦是什么意思吗？
text_es: Lo que me da energía es la insatisfacción con la situación actual (status quo). Mi creencia fundamental es que todo ese discurso sobre la tecnología, como si lo fuera a dominar todo, está exagerado: hay tantos libros que presentan la tecnología simplemente como el camino hacia una distopía (dystopia). ¿Sabes lo que es una distopía?
fullContext: Lenny asks Tobi about where he gets his energy as a builder and what drives him. Tobi explains that his energy source is dissatisfaction with the current state of things. He believes that despite all the talk about technology creating dystopia, today is actually primitive compared to what the future holds. This perspective drives him to build products that contribute to human progress rather than accepting the status quo.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of discontent or unhappiness with a situation or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, dissatisfaction can drive innovation and improvement, as companies seek to address customer complaints or inefficiencies in their operations.

insight.nuance: While dissatisfaction can indicate problems, it can also serve as a catalyst for positive change when channeled effectively.

vocabulary.definition: The existing state or condition of affairs, especially regarding social or political issues.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, challenging the status quo is often essential for disruption and innovation, as it encourages new ideas and approaches.

insight.nuance: The term can carry a negative connotation when used to imply stagnation or resistance to change.

vocabulary.definition: Serving as a basic, foundational principle or element that is essential to a system or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, understanding fundamental principles is crucial for making informed decisions and developing effective plans.

insight.nuance: The term often implies something that is not only basic but also vital for the integrity of a larger system or idea.

vocabulary.definition: An imagined society characterized by oppressive societal control, often presenting a bleak or nightmarish reality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology discussions, dystopia is frequently referenced in debates about the potential negative consequences of technological advancements, such as surveillance or loss of privacy.

insight.nuance: While often used in a literary or philosophical context, the term can evoke strong emotional responses and should be used thoughtfully to avoid alarmism.

speaker: Tobi Lütke
text: There's an aesthetic in the world that exists which is that business people dress in suit and tie, they are speaking much more sophisticated than I do, usually without an accent.
keySentence: There's an aesthetic in the world that exists which is that business people dress in suit and tie.
text_ko: 세상엔 그런 미학이 있어요. 비즈니스 사람들은 정장에 넥타이를 하고 다니고, 말투도 보통 저보다 훨씬 세련돼 보이고, 대개는 사투리 없이 표준어로 말해요.
text_zh: 社会上有一种既定印象：商界人士都穿西装打领带，说话听起来比我专业得多，而且通常没有口音。
text_es: Hay una estética en el mundo: la gente de negocios viste traje y corbata, habla de forma mucho más sofisticada que yo y, por lo general, sin acento.
fullContext: Lenny mentions quotes about how Tobi thinks differently from conventional business approaches.
